items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and use words and phrases heard in read-alouds.
items.zh: 理解并使用朗读中听到的词语和短语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Compare and contrast similarities and differences within a single read-aloud or between two or more read-alouds.
items.zh: 比较和对照单次朗读内部或两次及以上朗读之间的异同。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Make personal connections to events or experiences in a read-aloud and/or make connections among several read-alouds.
items.zh: 把朗读中的事件或经历与个人建立联系，和/或在多次朗读之间建立联系。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Prior to listening to a read-aloud, identify what they know and have learned that may be related to the specific story or topic to be read aloud.
items.zh: 在听朗读之前，确认自己所知道的、可能与被朗读的具体故事或主题相关的内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use pictures accompanying the read-aloud to check and support understanding of the read-aloud.
items.zh: 利用朗读所配的图片来检查和帮助理解朗读内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Make predictions prior to and during a read-aloud, based on the title, pictures, and/or text heard thus far and then compare the actual outcomes to predictions.
items.zh: 在朗读前和朗读过程中，根据标题、图片和/或目前已听到的文本作出预测，然后把实际结果与预测进行比较。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Answer questions that require making interpretations, judgments, or giving opinions about what is heard in a read-aloud, including answering “why” questions that require recognizing cause/effect relationships.
items.zh: 回答需要作出解释、判断或对朗读中所听内容发表看法的问题，包括回答需要识别因果关系的“为什么”问题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify who is telling a story or providing information in a text.
items.zh: 识别文本中谁在讲故事或提供信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Retell or dramatize a story, using narrative language to describe characters, setting(s), and a beginning, a middle and an end to events of the story in proper sequence.
items.zh: 复述或表演一个故事，用叙事性语言描述人物、背景，并按恰当顺序描述故事事件的开头、中间和结尾。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Change some story events and provide a different story ending.
items.zh: 改动某些故事事件，并给出一个不同的故事结局。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Create and tell an original story, using narrative language to describe characters, setting(s), and a beginning, a middle and an end to events of the story in proper sequence
items.zh: 创作并讲述一个原创故事，用叙事性语言描述人物、背景，并按恰当顺序描述故事事件的开头、中间和结尾

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Distinguish fantasy from realistic text in a story.
items.zh: 区分故事中的幻想情节与现实情节。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of literary language (e.g., author, illustrator, characters, setting, plot, dialogue, personification, simile, and metaphor) and use some of these terms in retelling stories or creating their own stories. E. Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Nonfiction and Informational Text Teachers: Select nonfiction read-aloud topics from the kindergarten history, science, music, and visual arts topics, with emphasis on history and science.
items.zh: 展示对文学语言的理解（如作者、插画者、人物、背景、情节、对话、拟人、明喻和隐喻），并能在复述故事或创编自己的故事时使用其中一些术语。E. 朗读的理解与讨论——非虚构与信息类文本 教师：非虚构类朗读主题应从幼儿园的历史、科学、音乐、视觉艺术主题中选取，重点放在历史与科学上。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Retell important facts and information from a nonfiction read-aloud.
items.zh: 复述非虚构类朗读材料中的重要事实和信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: With assistance, categorize and organize facts and information within a given topic.
items.zh: 在帮助下，将给定主题范围内的事实和信息分类整理。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: With assistance, create and interpret timelines and lifelines related to read-alouds.
items.zh: 在帮助下，制作并解读与朗读内容相关的时间线和生平线。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Distinguish read-alouds that describe events that happened long ago from those that describe contemporary or current events
items.zh: 区分描述久远以前发生事件的朗读材料与描述当代或当前事件的朗读材料。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that what is said can be written and that the writing system is a way of writing down sounds.
items.zh: 理解说出的话可以被写下来，文字系统就是把声音记录下来的一种方式。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of directionality (left to right, return sweep, top to bottom, front to back).
items.zh: 理解书写方向（从左到右、换行回扫、从上到下、从前到后）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify the parts of books and function of each part (front cover, back cover, title page, table of contents).
items.zh: 认识书的各部分及其功能（封面、封底、扉页、目录）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate correct book orientation by holding book correctly and turning pages.
items.zh: 能正确拿书并正确翻页，表现出正确的书本方向感。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Recognize that sentences in print are made up of separate words.
items.zh: 认识到印刷出来的句子是由一个个独立的词组成的。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand that words are separated by spaces.
items.zh: 理解词与词之间用空格分隔。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Distinguish letters, words, sentences, and stories.
items.zh: 区分字母、单词、句子和故事。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of basic print conventions by tracking and following print word for word when listening to text read aloud.
items.zh: 听朗读时能逐词跟随并指读印刷文字，表现出对基本印刷惯例的理解。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that the sequence of letters in a written word represents the sequence of sounds in the spoken word.
items.zh: 理解书写单词中字母的顺序代表口语单词中声音的顺序。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Recognize and name the twenty-six letters of the alphabet in both their upper-case and lower-case forms.
items.zh: 能识别并说出26个字母的大写和小写形式。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Say the letters of the alphabet in order, either in song or recitation
items.zh: 能用唱歌或背诵的方式按顺序说出字母表。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify environmental sounds, e.g., keys jingling, scissors cutting, clapping.
items.zh: 辨认环境中的声音，如钥匙叮当声、剪刀剪纸声、拍手声。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify whether pairs of environmental sounds are the same or different.
items.zh: 判断成对的环境声音是相同还是不同。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Count the number of environmental sounds heard, e.g., clapping, rhythm band instruments.
items.zh: 数出听到的环境声音的数量，如拍手声、节奏乐队乐器的声音。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Orally segment sentences into discrete words.
items.zh: 口头将句子切分成一个个独立的词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that words are made up of sequences of sounds.
items.zh: 理解单词是由一串声音组成的。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that vowel sounds are produced with the mouth open and airflow unobstructed, whereas consonant sounds involve closing parts of the mouth and blocking the air flow.
items.zh: 理解元音是张口、气流不受阻碍发出的音，而辅音则需要闭合口腔的某些部位、阻断气流而发出。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Given a pair of spoken words, select the one that is longer (i.e., contains more phonemes).
items.zh: 给出一对口头说出的单词，选出较长的那个（即包含更多音素的那个）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: In riddle games, supply words that begin with a target phoneme.
items.zh: 在猜谜游戏中，说出以目标音素开头的单词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Indicate whether a target phoneme is or is not present in the initial/medial/final position of a spoken word, e.g., hear /m/ at the beginning of mat and /g/ at the end of bag.
items.zh: 判断某个目标音素是否出现在口语单词的词首／词中／词尾，例如在 mat 的开头听到 /m/，在 bag 的结尾听到 /g/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Listen to one-syllable words and tell the beginning or ending sounds, e.g., given dog, identify initial /d/ or final /g/.
items.zh: 听单音节词并说出其开头或结尾的音，例如给出 dog，能指出开头的 /d/ 或结尾的 /g/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Recognize the same phoneme in different spoken words, e.g., /b/ in ball, bug, and big.
items.zh: 在不同的口语单词中识别相同的音素，如 ball、bug、big 中的 /b/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify whether pairs of phonemes are the same or different, including pairs that differ only in voicing, e.g., /b/ and /p/.
items.zh: 判断成对的音素是相同还是不同，包括仅在清浊上不同的音素对，如 /b/ 和 /p/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Orally blend two to three sounds to form a word, e.g., given the sounds /k/.../a/... /t/, blend to make cat.
items.zh: 口头把两到三个音拼合成一个单词，例如给出 /k/…/a/…/t/，拼成 cat。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Segment a spoken word into phonemes, e.g., given bat, produce the segments/b//a//t/.
items.zh: 把一个口语单词切分成音素，例如给出 bat，切分为 /b//a//t/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Given a spoken word, produce another word that rhymes, e.g., given hit, supply bit or mitt.
items.zh: 给出一个口语单词，说出另一个与之押韵的词，例如给出 hit，说出 bit 或 mitt。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify the number of syllables in a spoken word
items.zh: 数出口语单词中的音节数量。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Learning to read requires understanding and mastering the written English code through explicit and systematic phonics instruction. Research suggests that phonics instruction is most effective when specific letter-sound relationships are taught and reinforced by having students both read and write the letter-sound correspondence being studied. Reading and writing—decoding and encoding—are complementary processes that ensure mastery of the written code.
items.zh: 学会阅读需要通过明确、系统的自然拼读教学来理解和掌握英语书面代码。研究表明，当教师教授具体的字母—音对应关系，并让学生对所学的字母—音对应进行读和写的练习来加以巩固时，自然拼读教学最为有效。阅读与写作——解码与编码——是相辅相成的过程，能确保学生掌握书面代码。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that a systematic, predictable relationship exists between written letters (graphemes) and spoken sounds (phonemes).
items.zh: 理解书面字母（字素）与口语声音（音素）之间存在系统且可预测的关系。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Blend individual phonemes to pronounce printed words.
items.zh: 把单个音素拼合起来，读出印刷的单词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand that sometimes two or more printed letters stand for a single sound.
items.zh: 理解有时两个或更多印刷字母代表一个音。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read and write any CVC word, e.g., sit or cat.
items.zh: 能读、写任意 CVC 单词（辅音—元音—辅音），如 sit 或 cat。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read and write one-syllable words containing common initial consonant clusters such as tr-, fl-, dr- and sp- and consonant digraphs such as ch-, sh-, th-, etc.
items.zh: 能读、写含有常见词首辅音连缀（如 tr-、fl-、dr-、sp-）和辅音字母组合（如 ch-、sh-、th- 等）的单音节词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read and write words containing separated vowel graphemes, such as, late, bite, note, cute.
items.zh: 能读、写含有分离元音字母组合（元音加不发音的 e）的单词，如 late、bite、note、cute。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read tricky spellings that can be sounded two ways, e.g., the letter ‘s’ sounded /s/ as in cats and /z/ as in dogs.
items.zh: 能读有两种读音的棘手拼写，例如字母 s 在 cats 中读 /s/，在 dogs 中读 /z/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read and write chains of one-syllable words in which one sound is added, substituted, or omitted, e.g., read at > cat > bat > bad > bid.
items.zh: 能读、写单音节词链，其中一个音被添加、替换或去掉，例如 at > cat > bat > bad > bid。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read at least 15 words generally identified as very high frequency words.. Consonant Sounds and Spellings Taught in Kindergarten /b/ spelled ‘b’ as in boy, ‘bb’, as in tubby /d/ spelled ‘d’ as in dog, ‘dd’ as in madder /f/ spelled ‘f’ as in fun, ‘ff’ as in stuff /g/ spelled ‘g’ as in get, ‘gg’ as in egg /h/ spelled ‘h’ as in him /j/ spelled ‘j’ as in jump Vowel Sounds and Spellings Taught in Kindergarten /a/ spelled ‘a’ as in cat /e/ spelled ‘e’ as in get /i/ spelled ‘i’ as in hit /o/ spelled ‘o’ as in hot /u/ spelled ‘u’ as in but /ae/ spelled ‘a\_e’ as in cake /ee/ spelled ‘ee’ as in bee /ie/ spelled ‘i\_e’ as in bike /oe/ spelled ‘o\_e’ as in note /ue/ spelled ‘u\_e’ as in cute /er/ spelled ‘er’ as in her /ar/ spelled ‘ar’ as is car /or/ spelled ‘or’ as in for
items.zh: 能读至少15个通常被认为是高频词的单词。幼儿园教授的辅音及其拼写：/b/ 拼作 b（如 boy）、bb（如 tubby）；/d/ 拼作 d（如 dog）、dd（如 madder）；/f/ 拼作 f（如 fun）、ff（如 stuff）；/g/ 拼作 g（如 get）、gg（如 egg）；/h/ 拼作 h（如 him）；/j/ 拼作 j（如 jump）。幼儿园教授的元音及其拼写：/a/ 拼作 a（如 cat）；/e/ 拼作 e（如 get）；/i/ 拼作 i（如 hit）；/o/ 拼作 o（如 hot）；/u/ 拼作 u（如 but）；/ae/ 拼作 a_e（如 cake）；/ee/ 拼作 ee（如 bee）；/ie/ 拼作 i_e（如 bike）；/oe/ 拼作 o_e（如 note）；/ue/ 拼作 u_e（如 cute）；/er/ 拼作 er（如 her）；/ar/ 拼作 ar（如 car）；/or/ 拼作 or（如 for）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read decodable stories that incorporate the specific code knowledge that has been taught.
items.zh: 阅读包含已教授的特定拼写解码知识的可解码故事。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use phonics skills in conjunction with context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
items.zh: 结合自然拼读技巧与上下文来确认或自我纠正字词识别和理解，必要时重读。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of and use commas and end punctuation while reading orally.
items.zh: 朗读时能理解并使用逗号和句末标点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read aloud, alone, or with a partner at least 15 minutes each day. E. Reading Comprehension—All Texts Teachers: It is important to recognize that kindergartners are taught only some of the many letter-sound correspondences a reader needs to know to read a wide range of printed material. As a result, many kindergartners will be able to read only the simplest written text independently. At this grade level, mental energy will be directed primarily to the act of reading, i.e., decoding. A focus on the mechanics of decoding is appropriate and desirable at this early stage in the reading process. In kindergarten, attention to reading comprehension should be directed to ensuring a fundamental understanding of what has been read. At this grade level, it will generally be more effective and efficient to devote time to higher level thinking and comprehension skills at the listening and speaking level in response to written texts that are read aloud.
items.zh: 每天独自或与同伴一起朗读至少15分钟。E. 阅读理解——所有文本 教师：要认识到，幼儿园孩子只学习了阅读大量印刷材料所需的众多字母—音对应关系中的一部分。因此，许多幼儿园孩子只能独立阅读最简单的书面文本。在这个年级阶段，脑力主要用于阅读行为本身，即解码。在阅读过程的这一早期阶段，重点关注解码技巧是恰当且可取的。在幼儿园，对阅读理解的关注应放在确保对所读内容有基本理解上。在这一年级阶段，通常把时间用于听和说层面的高阶思维与理解技能（针对朗读出来的书面文本）会更有效、更高效。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of simple decodable text after reading independently.
items.zh: 独立阅读后能理解简单的可解码文本。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Answer questions requiring literal recall and understanding of the details and/or facts (i.e., who, what, where, when, etc.) about a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 回答需要直接回忆并理解所读文本细节和／或事实的问题（如谁、什么、哪里、何时等）。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Retell or dramatize a story, using narrative language to describe characters, setting(s), and a beginning, a middle and an end to events of the story in proper sequence.
items.zh: 用叙述性语言复述或表演故事，描述人物、场景，并按正确顺序讲出故事的开头、中间和结局。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use narrative language to describe people, places, things, locations, events, actions, a scene or facts from a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 用叙述性语言描述独立阅读的文本中的人物、地点、事物、场所、事件、动作、场景或事实。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and use words and phrases from a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 理解并使用独立阅读的文本中的单词和短语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Prior to reading, identify what they know and have learned that may be related to the specific story or topic to be read.
items.zh: 阅读前，说出自己已知和已学的、可能与将要读的故事或主题相关的内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use pictures accompanying the written text to check and support understanding.
items.zh: 利用随文配图来检验和帮助理解。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Make predictions prior to and while reading, based on the title, pictures, and/or text read thus far and then compare the actual outcomes to predictions.
items.zh: 阅读前和阅读中根据标题、图片和／或已读到的文本做出预测，然后把实际结果与预测进行比较。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify who is telling a story or providing information in a text.
items.zh: 识别文本中是谁在讲故事或提供信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: It is important to recognize that of all the communication skills—listening, speaking, reading, and writing—writing is the most demanding and challenging, especially for kindergartners who are just learning not only the code, but the fine motor skills and letter strokes necessary to put something down on paper. Kindergartners can, however, express themselves in writing by drawing pictures and, as they begin to learn some of the code, copying or writing words, phrases, and sentences. In addition, students can also participate in shared writing exercises modeled and scaffolded by an adult. The focus in shared writing should be on encouraging the students to verbally express themselves coherently and in complete sentences, as the teacher serves as a scribe.
items.zh: 要认识到，在听、说、读、写四项交流技能中，写是最难、最具挑战性的，对幼儿园孩子尤其如此——他们不仅刚在学习文字代码，还要学习把内容写到纸上所需的精细动作技能和字母笔画。不过，幼儿园孩子可以通过画画来进行书面表达；当他们开始掌握部分代码时，可以抄写或书写单词、短语和句子。此外，学生还可以参加由成人示范和搭建支架的共同写作活动。共同写作的重点应是鼓励学生用连贯、完整的句子口头表达自己，由教师充当记录者（执笔人）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Draw pictures to represent a text that has been heard or read independently.
items.zh: 画画来表现听过或独立读过的文本。
items.section: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose and Task
items.section_zh: 写作要体现读者对象、目的和任务

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Draw pictures to represent a preference or opinion.
items.zh: 画画表达自己的喜好或观点。
items.section: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose and Task
items.section_zh: 写作要体现读者对象、目的和任务

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write narratives, informative and explanatory texts, and offer an opinion through shared writing exercises.
items.zh: 通过共同写作活动写记叙文、说明性和解释性文本，并表达观点。
items.section: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose and Task
items.section_zh: 写作要体现读者对象、目的和任务

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: With assistance, add details to writing.
items.zh: 在帮助下，为自己的写作添加细节。
items.section: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose and Task
items.section_zh: 写作要体现读者对象、目的和任务

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Create a title or caption to accompany a picture and/or shared writing.
items.zh: 为图画和／或共同写出的内容拟一个标题或说明文字。
items.section: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose and Task
items.section_zh: 写作要体现读者对象、目的和任务

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Form letters, words, phrases and sentences to communicate thoughts and ideas.
items.zh: 书写字母、单词、短语和句子来表达思想和想法。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Apply basic spelling conventions.
items.zh: 运用基本的拼写规则。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use basic capitalization and punctuation in sentences to convey meaning.
items.zh: 在句子中使用基本的大小写和标点来传达意思。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Hold a pencil with a pincer grasp and make marks on paper.
items.zh: 用三指捏握（钳形握笔）拿铅笔，并在纸上留下痕迹。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Trace, copy, and print from memory the 26 letters of the alphabet accurately in both their upper-case and lower-case forms.
items.zh: 能准确描摹、抄写并凭记忆写出26个字母的大写和小写形式。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write own name.
items.zh: 写自己的名字。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write from left to right, leaving spaces between words, and top to bottom using return sweep.
items.zh: 书写时从左到右、词与词之间留空格，并从上到下、换行回扫。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Begin to write phonemically plausible spellings for words that cannot be spelled correctly with current code knowledge, e.g., write bote for boat, sum for some, hunee for honey.
items.zh: 对于用现有拼写知识还无法正确拼写的单词，开始写出符合读音的近似拼写，如把 boat 写成 bote、some 写成 sum、honey 写成 hunee。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write words, phrases, and sentences from dictation, applying phonics knowledge.
items.zh: 运用自然拼读知识，根据听写写出单词、短语和句子。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Use and understand question words, i.e., what, where, when, who, how.
items.zh: 使用并理解疑问词，即 what（什么）、where（哪里）、when（何时）、who（谁）、how（怎样）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Form regular plural nouns by adding ‘s’ or ‘es’, i.e., dog, dogs, wish, wishes.
items.zh: 通过加 s 或 es 构成规则复数名词，如 dog—dogs、wish—wishes。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring prepositions, i.e., to/from, in/out, on/off.
items.zh: 理解常见介词，如 to/from（到／从）、in/out（里／外）、on/off（上／关）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Produce and expand complete sentences orally and in shared writing exercises.
items.zh: 在口头表达和共同写作中说出并扩展完整的句子。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Capitalize the first word in a sentence; the pronoun I.
items.zh: 句首字母大写；代词 I 始终大写。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify and use end punctuation, including periods, question marks, and exclamation points.
items.zh: 识别并使用句末标点，包括句号、问号和感叹号。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Students should be introduced to a varied selection of poetry with strong rhyme and rhythm. Students should hear these rhymes read aloud, and should say some of them aloud. Some rhymes may also be sung to familiar melodies. The poems listed here represent some of the most popular and widely anthologized titles; students may certainly be introduced to more Mother Goose rhymes beyond the selection below. Although students are not expected to memorize the following rhymes, they will delight in knowing their favorites by heart, and will experience a sense of achievement and satisfaction in being able to recite some of the rhymes.
items.zh: 应让学生接触多种节奏和押韵感强的诗歌。要让学生听这些童谣的朗读，并让他们朗读其中一些；有些童谣还可以配上熟悉的旋律来唱。这里列出的诗歌是一些最受欢迎、被广为收录的作品；当然，除以下选篇外，还可以向学生介绍更多鹅妈妈童谣。虽然并不要求学生背诵这些童谣，但他们乐于熟记自己最喜欢的那几首，并能背诵一些童谣时会获得成就感和满足感。

items.en: While the following works make up a strong core of literature, the content of language arts includes not only stories, fables, and poems, but also the well-practiced, operational knowledge of how written symbols represent sounds, and how those sounds and symbols convey meaning. Thus, the stories specified below are meant to complement, not to replace, materials designed to help students practice decoding and encoding skills (see above, II. Reading and III. Writing).

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: illustrator E. Sayings and Phrases Teachers: Every culture has phrases and proverbs that make no sense when carried over literally into another culture. For many students, this section may not be needed; they will have picked up these sayings by hearing them at home and among friends. But the sayings have been one of the categories most appreciated by teachers who work with students from home cultures that differ from the standard culture of literate American English. A dog is man’s best friend. April showers bring May flowers. Better safe than sorry Do unto others as you would have them do unto you. The early bird gets the worm. Great oaks from little acorns grow. Look before you leap A place for everything and everything in its place Practice makes perfect. \[It’s\] raining cats and dogs. Where there’s a will there’s a way. Note: Children will read more American folk heroes and tall tales in Grade 2.
items.zh: 插画者 E. 谚语与短语 教师：每种文化都有一些短语和谚语，直译到另一种文化中就没有意义了。对许多学生来说，这一节可能并非必要，因为他们在家里和朋友那里听多了自然就学会了。但对于面对家庭文化与美国标准书面英语文化不同的学生的教师来说，这类谚语一直是最受认可的类别之一。狗是人类最好的朋友。四月雨带来五月花。谨慎总没错。己所不欲，勿施于人。早起的鸟儿有虫吃。伟大的橡树由小橡子长成。三思而后行。万物各得其所。熟能生巧。倾盆大雨（直译：下猫下狗）。有志者事竟成。注：学生将在二年级阅读更多美国民间英雄和夸张故事。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Teachers: In kindergarten, students often study aspects of the world around them: the family, the school, the community, etc. The following guidelines are meant to broaden and complement that focus. The goal of studying selected topics in World History in Kindergarten is to foster curiosity and the beginnings of understanding about the larger world outside the student’s locality, and about varied civilizations and ways of life. This can be done through a variety of means: story, drama, art, music, discussion, and more.
items.zh: 教师：在幼儿园，学生常常学习周围世界的各个方面：家庭、学校、社区等。以下指南旨在拓宽和补充这一重点。幼儿园学习世界历史中选定主题的目标，是培养孩子的好奇心，并初步理解其所在地区之外的广阔世界，以及各种文明和生活方式。这可以通过多种方式实现：故事、戏剧、艺术、音乐、讨论等等。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Teachers: Foster students’ geographical awareness through regular work with maps and globes. Have students regularly locate themselves on maps and globes in relation to places they are studying. Students should make and use a simple map of a locality (such as classroom, home, school grounds) or a map for a treasure hunt.
items.zh: 教师：通过经常使用地图和地球仪培养学生的地理意识。让学生定期在地图和地球仪上确定自己相对于所学地点的位置。学生应制作并使用本地（如教室、家庭、校园）简单地图，或寻宝地图。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: An Overview of the Seven Continents
items.en: Help students gain a beginning geographic vocabulary and a basic sense of how we organize and talk about the world by giving names to some of the biggest pieces of land. Introduce students to the seven continents through a variety of methods and media (tracing, coloring, relief maps, etc.), and associate the continents with familiar wildlife, landmarks, peoples, cultures, etc., for example, penguins in Antarctica; or the Eiffel Tower in Europe. Throughout the school year, reinforce names and locations of continents when potential connections arise in other disciplines, for example, connect Grimm’s fairy tales to Europe, the voyage of Pilgrims to Europe and North America the story of “Momotaro—Peach Boy” to Asia \[Japan\], or the study of Native Americans to North America.
items.zh: 帮助学生初步掌握地理词汇，并通过给最大的陆地命名来基本理解我们如何组织和谈论世界。通过多种方法和媒介（描摹、涂色、立体地图等）向学生介绍七大洲，并把各大洲与熟悉的野生动物、地标、民族和文化联系起来，例如南极洲的企鹅、欧洲的埃菲尔铁塔。在整个学年中，当其他学科出现可能的联系时，强化各大洲的名称和位置，例如把格林童话与欧洲联系起来，把清教徒的航行与欧洲和北美洲联系起来，把“桃太郎”的故事与亚洲（日本）联系起来，或把美洲原住民的研究与北美洲联系起来。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Teachers: The study of American history begins in Grades K-2 with a brief overview of major events and figures, from the earliest days to recent times. A more in-depth, chronological study of American history begins again in grade 3 and continues onward. The term “American” here generally, but not always, refers to the lands that became the United States. Other topics regarding North, Central, and South America may be found in the World History and Geography sections of this Sequence.
items.zh: 教师：美国历史的学习从幼儿园到二年级开始，先简要概述从最早时期到近现代的重大事件和人物。更深入、按时间顺序展开的美国历史学习从三年级重新开始并持续推进。这里所说的“美国（American）”通常但并非总是指后来成为美国的那片土地。关于北美、中美和南美的其他主题，可见本《序列》的世界历史与地理部分。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Native American Peoples, Past and Present
items.en: As students progress through the grades of the Core Knowledge Sequence, they will learn about many different Native American peoples in many different regions (such as Pacific Northwest: Kwakiutl (Kwakwaka’wakw, Chinook; Plateau: Nez Perce; Great Basin: Shoshone, Ute; Southwest: Dine \[Navajo\], Hopi, Apache, Zuni; Plains: Blackfoot, Comanche, Crow, Kiowa, Dakota, Lakota \[Sioux\], Cheyenne, Arapaho; Eastern Woodlands: Huron, Iroquois, Mohican, Delaware \[Lenni Lenape\], Susquehanna, Massachusett, Wampanoag, Powhatan; Southeast: Cherokee, Seminole). In kindergarten, study at least one specific group of Native Americans. You might explore a local or regional tribe or nation, and compare it with one far away.
items.zh: 随着学生在《核心知识序列》各年级的学习，他们将了解许多不同地区的众多美洲原住民民族（如太平洋西北地区：夸基乌特尔〔Kwakwaka'wakw〕、奇努克；高原地区：内兹佩尔塞；大盆地地区：肖肖尼、尤特；西南地区：迪内〔纳瓦霍〕、霍皮、阿帕奇、祖尼；大平原地区：黑脚、科曼奇、克劳、凯奥瓦、达科他、拉科塔〔苏族〕、夏延、阿拉帕霍；东部林地：休伦、易洛魁、莫希甘、特拉华〔莱尼莱纳佩〕、萨斯奎汉纳、马萨诸塞、万帕诺亚格、波瓦坦；东南部：切罗基、塞米诺尔）。在幼儿园，至少研究一个具体的美洲原住民族群。你可以考察当地或本地区的一个部落或民族，并与远方的另一个族群进行比较。

items.en: Columbus Day is an important holiday for many Americans, but in some states the holiday has been renamed Indigenous People’s Day in recognition of the harm that was caused to the indigenous peoples of the Americas by explorers, adventurers, and settlers from Europe. In fact, Columbus did enslave the Taino people and take them back to Europe with him. Although elements of Columbus’s story are dark, his voyages do mark a great change in the history of the world.
items.zh: 哥伦布日对许多美国人来说是重要节日，但在一些州，这个节日已被改名为“原住民日”，以承认欧洲探险家、冒险家和定居者给美洲原住民造成的伤害。事实上，哥伦布确实奴役过泰诺人，并把他们带回欧洲。尽管哥伦布的故事有阴暗的一面，但他的航行确实标志着世界历史上的巨大变化。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Note: Discussing slavery with younger students is a very challenging task. Slavery, which has existed for thousands of years in many cultures, is by definition an inhumane practice—people are reduced to property, to be bought and sold, and often treated with brutality and violence. Classroom discussion of slavery should acknowledge its cruelty while remaining mindful of the age of the students. Note: No historical evidence exists to confirm Plymouth Rock as the Pilgrims’ steppingstone to the New World. In fact, it is believed that the Pilgrims first made landfall on the tip of Cape Cod in November 1620 before sailing to safer harbors in Plymouth the following month. William Bradford, and his fellow Mayflower passengers, made no written references to setting foot on a rock as they disembarked to start their settlement on a new continent.
items.zh: 注：与年幼学生讨论奴隶制是一项非常具有挑战性的任务。奴隶制在许多文化中已存在数千年，按其本质就是一种不人道的做法——人被贬为财产，可以被买卖，且常常遭受残暴对待和暴力。课堂上讨论奴隶制时，既要承认其残酷性，也要顾及学生的年龄。注：没有历史证据能够证实普利茅斯岩就是清教徒登陆新大陆的第一块踏脚石。事实上，人们认为清教徒于1620年11月首次在科德角尖端登陆，之后于次月驶往普利茅斯更安全的港口。威廉·布拉德福德和“五月花号”上的同行乘客，在登陆开辟新大陆的定居点时，并没有留下任何关于踏上某块岩石的文字记载。

items.subject: Visual Arts
items.en: Teachers: In schools, lessons on the visual arts should illustrate important elements of making and appreciating art, and emphasize important artists, works of art, and artistic concepts. When appropriate, topics in the visual arts may be linked to topics in other disciplines. The following guidelines specify a variety of artwork in different media and from various cultures in order to expose students to a wide range of art and artists. While the list is robust, it may require teachers to narrow the selection in order to adequately address the works and related skills within an academic year.
items.zh: 教师：学校的视觉艺术课程应展示艺术创作与欣赏的重要元素，并重点介绍重要艺术家、艺术作品和艺术概念。在适当的时候，视觉艺术主题可以与其他学科主题相联系。以下指导方针列举了不同媒介和不同文化的多种艺术作品，以让学生接触广泛的艺术和艺术家。这份清单内容相当丰富，教师可能需要缩小选择范围，以便在一个学年内充分讲解这些作品及相关技能。

items.subject: Visual Arts
items.en: The generally recognized elements of art include line, shape, form, space, light, texture, and color. In kindergarten, introduce students to line and color. Engage students in recognizing and using different kinds of lines and colors, and point out lines and colors in nature. (You may also wish to observe shapes in art and nature—see Math: Geometry.)
items.zh: 公认的艺术元素包括线条、形状、形体、空间、光、质感和色彩。在幼儿园，向学生介绍线条和色彩。引导学生认识并使用不同种类的线条和色彩，并指出自然界中的线条和色彩。（也可以观察艺术和自然中的形状——见数学：几何。）

items.subject: Visual Arts
items.en: Observe how colors can create different feelings and how certain colors can seem “warm” (red, orange, yellow) or “cool” (blue, green, purple).
items.zh: 观察色彩如何引发不同的感受，以及某些颜色如何显得“暖”（红、橙、黄）或“冷”（蓝、绿、紫）。

items.en: After students have been introduced to some elements of art and a range of artworks and artists, engage them in looking at pictures and talking about them. Ask the students about their first impressions—what they notice first, and what the picture makes them think of or feel. Go on to discuss the lines and colors, details not obvious at first, why they think the artist chose to depict things in a certain way, etc.

items.subject: Music
items.en: Teachers: In schools, lessons on music should feature activities and works that illustrate important musical concepts and terms, and should introduce important composers and works. When appropriate, topics in music may be linked to topics in other disciplines. The following guidelines focus on content, not performance skills, though many concepts are best learned through active practice (singing, clapping rhythms, playing instruments, etc.).
items.zh: 教师：学校的音乐课应包含能够体现重要音乐概念和术语的活动与作品，并应介绍重要作曲家和作品。在适当的时候，音乐主题可以与其他学科主题相联系。以下指导方针侧重内容而非表演技能，不过许多概念最好通过积极实践来学习（唱歌、拍节奏、演奏乐器等）。

items.subject: Music
items.en: Through participation, become familiar with some basic elements of music (rhythm, melody, harmony, form, timbre, etc.).
items.zh: 通过参与，熟悉音乐的一些基本元素（节奏、旋律、和声、曲式、音色等）。

items.en: Recognize a steady beat; begin to play a steady beat.
items.zh: 感受稳定的拍子；开始能打出稳定的节拍。

items.subject: Music
items.en: Recognize that some beats have accents (stress).
items.zh: 认识到有些拍子带有重音（强调）。

items.subject: Music

items.zh: 随着音乐做出相应动作（列队行进、走、单脚跳、摇摆等）。

items.en: To encourage listening skills and the beginnings of understanding, play various kinds of music often and repeatedly. In the kindergarten classroom, music can be played for enjoyment, to accompany activities, to inspire creative movement, etc. Expose children to a wide range of music, including children’s music, popular instrumental music, and music from various cultures.
