items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Teachers: Mathematics has its own vocabulary and patterns of thinking. It is a discipline with its own language and conventions. Thus, while some lessons may offer occasional opportunities for linking mathematics to other disciplines, it is critically important to attend to math as math. From the earliest years, mathematics requires incremental review and steady practice: not only the diligent effort required to master basic facts and operations, but also thoughtful and varied practice that approaches problems from a variety of angles, and gives children a variety of opportunities to apply the same concept or operation in different types of situations. While it is important to work toward the development of “higher-order problem-solving skills,” it is equally important—indeed, it is prerequisite to achieving “higher order” skills—to have a sound grasp of basic facts, and an automatic fluency with fundamental operations.
items.zh: 教师：数学有自己的词汇和思维方式，是一门拥有自身语言和规范的学科。因此，虽然有些课程偶尔会提供把数学与其他学科联系起来的机会，但把数学当作数学来对待至关重要。从最早年级起，数学就需要循序渐进的复习和持续的练习：既要付出努力掌握基本事实和运算，也要进行深思熟虑、形式多样的练习，从多种角度处理问题，并让孩子有各种机会在不同情境中运用同一概念或运算。虽然培养“高阶问题解决能力”很重要，但扎实掌握基本事实、对基本运算达到自动化熟练同样重要——事实上，这是达到“高阶”技能的前提。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Know number names and the count sequence.
items.zh: 知道数的名称和数数的顺序。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
items.zh: 能一个一个地数到100，也能十个十个地数到100。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence.
items.zh: 在已知数序中，能从给定的数开始接着往后数。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Write numbers from 0 to 20.
items.zh: 能写出0到20的数字。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0–20.
items.zh: 用数字0–20表示物体的数量。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Count to tell the number of objects.
items.zh: 通过数数说出物体的数量。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities.
items.zh: 理解数与数量之间的关系。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Connect counting to cardinality.
items.zh: 把数数与基数（数量的多少）联系起来。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Count to answer “how many?” questions,
items.zh: 通过数数回答“有多少？”的问题，
details: With as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle;
With as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.
items.zh: 给出1–20之间的一个数，能数出相应数量的物体。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Compare numbers.
items.zh: 比较数的大小。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group.
items.zh: 判断一组物体的数量是大于、小于还是等于另一组物体的数量。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.
items.zh: 比较以数字形式呈现的1到10之间的两个数。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
items.zh: 理解加法是把东西合起来、加上去，理解减法是把东西分拆开、拿走。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Represent addition and subtraction with:
items.zh: 用以下方式表示加法和减法：
details: objects
fingers
mental images
drawings
sounds (e.g., claps)
acting out situations
verbal explanations
expressions
equations

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Solve addition and subtraction word problems (within 10).
items.zh: 解决10以内的加减法文字题。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way.
items.zh: 用多种方式把小于或等于10的数拆分成两个数之和。
details: Record each decomposition by a drawing or equation.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number. • Record the answer with a drawing or equation.
items.zh: 对于1到9中的任意一个数，找出与它相加等于10的那个数。用图画或算式记录答案。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Fluently add and subtract within 5. III. Number and Operations in Base Ten
items.zh: 熟练进行5以内的加减法。三、十进制中的数与运算

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Work with numbers 11–19 to gain foundations for place value.
items.zh: 学习11–19的数，为理解位值打基础。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Understand that numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
items.zh: 理解这些数由1个十和1、2、3、4、5、6、7、8或9个一组成。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones.
items.zh: 把11到19的数拆分成1个十和若干个一，并能组合起来。
details: Record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Describe and compare measurable attributes.
items.zh: 描述并比较可测量的属性。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight.
items.zh: 描述物体的可测量属性，如长度或重量。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.
items.zh: 描述同一个物体的多个可测量属性。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference.
items.zh: 直接比较两个具有共同可测量属性的物体，看哪个物体该属性“更多”／“更少”，并描述差异。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Classify objects into given categories.
items.zh: 按给定类别对物体进行分类。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.
items.zh: 数出每一类中物体的数量，并按数量多少对类别排序。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).
items.zh: 识别并描述形状（正方形、圆形、三角形、长方形、六边形、立方体、圆锥、圆柱和球体）。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects.
items.zh: 用形状名称描述环境中的物体，并描述这些物体的相对位置。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.
items.zh: 无论形状朝向或整体大小如何，都能正确说出其名称。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three-dimensional (“solid”).
items.zh: 区分二维图形（位于平面上，“平的”）和三维立体（“实心的”）。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
items.zh: 分析、比较、创造和拼组形状。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes:
items.zh: 分析并比较二维和三维形状：
details: In different sizes and orientations;
Using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts and other attributes.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components and drawing shapes.
items.zh: 通过用部件搭建形状和画出形状，来建立现实世界中形状的模型。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.
items.zh: 用简单形状拼组成更大的形状。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Teachers: Effective instruction in science requires hands-on experience and observation. In the words of the report from the National Academies of Science, A Framework for K-12 Science Education, “...children entering kindergarten have surprisingly sophisticated ways of thinking about the world, based in part on their direct experiences with the physical environment such as watching objects fall or collide and observing plants and animals. They also learn about the world through everyday activities, such as talking with their families, pursuing hobbies, watching television, and playing with friends. As children try to understand and influence the world around them, they develop ideas about their role in that world and how it works. In fact, the capacity of young children—from all backgrounds and socioeconomic levels—to reason in sophisticated ways is much greater than has long been assumed. Although they may lack deep knowledge and extensive experience, they often engage in a wide range of subtle and complex reasoning about the world. Thus, before they even enter school, children have developed their own ideas about the physical, biological, and social worlds and how they work. By listening to and taking these ideas seriously, educators can build on what children already know and can do.”
items.zh: 教师：有效的科学教学需要动手体验和观察。正如美国国家科学院《K-12 科学教育框架》报告所说：“……刚进幼儿园的孩子，对世界有着出人意料复杂精细的思考方式，这部分源于他们对物理环境的直接体验，比如观看物体下落或碰撞、观察动植物。他们也通过日常活动认识世界，例如与家人交谈、发展爱好、看电视、和朋友玩耍。当孩子试图理解并影响周围世界时，他们会形成关于自己在其中的角色以及世界如何运作的想法。事实上，幼儿——无论来自何种背景、何种社会经济阶层——进行复杂推理的能力，远比长期以来人们所认为的要强得多。虽然他们可能缺乏深入的知识和丰富的经验，但他们常常会对世界进行各种细致而复杂的推理。因此，甚至在入学之前，儿童就已经对物理世界、生物世界和社会世界及其运作方式形成了自己的看法。通过倾听并认真对待这些想法，教育者可以在儿童已有知识和能力的基础上进行教学。”

items.subject: Science
items.en: Through reading aloud, observation, and activities such as identifying examples of different kinds of pushes and pulls, explore the following with students:
items.zh: 通过朗读、观察，以及辨认不同种类推和拉的实例等活动，与学生一起探究以下内容：

items.subject: Science
items.en: A force is a push or a pull.
items.zh: 力是推或拉。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Pushes and pulls can involve direct or indirect contact between objects.
items.zh: 推和拉可以涉及物体之间的直接接触或间接接触。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Pushes and pulls can be explored in everyday life.
items.zh: 推和拉可以在日常生活中进行探究。

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: Pushes and Pulls can Change an Object’s Motion
items.en: Pushes and pulls can cause objects that are not moving, or at rest, to move.
items.zh: 推和拉能使静止不动的物体运动起来。

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: Pushes and Pulls can Change an Object’s Motion
items.en: Pushes and pulls can change the motion, —the speed and/or direction—of objects.
items.zh: 推和拉可以改变物体的运动状态，即速度和/或方向。

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: Pushes and Pulls can Change an Object’s Motion
items.en: When objects collide with one another, the motions of the colliding objects can change direction.
items.zh: 当物体相互碰撞时，碰撞物体的运动方向可能会改变。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Magnetism and gravity are examples of indirect, non-contact forces.
items.zh: 磁力和重力是间接的、非接触力的例子。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Magnets are certain metals that can push or pull some metal objects.
items.zh: 磁铁是某些能推或拉某些金属物体的金属。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Magnets have two ends, called poles, that behave differently.
items.zh: 磁铁有两个端点，称为磁极，它们的行为各不相同。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Magnets can be useful in everyday devices (cabinet doors, refrigerator magnets).
items.zh: 磁铁在日常设备中有用途（橱柜门、冰箱贴）。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Through reading aloud, observation, and activities such as investigating growing plants in your classroom, introduce students to the needs of living things. Students should explore the following:
items.zh: 通过朗读、观察以及诸如在教室里研究植物生长等活动，向学生介绍生物的需求。学生应探究以下内容：

items.subject: Science
items.en: A living thing is an organism.
items.zh: 生物就是有机体。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Organisms can grow, respond to environments, reproduce, and use food energy for life processes.
items.zh: 有机体能够生长、对环境作出反应、繁殖，并利用食物中的能量维持生命活动。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Plants are organisms. Collaborate with your third grade colleagues regarding future expectations and definitions of forces. Grade 3, Investigating Forces
items.zh: 植物是有机体。请与三年级同事协作，商讨今后对力的期望和定义。三年级《探究力》

items.subject: Science
items.en: There are many types of plants.
items.zh: 植物有很多种。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Most plants have stems, roots, and leaves.
items.zh: 大多数植物有茎、根和叶。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Animals are organisms.
items.zh: 动物是有机体。

items.subject: Science
items.en: There are many types of animals .
items.zh: 动物有很多种。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Animals have certain parts for certain functions (structure: exoskeleton or skeleton; movement: legs, fins, wings; nutrition: mouth, digestive tract; protection: fur, shell).
items.zh: 动物有特定的部位执行特定的功能（结构：外骨骼或骨骼；运动：腿、鳍、翅膀；营养：嘴、消化道；保护：皮毛、外壳）。

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: Plants, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Plants need air, water, light, and space.
items.zh: 植物需要空气、水、光和空间。

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: Plants, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Plants get what they need from their environment.
items.zh: 植物从环境中获取所需的一切。

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: Plants, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Different types of plants live in different types of environments.
items.zh: 不同类型的植物生活在不同的环境中。

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: Plants, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Plants make their own food using sunlight and air.
items.zh: 植物利用阳光和空气自己制造食物。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Animals, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Animals need air, food, water, and shelter to survive.
items.zh: 动物需要空气、食物、水和栖息地才能生存。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Animals, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Animals get what they need from their environments.
items.zh: 动物从环境中获取所需的一切。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Animals, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Different types of animals live in different types of environments.
items.zh: 不同类型的动物生活在不同的环境中。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Animals, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Animals get their food from eating other living things.
items.zh: 动物通过吃其他生物来获取食物。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Humans, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Human beings are a type of animal.
items.zh: 人类是一种动物。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Humans, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Humans need air, food, water, shelter to survive.
items.zh: 人类需要空气、食物、水和住所才能生存。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Humans, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Humans get what they need from their environment.
items.zh: 人类从环境中获取所需的一切。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: Humans, Their Needs, and Their Environments
items.en: Humans are omnivores.
items.zh: 人类是杂食动物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The emphasis in kindergarten should be on observation, description, and explanation of real world experiences of different environments and the exploration of how natural spaces can change over time. Technical explanations of ecological phenomena and human impacts on the environment should be taken up in later grades; see Grades 2, 3, and 5 for an increasingly more detailed study of Ecology:
items.zh: 幼儿园阶段的重点应是对不同环境的真实世界体验进行观察、描述和解释，并探索自然空间如何随时间变化。对生态现象及人类影响环境的技术性解释应留待更高年级；生态学日益详细的研究参见二、三、五年级：

items.subject: Science
items.en: Plants and animals live in environments that meet their needs.
items.zh: 动植物生活在能满足其需求的环境中。

items.subject: Science
items.en: habitats, ecosystems
items.zh: 栖息地、生态系统

items.subject: Science
items.en: Changes in environment affect the organisms that live there.
items.zh: 环境的变化会影响生活在那里的生物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Plants, such as water hyacinth and kudzu, can change ecosystems, affecting the ability of other living things in the ecosystem to meet their own needs.
items.zh: 凤眼莲（水葫芦）和葛藤等植物会改变生态系统，影响生态系统中其他生物满足自身需求的能力。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Animals, such as the zebra mussel and the beaver, can change ecosystems, affecting the ability of other living things in the ecosystem to meet their own needs.
items.zh: 斑马贻贝和海狸等动物会改变生态系统，影响生态系统中其他生物满足自身需求的能力。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Humans can change ecosystems through roads, cities, pollution, etc. affecting the ability of other living things in the ecosystem to meet their own needs.
items.zh: 人类可以通过道路、城市、污染等改变生态系统，影响生态系统中其他生物满足自身需求的能力。

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: People Design Solutions to Reduce Human Impact
items.en: People can make choices to reduce the amount of change they cause to ecosystems:
items.zh: 人们可以作出选择，减少自己对生态系统造成的改变：

items.subject: Science
items.subtopic: People Design Solutions to Reduce Human Impact
items.en: Sustainable farming, reforestation, recycling, and pollution reduction Collaborate with your fifth grade colleagues to connect this topic to learning in Grade 5, Protecting Earth’s Resources.
items.zh: 可持续农业、植树造林、资源回收和减少污染。请与五年级同事协作，将本主题与五年级《保护地球资源》的学习联系起来。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The sun is a star that lights the sky during the daytime.
items.zh: 太阳是一颗恒星，在白天照亮天空。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Sunlight warms Earth’s surface.
items.zh: 阳光使地球表面变暖。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Blocking sunlight reduces its warming effect on Earth’s surface and materials.
items.zh: 遮挡阳光会减弱其对地球表面和物体的升温作用。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Weather is what the air is like outside at any one time and place.
items.zh: 天气是指某一时间、某一地点外面的空气状况。

items.subject: Science
items.en: People collect and record weather data, such as temperature, rainfall, wind speed and direction, to reveal patterns.
items.zh: 人们收集和记录天气数据，如温度、降雨量、风速和风向，以揭示规律。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Seasons are repeating patterns of weather within the course of a year.
items.zh: 季节是一年之中反复出现的天气模式。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Weather can be severe and can cause damage, for example, thunder, lightning, heavy rain, high wind, tornadoes, hail, blizzards, hurricanes, drought, and heat waves.
items.zh: 天气可能很恶劣并造成破坏，例如雷、闪电、暴雨、大风、龙卷风、冰雹、暴风雪、飓风、干旱和热浪。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Looking at patterns in weather data helps people predict, or forecast, when severe weather will occur.
items.zh: 观察天气数据中的规律有助于人们预测（预报）恶劣天气何时出现。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: Vision is the ability to detect objects by light.
items.zh: 视觉是借助光察觉物体的能力。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: Eyes are the organs of vision.
items.zh: 眼睛是视觉器官。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: Hearing is the ability to detect sound.
items.zh: 听觉是察觉声音的能力。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: The ears are the organs of hearing.
items.zh: 耳朵是听觉器官。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: The senses of sight and hearing enable people to perform many important tasks.
items.zh: 视觉和听觉使人能够完成许多重要的任务。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: Corrective lenses and hearing aids may help with vision and hearing impairments.
items.zh: 矫正镜片和助听器有助于改善视力和听力障碍。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: Other ways to help those with impaired hearing or vision include sign language, assistive animals, and braille.
items.zh: 帮助听力或视力受损者的其他方式包括手语、辅助动物和盲文。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: The sense of smell is the ability to detect scent/odor.
items.zh: 嗅觉是察觉气味的能力。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: The nose is the organ of smell.
items.zh: 鼻子是嗅觉器官。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: The sense of taste is the ability to detect chemicals in the environment.
items.zh: 味觉是察觉环境中化学物质的能力。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: The taste buds enable a sense of taste.
items.zh: 味蕾使人产生味觉。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: The sense of touch is the ability to feel things in the environment.
items.zh: 触觉是感知环境中事物的能力。

items.subject: Science
items.topic: The Human Body: Our Five Senses
items.en: Nerves in the skin enable a sense of touch.
items.zh: 皮肤中的神经使人产生触觉。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Proper care of the body helps all senses to work most effectively.
items.zh: 适当照顾身体有助于各种感官最有效地发挥作用。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Healthy foods promote wellness of the senses. VI. Science Biographies Teachers: Through reading aloud and activities, explore with students the stories and accomplishments of these scientists and engineers. This list of science biographies is by no means exhaustive. Other individuals can be incorporated into learning during a corresponding topic of study for this grade level, and should include:
items.zh: 健康食品有助于感官健康。VI. 科学人物传记 教师：通过朗读和活动，与学生一起探究这些科学家和工程师的故事与成就。这份科学人物传记列表并不详尽。其他人物也可在本年级相应主题的学习中引入，应包括：

items.subject: Science
items.en: Isaac Newton—English physicist and mathematician, described the roles of forces in the universe
items.zh: 艾萨克·牛顿——英国物理学家和数学家，描述了力在宇宙中的作用

items.subject: Science
items.en: Rachel Carson—discussed the dangers of pesticides
items.zh: 蕾切尔·卡逊——探讨了农药的危害

items.subject: Science
items.en: George Washington Carver—used plants for human benefit
items.zh: 乔治·华盛顿·卡弗——利用植物造福人类

items.subject: Science
items.en: Abbe Cleveland—founded the National Weather Service
items.zh: 阿比·克利夫兰——创建了美国国家气象局

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: NOTE: The objectives listed in sections I–IV of Language Arts below are consistent with the Core Knowledge Language Arts program and embed all of the skills and concepts within the Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts.
items.zh: 注：以下语言艺术第 I—IV 节所列的目标与“核心知识语言艺术”课程一致，并涵盖了《共同核心州立标准》英语语言艺术中的全部技能和概念。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Traditional language arts instruction has typically accorded little, if any, attention to the ongoing development of children’s listening and speaking ability. This failure to focus on the development of oral language in language arts instruction has been a serious oversight. Literacy, the ability to read and write written language, is highly correlated with students’ oral language proficiency, and the ability to understand a text read aloud is a prerequisite for making sense of the same text in printed form. It is therefore essential that children build listening and speaking competency while also developing reading and writing skills.
items.zh: 传统的语言艺术教学通常很少甚至根本不关注儿童听说能力的持续发展。这种在语言艺术教学中忽视口语能力发展的做法是一个严重的疏漏。读写能力，即阅读和书写书面语言的能力，与学生的口语水平高度相关；而听懂朗读文本的能力，是理解同一印刷文本的前提。因此，儿童在发展读写技能的同时，必须培养听说能力。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Participate in age appropriate activities involving listening and speaking.
items.zh: 参加适合年龄的、涉及听和说的活动。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Speak clearly with volume appropriate to the setting.
items.zh: 说话清晰，音量适合场合。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use agreed-upon rules for group discussions, i.e., look at and listen to the speaker, raise hand to speak, take turns, say “excuse me” or “please,” etc.
items.zh: 遵守约定的小组讨论规则，即：看着并倾听说话者、举手发言、轮流、说“打扰一下”或“请”等。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Ask questions to clarify conversations, directions, exercises, and/or classroom routines.
items.zh: 通过提问来澄清对话、指令、练习和/或课堂常规。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Carry on and participate in a conversation over at least six turns, staying on topic, initiating comments or responding to a partner’s comments, with either an adult or another child of the same age.
items.zh: 与成人或同龄儿童进行至少六个来回的对话，保持话题，主动发表意见或回应对方。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify and express physical sensations, mental states, and emotions of self and others.
items.zh: 识别并表达自己和他人的身体感觉、心理状态和情绪。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and use language to express spatial and temporal relationships (up, down, first, last, before, after, etc.).
items.zh: 理解并使用语言表达空间和时间关系（上、下、第一、最后、以前、以后等）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and use narrative language to describe people, places, things, locations, events, actions.
items.zh: 理解并使用叙事性语言描述人物、地点、事物、位置、事件和动作。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and use common sayings and phrases such as “Hit the nail on the head” and “Let the cat out of the bag.”
items.zh: 理解并使用常见谚语和短语，如“一针见血”（Hit the nail on the head）和“泄露秘密”（Let the cat out of the bag）。
items.work: Hit the nail on the head

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Follow multi-step, oral directions.
items.zh: 听从多步骤的口头指令。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Give simple directions.
items.zh: 给出简单的指令。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Provide simple explanations.
items.zh: 给出简单的解释。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Recite a nursery rhyme, poem or song independently, using appropriate eye contact, volume and clear enunciation.
items.zh: 独立朗诵童谣、诗歌或唱歌，眼神交流、音量和吐字恰当。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Give oral presentations about personal experiences, topics of interest, and/or stories, using appropriate eye contact, volume and clear enunciation.
items.zh: 就个人经历、感兴趣的话题和/或故事作口头陈述，眼神交流、音量和吐字恰当。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Written text makes use of richer vocabulary and more complex syntax than conversational language. It is important that young children be exposed not only to the language of everyday conversation but also to the richer and more formal language of books.
items.zh: 书面文本使用的词汇比会话语言更丰富，句法更复杂。幼儿不仅应接触日常会话语言，也应接触书籍中更丰富、更正式的语言。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Listen to and understand a variety of texts read aloud, including fictional stories, fairy tales, fables, historical narratives, drama, informational text, and poems.
items.zh: 听懂各种朗读文本，包括虚构故事、童话、寓言、历史叙述、戏剧、说明性文本和诗歌。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Distinguish the following genres of literature: fiction, nonfiction and drama.
items.zh: 区分以下文学体裁：小说、非虚构作品和戏剧。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Describe illustrations.
items.zh: 描述插图。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与关键思想

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Sequence four to six pictures illustrating events in a read-aloud.
items.zh: 将四到六幅描绘朗读内容的图片排序。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与关键思想

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Answer questions requiring literal recall and understanding of the details and/or facts of a read-aloud, i.e., who, what, where, when, etc.
items.zh: 回答需要直接回忆和理解朗读细节和/或事实的问题，即谁、什么、哪里、何时等。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与关键思想

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Retell key details.
items.zh: 复述关键细节。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与关键思想

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Ask questions to clarify information in a read-aloud.
items.zh: 通过提问弄清朗读中的信息。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与关键思想

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Use narrative language to describe people, places, things, locations, events, actions, a scene or facts in a read-aloud.
items.zh: 使用叙述性语言描述朗读中的人物、地点、事物、位置、事件、动作、场景或事实。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与关键思想

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Understand and use words and phrases heard in read-alouds.
items.zh: 理解并使用朗读中听到的单词和短语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Compare and contrast similarities and differences within a single read-aloud or between two or more read-alouds.
items.zh: 比较和对比单篇朗读内或多篇朗读之间的异同。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Make personal connections to events or experiences in a read-aloud and/or make connections among several read-alouds.
items.zh: 将个人经历与朗读中的事件或体验联系起来，和/或在多篇朗读之间建立联系。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Prior to listening to a read-aloud, identify what they know and have learned that may be related to the specific story or topic to be read aloud.
items.zh: 在听朗读之前，找出自己已知的、可能与将要朗读的具体故事或主题相关的内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Use pictures accompanying the read-aloud to check and support understanding of the read-aloud.
items.zh: 利用朗读配图检查和帮助理解朗读内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Make predictions prior to and during a read-aloud, based on the title, pictures, and/or text heard thus far and then compare the actual outcomes to predictions.
items.zh: 朗读前和朗读中根据标题、图片和/或已听到的文本进行预测，然后将实际结果与预测比较。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Answer questions that require making interpretations, judgments, or giving opinions about what is heard in a read-aloud, including answering “why” questions that require recognizing cause/effect relationships.
items.zh: 回答需要对朗读内容作出解读、判断或发表看法的问题，包括需要识别因果关系的“为什么”类问题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Interpret information that is presented orally and then ask additional questions to clarify information or the topic in the read-aloud.
items.zh: 解读口头呈现的信息，然后进一步提问以弄清朗读中的信息或主题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—All Texts
items.en: Identify who is telling a story or providing information in a text.
items.zh: 识别文本中是谁在讲故事或提供信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Retell or dramatize a story, using narrative language to describe characters, setting(s), and a beginning, a middle and an end to events of the story in proper sequence.
items.zh: 复述或表演一个故事，用叙事性语言描述人物、背景，并按恰当顺序描述故事事件的开头、中间和结尾。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Compare and contrast characters from different stories.
items.zh: 比较和对比不同故事中的人物。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Change some story events and provide a different story ending.
items.zh: 改动某些故事事件，并给出一个不同的故事结局。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Create and tell an original story, using narrative language to describe characters, setting(s), and a beginning, a middle and an end to events of the story in proper sequence.
items.zh: 创作并讲述一个原创故事，用叙述性语言描述人物、场景，并按正确顺序描述故事的开头、中间和结尾。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Distinguish fantasy from realistic text in a story.
items.zh: 区分故事中的幻想情节与现实情节。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Identify the moral or lesson of a fable, folktale, or myth.
items.zh: 找出寓言、民间故事或神话的寓意或教训。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of literary language (e.g., author, illustrator, characters, setting, plot, dialogue, personification, simile, and metaphor) and use some of these terms in retelling stories or creating their own stories.
items.zh: 理解文学语言（如作者、插画家、人物、场景、情节、对话、拟人、明喻和暗喻），并在复述故事或创作自己的故事时使用其中一些术语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Identify sensory language and how it is used to describe people, objects, places and events. E. Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Nonfiction and Informational Text Teachers: Select nonfiction read-aloud topics from the first grade history, science, music, and visual arts topics, with emphasis on history and science.
items.zh: 识别感官语言及其如何用于描述人物、物体、地点和事件。E. 朗读的理解与讨论——非虚构与说明性文本 教师：从一年级历史、科学、音乐和视觉艺术主题中选择非虚构朗读主题，重点为历史和科学。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Generate questions and seek information from multiple sources to answer questions.
items.zh: 提出问题，并从多个来源寻找信息来回答问题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Answer questions about the details of a nonfiction text, indicating which part of the text provided the information needed to answer specific questions.
items.zh: 回答有关非虚构文本细节的问题，并指出文本的哪一部分提供了回答特定问题所需的信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: With assistance, categorize and organize facts and information within a given topic.
items.zh: 在帮助下，将给定主题范围内的事实和信息分类整理。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: With assistance, create and interpret timelines and lifelines related to read-alouds.
items.zh: 在帮助下，制作并解读与朗读内容相关的时间线和生平线。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Comprehension and Discussion of Read-Alouds—Fiction, Drama, and Poetry
items.en: Distinguish read-alouds that describe events that happened long ago from those that describe contemporary or current events.
items.zh: 区分描述很久以前发生的事件的朗读与描述当代或当前事件的朗读。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that what is said can be written and that the writing system is a way of writing down sounds.
items.zh: 理解说出的话可以被写下来，文字系统就是把声音记录下来的一种方式。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of directionality (left to right, return sweep, top to bottom, front to back).
items.zh: 理解书写方向（从左到右、换行回扫、从上到下、从前到后）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify the parts of books and function of each part (front cover, back cover, title page, table of contents).
items.zh: 认识书的各部分及其功能（封面、封底、扉页、目录）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate correct book orientation by holding book correctly and turning pages.
items.zh: 能正确拿书并正确翻页，表现出正确的书本方向感。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Recognize that sentences in print are made up of separate words.
items.zh: 认识到印刷出来的句子是由一个个独立的词组成的。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand that words are separated by spaces.
items.zh: 理解词与词之间用空格分隔。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Distinguish letters, words, sentences, and stories.
items.zh: 区分字母、单词、句子和故事。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of basic print conventions by tracking and following print word for word when listening to text read aloud.
items.zh: 听朗读时能逐词跟随并指读印刷文字，表现出对基本印刷惯例的理解。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that the sequence of letters in a written word represents the sequence of sounds in the spoken word.
items.zh: 理解书写单词中字母的顺序代表口语单词中声音的顺序。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Recognize and name the 26 letters of the alphabet in both their upper-case and lower-case forms.
items.zh: 识别并说出字母表中 26 个字母的大写和小写形式。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Say the letters of the alphabet in order, either in song or recitation. B. Phonemic Awareness
items.zh: 以唱歌或背诵的方式按顺序说出字母表。B. 音素意识

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that words are made up of sequences of sounds.
items.zh: 理解单词是由一串声音组成的。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that vowel sounds are produced with the mouth open and airflow unobstructed, whereas consonant sounds involve closing parts of the mouth and blocking the air flow.
items.zh: 理解元音是张口、气流不受阻碍发出的音，而辅音则需要闭合口腔的某些部位、阻断气流而发出。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Given a pair of spoken words, select the one that is longer (i.e., contains more phonemes).
items.zh: 给出一对口头说出的单词，选出较长的那个（即包含更多音素的那个）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: In riddle games, supply words that begin with a target phoneme.
items.zh: 在猜谜游戏中，说出以目标音素开头的单词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Indicate whether a target phoneme is or is not present in the initial/medial/final position of a spoken word, e.g., hear /m/ at the beginning of mat and /g/ at the end of bag.
items.zh: 判断某个目标音素是否出现在口语单词的词首／词中／词尾，例如在 mat 的开头听到 /m/，在 bag 的结尾听到 /g/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Listen to one-syllable words and tell the beginning or ending sounds, e.g., given dog, identify initial /d/ or final /g/.
items.zh: 听单音节词并说出其开头或结尾的音，例如给出 dog，能指出开头的 /d/ 或结尾的 /g/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Recognize the same phoneme in different spoken words, e.g., /b/ in ball, bug, and big.
items.zh: 在不同的口语单词中识别相同的音素，如 ball、bug、big 中的 /b/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify whether pairs of phonemes are the same or different, including pairs that differ only in voicing, e.g., /b/ and /p/.
items.zh: 判断成对的音素是相同还是不同，包括仅在清浊上不同的音素对，如 /b/ 和 /p/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Orally blend two to three sounds to form a word, e.g., given the sounds /k/... /a/.../t/, blend to make cat.
items.zh: 口头把两三个音拼合成一个词，例如给出 /k/…/a/…/t/，拼成 cat。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Segment a spoken word into phonemes, e.g., given bat, produce the segments/b//a//t/.
items.zh: 把一个口语单词切分成音素，例如给出 bat，切分为 /b//a//t/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Given a spoken word, produce another word that rhymes, e.g., given hit, supply bit or mitt.
items.zh: 给出一个口语单词，说出另一个与之押韵的词，例如给出 hit，说出 bit 或 mitt。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify the number of syllables in a spoken word.
items.zh: 识别口头单词中的音节数量。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Learning to read requires understanding and mastering the written English code through explicit and systematic phonics instruction. Research suggests that phonics instruction is most effective when specific letter-sound relationships are taught and reinforced by having students both read and write the letter-sound correspondence being studied. Reading and writing—decoding and encoding—are complementary processes that ensure mastery of the written code.
items.zh: 学会阅读需要通过明确、系统的自然拼读教学来理解和掌握英语书面代码。研究表明，当教师教授具体的字母—音对应关系，并让学生对所学的字母—音对应进行读和写的练习来加以巩固时，自然拼读教学最为有效。阅读与写作——解码与编码——是相辅相成的过程，能确保学生掌握书面代码。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding that a systematic, predictable relationship exists between written letters (graphemes) and spoken sounds (phonemes).
items.zh: 理解书面字母（字素）与口语声音（音素）之间存在系统且可预测的关系。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Blend individual phonemes to pronounce printed words.
items.zh: 把单个音素拼合起来，读出印刷的单词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand that sometimes two or more printed letters stand for a single sound.
items.zh: 理解有时两个或更多印刷字母代表一个音。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read one to two syllable words containing any of the grapheme-phoneme correspondences listed below.
items.zh: 读含有一到两个音节、包含下列任一字素—音素对应关系的单词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read and write words with inflectional endings, i.e., -s, -ed, -ing, -er, -est.
items.zh: 读写带有屈折词尾的单词，即 -s、-ed、-ing、-er、-est。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read, understand, and write contractions, i.e., isn’t, I’m, can’t, etc.
items.zh: 读写并理解缩写形式，如 isn’t、I’m、can’t 等。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Sort and classify words according to the spelling used to represent a specific phoneme.
items.zh: 根据表示特定音素的拼写对单词进行分类。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read tricky spellings that can be sounded two ways, e.g., the letter ‘s’ sounded /s/ as in cats and /z/ as in dogs.
items.zh: 能读有两种读音的棘手拼写，例如字母 s 在 cats 中读 /s/，在 dogs 中读 /z/。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read and spell chains of one-syllable words in which one sound is added, substituted, or omitted, i.e., read at > cat > bat > bad > bid.
items.zh: 读写单音节词链，其中一个音被添加、替换或省略，例如读 at > cat > bat > bad > bid。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read at least 30 words generally identified as high frequency words. Consonant Sounds and Spellings Taught in First Grade /b/ spelled ‘b’ as in boy, ‘bb’; as in tubby /d/ spelled ‘d’ as in dog, ‘dd’ as in madder, ‘ed’ as in filled /f/ spelled ‘f’ as in fun, ‘ff’ as in stuff /g/ spelled ‘g’ as in get, ‘gg’ as in egg /h/ spelled ‘h’ as in him /j/ spelled ‘j’ as in jump, ‘g’ as in gem, ‘ge’ as in fringe /k/ spelled ‘c’ as in cat, ‘k’ as in kitten, ‘ck’ as in sick, ‘cc’ as in moccasin Vowel Sounds and Spellings Taught in First Grade /a/ spelled ‘a’ as in cat /e/ spelled ‘e’ as in get /i/ spelled ‘i’ as in hit /o/ spelled ‘o’ as in hot /u/ spelled ‘u’ as in but /ae/ spelled ‘a\_e’ as in cake, ‘ai’ as in wait, ‘ay’ as in day, ‘a’ as in paper /ee/ spelled ‘ee’ as in bee, ‘e’ as in me, ‘y’ as in funny, ‘ea’ as in beach, ‘e\_e’ as in Pete, ‘ie’ as in cookie /ie/ spelled ‘i\_e’ as in bike, ‘i’ as in biting, ‘y’ as in try, ‘ie’ as in tie, ‘igh’ as in night /oe/ spelled ‘o\_e’ as in note, ‘oa’ as in boat, ‘oe’ as in toe, ‘o’ as in open, ‘ow’ as in snow /ue/ spelled ‘u\_e’ as in cute /aw/ spelled ‘aw’ as in paw /oo/ spelled ‘oo’ as in look, /oo/ spelled ‘oo’ as in soon /ou/ spelled ‘ou’ as in shout /oi/ spelled ‘oi’ as in oil /er/ spelled ‘er’ as in her /ar/ spelled ‘ar’ as is car /or/ spelled ‘or’ as in for
items.zh: 至少认读 30 个通常被认定为高频词的单词。一年级教授的辅音与拼写：/b/ 拼作“b”（如 boy）、“bb”（如 tubby）；/d/ 拼作“d”（如 dog）、“dd”（如 madder）、“ed”（如 filled）；/f/ 拼作“f”（如 fun）、“ff”（如 stuff）；/g/ 拼作“g”（如 get）、“gg”（如 egg）；/h/ 拼作“h”（如 him）；/j/ 拼作“j”（如 jump）、“g”（如 gem）、“ge”（如 fringe）；/k/ 拼作“c”（如 cat）、“k”（如 kitten）、“ck”（如 sick）、“cc”（如 moccasin）。一年级教授的元音与拼写：/a/ 拼作“a”（如 cat）；/e/ 拼作“e”（如 get）；/i/ 拼作“i”（如 hit）；/o/ 拼作“o”（如 hot）；/u/ 拼作“u”（如 but）；/ae/ 拼作“a_e”（如 cake）、“ai”（如 wait）、“ay”（如 day）、“a”（如 paper）；/ee/ 拼作“ee”（如 bee）、“e”（如 me）、“y”（如 funny）、“ea”（如 beach）、“e_e”（如 Pete）、“ie”（如 cookie）；/ie/ 拼作“i_e”（如 bike）、“i”（如 biting）、“y”（如 try）、“ie”（如 tie）、“igh”（如 night）；/oe/ 拼作“o_e”（如 note）、“oa”（如 boat）、“oe”（如 toe）、“o”（如 open）、“ow”（如 snow）；/ue/ 拼作“u_e”（如 cute）；/aw/ 拼作“aw”（如 paw）；/oo/ 拼作“oo”（如 look），/oo/ 拼作“oo”（如 soon）；/ou/ 拼作“ou”（如 shout）；/oi/ 拼作“oi”（如 oil）；/er/ 拼作“er”（如 her）；/ar/ 拼作“ar”（如 car）；/or/ 拼作“or”（如 for）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read decodable stories that incorporate the specific code knowledge that has been taught.
items.zh: 阅读包含已教授的特定拼写解码知识的可解码故事。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate increased accuracy, fluency, and expression on successive reading of a decodable text (50 wpm by the end of the year).
items.zh: 在反复朗读可解码文本时表现出更高的准确性、流利度和表现力（到学年末达到每分钟 50 词）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use phonics skills in conjunction with context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
items.zh: 结合自然拼读技巧与上下文来确认或自我纠正字词识别和理解，必要时重读。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of and use of commas and end punctuation while reading orally.
items.zh: 在口头朗读时理解并使用逗号和句末标点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Read aloud, alone, or with a partner at least 15 minutes each day. E. Reading Comprehension—All Texts Teachers: During the beginning of first grade, most students will still need to devote considerable energy when reading to deciphering the written text. Over the course of this year, they will learn even more elements of the code, meaning that the decodable texts that they can read independently will increasingly resemble “real stories” and trade books. With practice and repeated readings of the same text, students will develop increasing automaticity, allowing them to focus more intently on the meaning of what they are reading. Both of these factors, i.e., the student’s increasing fluency and the use of more authentic text—which is now decodable because of the student’s increasing code knowledge—mean that attention to reading comprehension can move to a higher level than just the rudimentary understanding of text expected at the kindergarten level. This expectation is reflected in the increased number of objectives below that have been added to the kindergarten level objectives. However, it is important to remember that listening comprehension still far exceeds reading comprehension and that children’s ability to talk about what they have heard and/or read will exceed their ability to demonstrate that understanding in writing.
items.zh: 每天独自或与同伴一起朗读至少 15 分钟。E. 所有文本的理解 教师：在一年级刚开始时，大多数学生在阅读时仍需把大量精力用于解码书面文本。在这一年中，他们将学习更多的代码要素，因此他们能独立阅读的可解码文本将越来越接近“真正的故事”和通俗读物。通过练习和反复阅读同一文本，学生的自动化程度会不断提高，从而能更专注地理解所读内容。这两个因素——学生流利度的提高以及更真实文本的使用（由于学生代码知识的增加而变得可解码）——意味着对阅读理解的要求可以提升到高于幼儿园阶段所期望的对文本的基本理解。这一点反映在下面目标数量的增加上，这些目标是在幼儿园目标基础上新增的。但重要的是要记住，听力理解仍然远超阅读理解，儿童谈论所听和/或所读内容的能力将超过他们以书写形式展示这种理解的能力。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of completely decodable text after reading independently.
items.zh: 独立阅读后理解完全可解码的文本。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Sequence four to six pictures illustrating events from a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 将四到六幅描绘独立阅读文本中事件的图片排序。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Answer questions requiring literal recall and understanding of the details and/or facts (i.e., who, what, where, when, etc.) about a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 回答需要直接回忆并理解所读文本细节和／或事实的问题（如谁、什么、哪里、何时等）。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Retell key details from a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 复述独立阅读文本中的关键细节。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Ask questions to clarify information about a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 通过提问弄清独立阅读文本中的信息。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use narrative language to describe people, places, things, locations, events, actions, a scene or facts from a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 用叙述性语言描述独立阅读的文本中的人物、地点、事物、场所、事件、动作、场景或事实。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify basic text features and what they mean, including title, table of contents, and chapters.
items.zh: 识别基本的文本特征及其含义，包括标题、目录和章节。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and use words and phrases from a text that has been read independently.
items.zh: 理解并使用独立阅读的文本中的单词和短语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Compare and contrast similarities and differences within a single text or between multiple texts read independently.
items.zh: 比较和对比单篇文本内或多篇独立阅读文本之间的异同。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Make personal connections to events or experiences in a text that has been read independently and/or make connections among several texts that have been read independently.
items.zh: 将个人经历与独立阅读文本中的事件或体验联系起来，和/或在多篇独立阅读文本之间建立联系。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Prior to reading, identify what they know and have learned that may be related to the specific story or topic to be read.
items.zh: 阅读前，说出自己已知和已学的、可能与将要读的故事或主题相关的内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use pictures accompanying the written text to check and support understanding.
items.zh: 利用随文配图来检验和帮助理解。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Make predictions prior to and while reading, based on the title, pictures, and/or text read thus far and then compare the actual outcomes to predictions.
items.zh: 阅读前和阅读中根据标题、图片和／或已读到的文本做出预测，然后把实际结果与预测进行比较。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Answer questions that require making interpretations, judgments, or giving opinions about what is read independently, including answering “why” questions that require recognizing cause/effect relationships.
items.zh: 回答需要对独立阅读内容作出解读、判断或发表看法的问题，包括需要识别因果关系的“为什么”类问题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify who is telling a story or providing information in a text.
items.zh: 识别文本中是谁在讲故事或提供信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify temporal words that link and sequence events, i.e., first, next, then, etc.
items.zh: 识别连接和排序事件的时间词，即首先、接着、然后等。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify words that link ideas, i.e., for example, also, in addition.
items.zh: 识别连接观点的词，例如“例如”“也”“此外”。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Retell or dramatize a story, using narrative language to describe characters, setting(s), and a beginning, a middle and an end to events of the story in proper sequence.
items.zh: 用叙述性语言复述或表演故事，描述人物、场景，并按正确顺序讲出故事的开头、中间和结局。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Compare and contrast characters from different stories.
items.zh: 比较和对比不同故事中的人物。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Change some story events and provide a different story ending.
items.zh: 改动故事中的某些情节，给出不同的故事结局。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Distinguish fantasy from realistic text in a story.
items.zh: 区分故事中的幻想内容与现实内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify the moral or lesson of a fable, folktale, or myth.
items.zh: 找出寓言、民间故事或神话的寓意或教训。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate understanding of literary language (e.g., author, illustrator, characters, setting, plot, dialogue, personification, simile, and metaphor) and use some of these terms in retelling stories or creating their own stories.
items.zh: 理解文学语言（如作者、插画家、人物、场景、情节、对话、拟人、明喻和暗喻），并在复述故事或创作自己的故事时使用其中一些术语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify sensory language and how it is used to describe people, objects, places and events. G. Reading Comprehension—Nonfiction and Informational Text Teachers: Select nonfiction topics from the first grade history, science, music and visual arts topics listed on pages 35–47, with emphasis on history and science.
items.zh: 识别感官语言及其如何用于描述人物、物体、地点和事件。G. 阅读理解——非虚构与说明性文本 教师：从第 35–47 页列出的一年级历史、科学、音乐和视觉艺术主题中选择非虚构主题，重点为历史和科学。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: With assistance, create and interpret timelines and lifelines related to text read independently.
items.zh: 在帮助下，制作并解读与独立阅读文本相关的时间线和生命线。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Distinguish text that describes events that happened long ago from text that describes contemporary or current events.
items.zh: 区分描述很久以前发生的事件的文本与描述当代或当前事件的文本。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: It is important to recognize that of all the communication skills—listening, speaking, reading, and writing—writing is the most demanding and challenging. During the beginning of first grade, students still need to devote much of their focus and cognitive energy to the code itself, as well as the fine motor act of writing. During this period, teachers should continue to support written expression through shared writing experiences that are modeled and scaffolded by an adult.
items.zh: 重要的是要认识到，在所有交流技能——听、说、读、写——中，写是最难、最具挑战性的。在一年级刚开始时，学生仍需把大量注意力和认知精力放在代码本身以及书写的精细动作上。在此期间，教师应通过成人示范和搭建支架的共同写作活动，继续支持书面表达。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Add details to writing
items.zh: 为写作添加细节
items.section: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose and Task
items.section_zh: 写作要体现读者对象、目的和任务

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Begin to use tools, including technology, to plan, draft, and edit writing
items.zh: 开始使用工具（包括技术）来构思、起草和修改写作
items.section: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose and Task
items.section_zh: 写作要体现读者对象、目的和任务

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Gather information from experiences or provided text sources.
items.zh: 从经历或提供的文本来源中收集信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write or retell a story that includes characters, setting(s), and a beginning, a middle and an end to events of the story in proper sequence.
items.zh: 写或复述一个故事，包含人物、场景，并按正确顺序描述故事的开头、中间和结尾。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write a descriptive paragraph using sensory language.
items.zh: 用感官语言写一段描述性文字。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Create a title and an ending that are relevant to the narrative. B. Informative/Explanatory Writing
items.zh: 创作一个与叙事相关的标题和结尾。B. 说明/解释性写作

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write about a topic, including a beginning and ending sentence, facts and examples relevant to the topic, and specific steps (if writing explanatory text).
items.zh: 围绕一个主题写作，包括开头句和结尾句、与主题相关的事实和例子，以及具体步骤（若写说明性文本）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Express an opinion or point of view in writing, providing reasons and supporting details for preference or opinion using the linking word because.
items.zh: 在写作中表达观点或看法，用连接词“因为”给出理由和支持性细节。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Create a title that is relevant to the topic or subject of the text.
items.zh: 创作一个与文本主题相关的标题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: If writing about a specific book or read-aloud, refer to the content of the text.
items.zh: 如果写某本具体的书或某次朗读，要提及文本内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Form letters, words, phrases and sentences to communicate thoughts and ideas.
items.zh: 书写字母、单词、短语和句子来表达思想和想法。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Apply basic spelling conventions.
items.zh: 运用基本的拼写规则。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use basic capitalization and punctuation in sentences to convey meaning.
items.zh: 在句子中使用基本的大小写和标点来传达意思。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Print from memory the twenty-six letters of the alphabet accurately in both their upper case and lower-case forms.
items.zh: 凭记忆准确书写字母表中 26 个字母的大写和小写形式。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write on primary lined paper from left to right, staying within the lines and leaving spaces between words, and from top to bottom, using return sweep.
items.zh: 在初级横线纸上从左到右书写，保持在横线内并在词间留空格，从上到下书写并换行回扫。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write phonemically plausible spellings for words that cannot be spelled correctly with current code knowledge, e.g., write ate for eight, boi for boy, fone for phone.
items.zh: 对以现有代码知识无法正确拼写的单词，写出符合语音的拼写，例如把 eight 写成 ate、boy 写成 boi、phone 写成 fone。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write words, phrases, and sentences from dictation, applying phonics knowledge.
items.zh: 运用自然拼读知识，根据听写写出单词、短语和句子。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify and use synonyms and antonyms.
items.zh: 识别并使用同义词和反义词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Recognize, identify and use subject, object, and possessive pronouns, i.e., I, me, my, they, them, orally, in written text, and in own writing.
items.zh: 在口头表达、阅读文本和自己的写作中识别并使用主格、宾格和所有格代词，即 I、me、my、they、them。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Recognize, identify, and use common and proper nouns, orally, in written text, and in own writing.
items.zh: 在口头表达、阅读文本和自己的写作中识别并使用普通名词和专有名词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Recognize, identify and use regular verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future tense orally, in written text, and in own writing.
items.zh: 在口头表达、阅读文本和自己的写作中识别并使用规则动词来表达过去、现在和将来时态。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Recognize, identify, and use adjectives orally, in written text, and in own writing.
items.zh: 在口头表达、阅读文本和自己的写作中识别并使用形容词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Recognize, identify, and use subjects and predicates, orally, in written text, and in own writing.
items.zh: 在口头表达、阅读文本和自己的写作中识别并使用主语和谓语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Recognize, identify, and use statements, questions, and exclamations orally, in written text, and in own writing.
items.zh: 在口头表达、阅读文本和自己的写作中识别并使用陈述句、疑问句和感叹句。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Parts of Speech and Sentence Structure
items.en: Produce and expand complete sentences orally and in shared writing exercises.
items.zh: 在口头表达和共同写作中说出并扩展完整的句子。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Capitalize the first word in a sentence, the pronoun I, and proper nouns (names and places,) months, days of the week.
items.zh: 句子首字母、代词 I、专有名词（人名和地名）、月份和一周中的各天要大写。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify and use end punctuation, including periods, question marks, and exclamation points.
items.zh: 识别并使用句末标点，包括句号、问号和感叹号。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use commas appropriately in greetings and closings of letters, dates, and items in a series.
items.zh: 在书信的称呼和结尾、日期以及并列项目中恰当使用逗号。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write a simple friendly letter.
items.zh: 写一封简单的友好书信。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use apostrophes to create contractions and indicate possession, i.e., cat’s meow.
items.zh: 使用撇号构成缩写和表示所有格，如 cat’s meow。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use quotation marks appropriately to designate direct speech.
items.zh: 恰当使用引号表示直接引语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: While the following works make up a strong core of literature, the content of language arts includes not only stories, fables, and poems, but also the well-practiced, operational knowledge of how written symbols represent sounds, and how those sounds and symbols convey meaning. Thus, the stories specified below are meant to complement, not to replace, materials designed to help students practice decoding and encoding skills (see above, II. Reading and III. Writing).
items.zh: 以下作品构成了文学的核心内容，但语言艺术的内容不仅包括故事、寓言和诗歌，还包括对书面符号如何代表声音、这些声音和符号如何传达意义的熟练运用的操作性知识。因此，下面列出的故事是为了补充、而不是取代帮助学生练习解码和编码技能的材料（见上文第二部分阅读与第三部分写作）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: The Boy at the Dike
items.zh: 《堤坝边的男孩》(The Boy at the Dike)

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: The Frog Prince
items.zh: 《青蛙王子》(The Frog Prince)

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Hansel and Gretel
items.zh: 《汉塞尔与格莱特》(Hansel and Gretel)

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: How Anansi Got Stories from the Sky God
items.zh: 《阿南西如何从天神那里得到故事》(How Anansi Got Stories from the Sky God)
items.work: How Anansi Got Stories from the Sky God

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: It Could Always Be Worse
items.zh: 《情况总能更糟》(It Could Always Be Worse)

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Jack and the Beanstalk
items.zh: 《杰克与魔豆》(Jack and the Beanstalk)

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: The Knee-High Man
items.zh: 《膝盖高的人》(The Knee-High Man)

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Medio Pollito

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: theater, stage, audience E. Sayings and Phrases Teachers: Every culture has phrases and proverbs that make no sense when carried over literally into another culture. For many students, this section may not be needed; they will have picked up these sayings by hearing them at home and among friends. But the sayings have been one of the categories most appreciated by teachers who work with students from home cultures that differ from the standard culture of literate American English. a.m. and p.m. An apple a day keeps the doctor away. Do unto others as you would have them do unto you. \[also in Kindergarten\] Fish out of water Hit the nail on the head. If at first you don’t succeed, try, try again. Land of Nod Let the cat out of the bag. The more the merrier Never leave till tomorrow what you can do today. Practice makes perfect. \[also in Kindergarten\] Sour grapes There’s no place like home. Wolf in sheep’s clothing Note: Students should learn terms relating to drama as part of their participation in a play appropriate for first graders—possibly a dramatized version of one of the stories listed above.

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Teachers: In first grade, students often study aspects of the world around them: the family, the school, the community, etc. The following guidelines are meant to broaden and complement that focus. The goal of studying selected topics in World History in first grade is to foster curiosity and the beginnings of understanding about the larger world outside the child’s locality, and about varied civilizations and ways of life. This can be done through a variety of means: story, drama, art, music, discussion, and more.
items.zh: 教师：一年级时，学生常常学习周围世界的各个方面：家庭、学校、社区等。以下指南旨在拓宽和补充这一重点。一年级学习世界历史中选定主题的目标，是培养孩子的好奇心，并初步理解其所在地区之外的广阔世界，以及各种文明和生活方式。这可以通过多种方式实现：故事、戏剧、艺术、音乐、讨论等等。

items.en: Since religion is a shaping force in the story of civilization, the Core Knowledge Sequence introduces students in the early grades to major world religions, beginning with a focus on geography and major symbols and figures. The purpose is not to explore matters of theology but to provide a basic vocabulary for understanding many events and ideas in history. The goal is to familiarize, not proselytize; to be descriptive, not prescriptive. The tone should be one of respect and balance: no religion should be disparaged by implying that it is a thing of the past. To the question, “Which one is true?” an appropriate response is: “People of different faiths believe different things to be true. The best people to guide you on this right now are your parents or someone at home.”
items.zh: 由于宗教是文明故事中一股塑造性的力量，核心知识序列在低年级向学生介绍世界主要宗教，首先从地理和主要象征与人物入手。目的不是探讨神学问题，而是提供理解历史上许多事件和思想的基本词汇。目标是让学生熟悉而非传教，是描述而非规定。语气应尊重且平衡：不应暗示任何宗教是过去的事物而贬低它。对于“哪一个才是真的？”这一问题，恰当的回答是：“不同信仰的人相信不同的事物为真。眼下最能引导你的是你的父母或家里的长辈。”

items.en: Teachers: The study of American history begins in grades K–2 with a brief overview of major events and figures, from the earliest days to recent times. A more in-depth, chronological study of American history begins again in Grade 3 and continues onward. The term “American” here generally, but not always, refers to the lands that became the United States. Other topics regarding North, Central, and South America may be found in the World History and Geography sections of this Sequence.

items.en: Pocahontas and Powhatan Archaeological discoveries in North and South America, dating back 14,000 to 15,000 years, show that humans arrived on the continent 1,000 or even 2,000 years earlier than previously believed. According to a new theory, known as “Kelp Highway,” massive ice sheets covering western North America retreated allowing the first humans to arrive on the continent not only by foot but by boat. They traveled down the Pacific shore and subsisted on abundant coastal resources. Note: Early exploration and the colonial years will be studied in greater depth and detail in Grade 3. First grade teachers should examine the Grade 3 guidelines to see how these topics build in the later grades.
items.zh: 波卡洪塔斯与波瓦坦 考古发现表明，北美和南美的考古遗迹可追溯到 14000 至 15000 年前，这说明人类到达该大陆的时间比此前认为的早 1000 甚至 2000 年。根据一种被称为“海藻高速路”的新理论，覆盖北美西部的巨大冰盖消退，使最早的人类不仅可以通过步行、还可以乘船到达该大陆。他们沿着太平洋海岸航行，依靠丰富的沿海资源生存。注：早期探索和殖民时期将在三年级进行更深入、详细的学习。一年级教师应查阅三年级指南，了解这些主题如何在更高年级逐步展开。

items.topic: From Colonies to Independence: The American Revolution
items.en: The American Revolution will be studied in greater depth and detail in Grade 4. First grade teachers should examine the fourth grade guidelines to see how these topics build in the later grade. It is recommended that first grade teachers focus on the topics specified here, and leave for fourth grade the more detailed study of the Revolution. In first grade, emphasize the story of the birth of our nation.

items.subject: Visual Arts
items.en: Teachers: In schools, lessons on the visual arts should illustrate important elements of making and appreciating art, and emphasize important artists, works of art, and artistic concepts. When appropriate, topics in the visual arts may be linked to topics in other disciplines. The following guidelines specify a variety of artwork in different media and from various cultures in order to expose students to a wide range of art and artists. While the list is robust, it may require teachers to narrow the selection in order to adequately address the works and related skills within an academic year.
items.zh: 教师：学校的视觉艺术课程应展示艺术创作与欣赏的重要元素，并重点介绍重要艺术家、艺术作品和艺术概念。在适当的时候，视觉艺术主题可以与其他学科主题相联系。以下指导方针列举了不同媒介和不同文化的多种艺术作品，以让学生接触广泛的艺术和艺术家。这份清单内容相当丰富，教师可能需要缩小选择范围，以便在一个学年内充分讲解这些作品及相关技能。

items.en: Introduce students to the terms we use to describe different kinds of paintings, discuss examples, and provide opportunities for students to create their own works in different genres. When you look at the specified works, ask the students about their first impressions— what they notice first, and what the picture makes them think of or feel. Go on to discuss lines, shapes, colors, and textures; details not obvious at first; why they think the artist chose to depict things in a certain way, etc.
items.zh: 向学生介绍用于描述不同绘画种类的术语，讨论范例，并让学生有机会创作不同体裁的作品。观看指定作品时，先问学生的第一印象——他们首先注意到什么，画面让他们想到或感受到什么。接着讨论线条、形状、色彩和肌理，一开始不明显之处，以及他们认为艺术家为何选择以某种方式描绘事物等。

items.subject: Music
items.en: Teachers: In schools, lessons on music should feature activities and works that illustrate important musical concepts and terms, and should introduce important composers and works. When appropriate, topics in music may be linked to topics in other disciplines. The following guidelines focus on content, not performance skills, though many concepts are best learned through active practice (singing, clapping rhythms, playing instruments, etc.).
items.zh: 教师：学校的音乐课应包含能够体现重要音乐概念和术语的活动与作品，并应介绍重要作曲家和作品。在适当的时候，音乐主题可以与其他学科主题相联系。以下指导方针侧重内容而非表演技能，不过许多概念最好通过积极实践来学习（唱歌、拍节奏、演奏乐器等）。

items.subject: Music
items.en: Through participation become familiar with basic elements of music (rhythm, melody, harmony, form, timbre, etc.).
items.zh: 通过参与，熟悉音乐的基本要素（节奏、旋律、和声、曲式、音色等）。

items.subject: Music
items.en: Recognize a steady beat; moving to a beat; play a steady beat; recognize accents.
items.zh: 识别稳定的节拍；随节拍律动；打出稳定节拍；识别重音。

items.subject: Music
items.en: Move responsively to music (marching, walking, hopping, swaying, etc.).
items.zh: 随着音乐做出相应动作（列队行进、走、单脚跳、摇摆等）。

items.subject: Music

items.subject: Music

items.subject: Music

items.zh: 区分响与轻（强与弱）。
