items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.
items.zh: 解决涉及角度、面积、表面积和体积的现实生活与数学问题。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle.
items.zh: 掌握圆的面积和周长公式。
details: Use to solve problems.
Give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.
items.zh: 利用补角、余角、对顶角和邻角的知识，在多步骤问题中列写并求解简单方程，求出图形中未知角的度数。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. p, q, and r are specific rational numbers Including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale. Freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology. Noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle. As in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.
items.zh: 解决涉及 p、q、r（均为特定有理数）的现实世界和数学问题。p、q、r 为特定有理数，包括根据按比例绘制的图计算实际长度和面积，以及按不同比例重新绘制比例图。徒手绘制、借助直尺和量角器，以及借助技术工具。注意判断给定条件何时确定唯一的三角形、不止一个三角形或没有三角形。例如直棱柱和直棱锥的平面截面。
details: area
volume

surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects (triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms) Know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.
items.zh: 使用随机抽样对总体进行推断。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population. • Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.
items.zh: 理解统计学可通过考察总体的样本来获取有关总体的信息。理解随机抽样往往能产生有代表性的样本，从而支持有效的推断。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. • Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.
items.zh: 利用随机样本的数据，对具有未知关注特征的总体进行推断。生成多个同样大小的样本（或模拟样本），以衡量估计或预测的变化。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
items.zh: 对两个总体进行非正式的比较推断。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities.
items.zh: 非正式地评估变异性相近的两个数值数据分布在视觉上的重叠程度。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
items.zh: 对来自随机样本的数值数据使用集中趋势度量和变异性度量，对两个总体进行非正式的比较推断。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.
items.zh: 研究随机过程，并建立、使用和评估概率模型。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. • Understand that larger numbers indicate greater likelihood.
items.zh: 理解随机事件的概率是介于 0 和 1 之间的数，表示事件发生的可能性。理解数值越大表示可能性越大。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event.
items.zh: 接近 0 的概率表示不太可能发生的事件。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: A probability around 1 2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely.
items.zh: 接近 1/2 的概率表示既非不太可能也非很可能发生的事件。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: A probability near 1 indicates a likely event.
items.zh: 接近 1 的概率表示很可能发生的事件。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Approximate the probability of a chance event.
items.zh: 近似求出随机事件的概率。
details: Collect data on the chance process that produces it.
Observe its long-run relative frequency.
Predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events.
items.zh: 建立概率模型并用它求事件发生的概率。
details: Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.
items.zh: 通过给所有结果赋予相等的概率来建立均匀概率模型，并用该模型确定事件的概率。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.
items.zh: 通过观察随机过程产生的数据中的频率，建立概率模型（可能不是均匀的）。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation. • Understand that the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs. • Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams.
items.zh: 使用有序列举、表格、树状图和模拟来求复合事件的概率。理解复合事件的概率是样本空间中该复合事件发生的结果所占的比例。用有序列举、表格和树状图等方法表示复合事件的样本空间。

items.subject: Mathematics
items.en: For an event described in everyday language, identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event. • Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events. Generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Measure the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability. If the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.
items.zh: 对于用日常语言描述的事件，指出样本空间中组成该事件的结果。设计并使用模拟来生成复合事件的频率。从样本对总体作出的概括只有在样本对该总体具有代表性时才有效。用变异性度量的倍数来表示中心之间的差异。如果吻合度不好，解释差异的可能来源。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Teachers: Effective instruction in science requires not only direct experience and observation but also book learning, which helps bring coherence and order to a student’s scientific knowledge. Only when topics are presented systematically and clearly can students make steady and secure progress in their scientific learning. The Science sequence for the middle school grades aims for more intensive and selective study of topics, a number of which were introduced in earlier grades. The Sequence continues the practice of studying topics from each of the major realms of science (physical, life, and earth science). Students are expected to do experiments and write reports on their findings.
items.zh: 教师须知：有效的科学教学不仅需要直接经验和观察，也需要书本学习，因为书本学习有助于使学生的科学知识连贯而有条理。只有系统、清晰地呈现主题，学生才能在科学学习上稳步而扎实地进步。中学阶段的科学知识序列旨在对主题进行更深入、有所侧重的研习，其中不少主题在更早的年级已经介绍过。该序列延续了从科学的各大领域（物理科学、生命科学和地球科学）研究主题的做法。学生应动手做实验，并撰写关于研究发现的报告。

items.subject: Science
items.en: A chemical reaction is indicated by changes in color, odor, or temperature.
items.zh: 化学反应可通过颜色、气味或温度的变化来识别。

items.subject: Science
items.en: In a chemical reaction, a new substance is form, called the product. The substances that interact in a chemical reaction are called reactants.
items.zh: 在化学反应中，会生成一种新物质，称为生成物。参与化学反应的物质称为反应物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The total number of atoms in the reactants is the same as the total number of atoms in the product. Matter is neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions—it is conserved.
items.zh: 反应物中的原子总数与生成物中的原子总数相同。化学反应中物质既不会凭空产生也不会消失——物质是守恒的。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Equations describe chemical reactions.
items.zh: 化学方程式描述化学反应。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Atom: consists of a nucleus and electrons.
items.zh: 原子：由原子核和电子组成。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Nucleus: consists of protons and neutrons, both of which are built from quarks.
items.zh: 原子核：由质子和中子组成，二者都由夸克构成。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Elements: substances consisting of only one kind of atom
items.zh: 元素：只由一种原子构成的物质

items.subject: Science
items.en: Compounds: made up of two or more atoms and have properties.
items.zh: 化合物：由两个或更多原子构成，并具有特定的性质。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Role of chemical bonds in formation of compounds
items.zh: 化学键在化合物形成中的作用

items.subject: Science
items.en: Role of electrons in formation of compounds
items.zh: 电子在化合物形成中的作用

items.subject: Science
items.en: Models can represent chemical compounds.
items.zh: 模型可以表示化合物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: When a chemical reaction occurs it will be accompanied by either absorbing energy or releasing energy. The energy may be in any of the following or any combination:
items.zh: 化学反应发生时，总会伴随吸收能量或释放能量。能量可能表现为以下任意一种或几种的组合：

items.subject: Science
items.en: Thermal energy
items.zh: 热能

items.subject: Science
items.en: Light
items.zh: 光

items.subject: Science
items.en: Sound
items.zh: 声

items.subject: Science
items.en: Motion
items.zh: 运动

items.subject: Science
items.en: In a chemical reaction, a new substance is form, called the product. The substances that interact in a chemical reaction are called reactants.
items.zh: 在化学反应中，会生成一种新物质，称为生成物。参与化学反应的物质称为反应物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Examples: fireworks give off heat, light, odor, and sound; exploding dynamite gives off sound and motion.
items.zh: 例如：烟花放出热、光、气味和声音；炸药爆炸发出声音并产生运动。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Energy in any chemical reaction is never created or destroyed, it just changes form.
items.zh: 任何化学反应中的能量都不会凭空产生或消失，只是改变了形式。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Some chemical reactions give off heat; they release thermal energy. These are exothermic.
items.zh: 有些化学反应放出热量，即释放热能，这类反应称为放热反应。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Some chemical reactions need heat to be input to occur; these are called endothermic.
items.zh: 有些化学反应需要输入热量才能发生，这类反应称为吸热反应。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The energy released by a chemical reaction can be used to create useful products such as hand warmers, flameless heaters, and heating up food.
items.zh: 化学反应释放的能量可用于制造有用的产品，如暖手宝、无焰加热器，以及加热食物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Chemical reactions may need thermal energy to occur; example. a spark needed to ignite gasoline.
items.zh: 化学反应可能需要热能才能发生；例如，点燃汽油需要火花。

items.subject: Science
items.en: A catalyst is something that reduces the amount of energy needed for a chemical reaction to occur.
items.zh: 催化剂是能降低化学反应发生所需能量的物质。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The human body takes in food and breaks down the food by the process of digestion.
items.zh: 人体摄入食物，并通过消化过程将食物分解。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Digestion allows carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and vitamins to become available to all the cells in the body.
items.zh: 消化使碳水化合物、蛋白质、脂肪和维生素能够被全身所有细胞利用。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Disruption of the processes of digestion and cell respiration can lead to disorders of human health.
items.zh: 消化和细胞呼吸过程受到干扰会导致人体健康失调。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Humans are omnivores and must eat plants or other animals to survive.
items.zh: 人类是杂食动物，必须吃植物或其他动物才能生存。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Human health requires food and other substances such as vitamins and minerals.
items.zh: 人体健康需要食物以及维生素和矿物质等其他物质。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Balanced diet, e.g. the food pyramid or “MyPlate,” includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals.
items.zh: 均衡饮食，例如食物金字塔或“我的餐盘”（MyPlate），包括碳水化合物、蛋白质、脂肪、维生素和矿物质。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Humans must get vitamins from external sources.
items.zh: 人类必须从外部来源获取维生素。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Energy for most life on earth comes from the sun.
items.zh: 地球上大多数生命所需的能量来自太阳。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Sunlight and the process of photosynthesis
items.zh: 阳光与光合作用过程

items.subject: Science
items.en: Glucose is the major source of chemical energy for living things.
items.zh: 葡萄糖是生物体化学能量的主要来源。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Food is both what we eat and the chemical substances cells need to perform chemical reactions.
items.zh: 食物既是我们吃的东西，也是细胞进行化学反应所需的化学物质。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The three classes of chemicals that make up food are carbohydrates, proteins, and fats (lipids).
items.zh: 构成食物的三大类化学物质是碳水化合物、蛋白质和脂肪（脂类）。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen (plus many others in lesser amounts) are the main constituents of cell chemistry.
items.zh: 碳、氢、氧（以及含量较少的许多其他元素）是细胞化学的主要组成成分。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Cellular respiration breaks down the sugar glucose and uses released chemical energy to allow all chemical reactions in the cell.
items.zh: 细胞呼吸分解葡萄糖，并利用释放出的化学能来支持细胞内的所有化学反应。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Only plants photosynthesize, but all living things (including plants) have cellular respiration.
items.zh: 只有植物能进行光合作用，但所有生物（包括植物）都有细胞呼吸。

items.subject: Science
items.en: While most living things use oxygen for cellular respiration, some do not.
items.zh: 虽然大多数生物利用氧气进行细胞呼吸，但有些生物不需要氧气。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Animals must eat organic compounds from plants or other animals for energy.
items.zh: 动物必须摄入来自植物或其他动物的有机物以获取能量。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Humans need oxygen for most types of cellular respiration.
items.zh: 人体进行大多数类型的细胞呼吸都需要氧气。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Oxygen is transported from the lungs to the cells through hemoglobin in the blood.
items.zh: 氧气通过血液中的血红蛋白从肺部输送到细胞。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The interdependence and balance between plant and animal life is bound to the processes of photosynthesis and respiration.
items.zh: 动植物生命之间的相互依存与平衡与光合作用和呼吸作用的过程紧密相连。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The energy for most life comes from the sun.
items.zh: 大多数生命所需的能量来自太阳。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Sunlight strikes the chemical chlorophyll, which is found in the leaf and stem tissues of plants.
items.zh: 阳光照射到叶绿素这种化学物质上，叶绿素存在于植物的叶片和茎部组织中。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Sunlight energy is transformed into chemical energy by plant cells by a complex set of reactions called photosynthesis.
items.zh: 植物细胞通过一系列复杂的反应将阳光能量转化为化学能，这一过程称为光合作用。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The result of photosynthesis is the formation of the simple sugar glucose.
items.zh: 光合作用的结果是生成一种简单的糖——葡萄糖。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Glucose is the chemical food of life on earth.
items.zh: 葡萄糖是地球上生命的化学养料。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Glucose produced by plants is the food of all living things.
items.zh: 植物产生的葡萄糖是所有生物的食物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Matter (glucose, food) flows from plants to all other organisms in the ecosystem in feeding chains.
items.zh: 物质（葡萄糖、食物）通过食物链从植物流向生态系统中的所有其他生物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: All the interacting food chains make up the food web of an ecosystem.
items.zh: 所有相互交错的食物链构成一个生态系统的食物网。

items.subject: Science
items.en: About 10% of the food energy flows to the next level in food chain.
items.zh: 大约 10% 的食物能量流向食物链的下一级。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Bacteria and fungi recycle chemical substances and return organic matter to an ecosystem using carbon, oxygen, and nitrogen cycles.
items.zh: 细菌和真菌通过碳、氧和氮循环回收化学物质，并将有机物归还给生态系统。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Cycles of matter occur throughout all of earth’s spheres, including the atmosphere, biosphere, geosphere, and hydrosphere.
items.zh: 物质循环发生在地球的所有圈层中，包括大气圈、生物圈、岩石圈和水圈。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Cycles of matter are called biogeochemical sice they involve both abiotic and biotic elements of the earth.
items.zh: 物质循环被称为生物地球化学循环，因为它们涉及地球的非生物和生物要素。

items.subject: Science
items.en: The carbon, oxygen, and phosphorus cycles are important biogeochemical cycles.
items.zh: 碳循环、氧循环和磷循环是重要的生物地球化学循环。

items.subject: Science
items.en: An ecosystem is all the biotic and abiotic factors that make up a defined area.
items.zh: 生态系统是构成一个特定区域的所有生物因素和非生物因素。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Abiotic: temperature, wind, precipitation, soil type, weather, water conditions
items.zh: 非生物因素：温度、风、降水、土壤类型、天气、水文条件

items.subject: Science
items.en: Biotic: all the living organisms in an area
items.zh: 生物因素：某一区域内的所有生物

items.subject: Science
items.en: Range of size of ecosystems
items.zh: 生态系统大小的分布范围

items.subject: Science
items.en: An ecosystem consists of individual organisms, of populations made up of member of the same species, and of all other populations of all the species in the area.
items.zh: 生态系统由个体生物、由同种成员组成的种群，以及该区域内所有物种的其他种群构成。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Limited resources promote competition among individuals and species.
items.zh: 有限的资源促使个体之间和物种之间产生竞争。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Species can interact symbiotically by mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism.
items.zh: 物种之间可通过互利共生、共栖和寄生等方式形成共生关系。

items.subject: Science
items.en: All ecosystems, regardless of size or nature, consist of interactions between producers and consumers and between predators and prey.
items.zh: 所有生态系统，无论大小或性质如何，都由生产者与消费者之间以及捕食者与被捕食者之间的相互作用构成。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Ecosystems vary widely in type, but all involve similar interaction of biotic and abiotic factors.
items.zh: 生态系统类型差异很大，但都涉及生物因素与非生物因素的类似相互作用。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Biotic and abiotic aspects of an ecosystem can change.
items.zh: 生态系统的生物和非生物方面都可能发生变化。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Ecosystem disruptions include: the immigration or emigration of new species, the arrival of prey organisms, long-term changes in precipitation, disasters such as flood or fire.
items.zh: 生态系统的扰动包括：新物种的迁入或迁出、猎物种群的到来、降水的长期变化，以及洪水或火灾等灾害。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Poor agricultural practices can damage ecosystems. Examples are the destruction of rain forests for the production of palm oil and t monoculture farming that harm native prairies.
items.zh: 不良的农业做法会破坏生态系统。例如为生产棕榈油而毁坏雨林，以及危害原生草原的单一作物种植。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Individuals and species may find the changes in conditions favorable or unfavorable.
items.zh: 个体和物种可能会发现环境的变化对自己有利或不利。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Humans can preserve an ecosystem’s structure, e.g. by wroking to preserve biodiversity or eliminate invasive species.
items.zh: 人类可以保护生态系统的结构，例如努力保护生物多样性或清除入侵物种。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Humans use the energy inherent in natural resources to live.
items.zh: 人类利用自然资源中蕴含的能量来生存。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Renewable resources
items.zh: 可再生资源

items.subject: Science
items.en: Sunlight — solar panels and solar heating devices
items.zh: 阳光——太阳能电池板和太阳能加热装置

items.subject: Science
items.en: Wind — windmills
items.zh: 风——风车

items.subject: Science
items.en: Hydroelectric power uses the gravitational effect on water.
items.zh: 水力发电利用水所受的重力作用。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Geothermal power uses thermal energy from Earth’s interior.
items.zh: 地热能利用地球内部的热能。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Tidal power uses the movement of oceanic tides.
items.zh: 潮汐能利用海洋潮汐的运动。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Biofuels use raw materials, such as forest resources, and are renewable if produced sustainably.
items.zh: 生物燃料使用森林资源等原材料，如果以可持续方式生产，就是可再生的。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Nonrenewable resources:
items.zh: 不可再生资源：

items.subject: Science
items.en: Fossil fuels such as oil, natural gas, and coal
items.zh: 化石燃料，如石油、天然气和煤

items.subject: Science
items.en: Nuclear power from uranium
items.zh: 来自铀的核能

items.subject: Science
items.en: Nuclear power plants—monitored for safety and accidents such as Three Mile Island and Chernobyl
items.zh: 核电站——需进行安全监控，以及三里岛和切尔诺贝利等事故

items.subject: Science
items.en: The use of natural resources, while necessary for modern life, can have undesired environmental effects.
items.zh: 自然资源的利用虽然是现代生活所必需的，但也可能产生不良的环境影响。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Fossil fuels — air pollution, including smog and greenhouse gases, causing atmospheric warming
items.zh: 化石燃料——造成空气污染，包括烟雾和温室气体，导致大气变暖

items.subject: Science
items.en: Nuclear power generates radioactive waste.
items.zh: 核能会产生放射性废物。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Wind turbines can be noisy and may affect bird life.
items.zh: 风力涡轮机可能噪音较大，并可能影响鸟类。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Human ingenuity and its uses to create a healthy environment.
items.zh: 人类的聪明才智及其在创造健康环境中的应用。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Scientific data and effective communication can be used to make informed decisions about the environment.
items.zh: 科学数据和有效沟通可用于就环境问题作出明智的决策。

items.subject: Science
items.en: Charles Darwin— the theory of evolution by natural selection
items.zh: 查尔斯·达尔文——自然选择进化论

items.subject: Science
items.en: Antoine Lavoisier—the process of oxidation
items.zh: 安托万·拉瓦锡——氧化过程

items.subject: Science
items.en: Lise Meitner—helped establish the process of controlled nuclear fission
items.zh: 莉泽·迈特纳——帮助确立了可控核裂变的过程

items.subject: Science
items.en: Dmitri Mendeleev: first widely accepted periodic table
items.zh: 德米特里·门捷列夫：提出首个被广泛接受的元素周期表

items.subject: Science
items.en: Francis Crick, James Watson, Severo Ochoa, Barbara McClintock, etc., elucidated the hereditary workings of the cell
items.zh: 弗朗西斯·克里克、詹姆斯·沃森、塞韦罗·奥乔亚、芭芭拉·麦克林托克等阐明了细胞的遗传机制

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Actively participate in discussions about a variety of Grade 8 topics, ideas, and texts in a variety of settings, including partners, small and large groups, and teacher-led groups.
items.zh: 积极参与关于八年级各种主题、观点和课文的讨论，讨论形式多样，包括两人搭档、小组和大组以及教师带领的小组。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Prepare for discussions in advance, including researching the topic and organizing information for the discussion. Draw on preparations during the discussion to analyze ideas and explore the topic further.
items.zh: 提前为讨论做准备，包括研究主题和整理讨论所需信息；在讨论中运用这些准备来分析观点并进一步探讨主题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Manage goals and deadlines, and define specific roles appropriate to a discussion.
items.zh: 管理目标和完成期限，并明确适合讨论的具体角色分工。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Follow rules for productive social engagement among peers; follow decision-making protocols (e.g., rubrics or principles) that help build effective social skills related to public discussions.
items.zh: 遵守同伴间富有成效的社交互动规则；遵循有助于培养公共讨论所需有效社交技能的决策规程（如评分标准或原则）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Ask relevant questions to clarify conversations and ideas and to build upon remarks made by others.
items.zh: 提出相关问题，以澄清谈话和想法，并在他人发言的基础上进一步展开。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use details to elaborate and comment on a topic, text, or issue being discussed; add insight to discussions or move discussions forward.
items.zh: 运用细节对所讨论的主题、文本或问题进行阐述和评论；为讨论增添见解或推动讨论深入。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Integrate the ideas, evidence, and viewpoints of multiple speakers before responding or posing questions during a discussion.
items.zh: 在讨论中作出回应或提问之前，先综合多位发言者的观点、论据和看法。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Craft responses to questions, as well as comments, so that ideas, insights, observations, and evidence are relevant to the topic or issue being discussed.
items.zh: 精心组织对问题的回答和评论，使观点、见解、观察和论据都与所讨论的主题或问题相关。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate the ability to defend one’s own point of view when presented with new information; adjust one’s own point of view, if necessary, when presented with new evidence during a discussion.
items.zh: 展现出在面对新信息时捍卫自己观点的能力；讨论中若出现新证据，必要时调整自己的观点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Interpret information from an array of media formats, such as visual (paintings, pictures, and animations), quantitative (graphs, charts, and diagrams), videos, and recordings.
items.zh: 解读多种媒体形式呈现的信息，如视觉类（绘画、图片和动画）、数据类（曲线图、图表和示意图）、视频以及录音。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Explain how information from media formats reflects, enhances, or is otherwise suitable for the discussion, issue, or topic at hand.
items.zh: 说明媒体形式的信息如何反映、增强或以其他方式适用于当前的讨论、问题或主题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify and interpret the purposes, motives, or intentions of an array of information from media formats, such as political, commercial, and social agendas.
items.zh: 识别并解读各类媒体信息背后的目的、动机或意图，如政治、商业和社会方面的图谋。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Explain a speaker’s argument, distinguishing the claims, evidence, and reasons speakers give and whether the claims are adequately supported.
items.zh: 解释说话者的论点，区分其提出的主张、证据和理由，并判断这些主张是否得到充分支持。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Evaluate the overall quality of the reasoning used in an argument and the relevancy of the evidence provided; identify and explain when and why particular evidence may be unnecessary, unrelated, or inappropriate.
items.zh: 评估论证中推理的整体质量以及所提供证据的相关性；识别并说明某些证据在何时、为何可能是不必要的、无关的或不恰当的。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Give a presentation about a topic or text, tell a story, or orally relate a personal experience in a logical and organized manner, including relevant descriptions, details, and facts that support main ideas or themes.
items.zh: 以条理清晰、逻辑严密的方式就某一主题或文本作报告、讲故事或口头讲述个人经历，包括支持主要观点或主题的相关描述、细节和事实。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Orally present a claim-based argument supported by evidence, curated details, and solid reasoning that demonstrates a focused emphasis on the essential points.
items.zh: 口头陈述以主张为核心的论证，用证据、精选细节和扎实的推理加以支撑，突出要点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Speak clearly at an understandable volume and pace; maintain eye contact.
items.zh: 以清晰、易于理解的音量和语速讲话；保持眼神交流。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Support claims in presentations by adding evidence from relevant multimedia such as displays, images, videos, graphics, music, and recordings.
items.zh: 在陈述中通过加入相关多媒体（如展品、图片、视频、图形、音乐和录音）的证据来支撑主张。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use relevant multimedia to enhance presentations and capture viewers’/listeners’ attention.
items.zh: 运用相关多媒体增强陈述效果，吸引观众／听众的注意力。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use information from several multimedia sources, synthesizing it to explain, crystalize, elaborate, or elucidate information for viewers/listeners.
items.zh: 运用多个多媒体来源的信息，加以综合，为观众／听众进行解释、提炼、详述或阐明。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Switch between formal and informal English as appropriate to the situation or task; adapt speech to a variety of contexts.
items.zh: 根据情境或任务在正式与非正式英语之间切换；使言语适应各种语境。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Show proficiency when using formal English, such as standard pronunciation when giving speeches or speaking to large groups and in formal circumstances, such as a job interview.
items.zh: 在使用正式英语时表现出熟练能力，例如在演讲、面对大群人讲话或在求职面试等正式场合使用标准发音。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Independently and proficiently read and comprehend longer works of fiction (stories, plays, and poems) and literary nonfiction written at the high end of grades 6 through 8.
items.zh: 独立且熟练地阅读并理解难度达到6至8年级上限的较长虚构作品（故事、戏剧和诗歌）以及文学性非虚构作品。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify and utilize the most appropriate supporting evidence from texts when explaining them or making inferences.
items.zh: 在解说课文或进行推断时，找出并运用文本中最恰当的支持性证据。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Quote or cite accurately from texts when using evidence to explain them or make inferences.
items.zh: 用证据解说文本或进行推断时，准确引用或标注文本出处。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify the central ideas or themes in a text and explain how they develop.
items.zh: 识别文本的中心思想或主题，并解释其如何展开。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand how the component parts in literary works or supporting ideas in informational texts build themes or big ideas.
items.zh: 理解文学作品中的组成部分或说明性文本中的支撑观点如何构建主题或核心思想。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Summarize texts objectively.
items.zh: 客观地概括文本。
items.section: Grasping Specific Details and Key Ideas
items.section_zh: 把握具体细节与核心观点

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a literary or nonfiction text, including Tier 2 academic vocabulary and Tier 3 subject-area vocabulary.
items.zh: 确定文学或非虚构文本中词语和短语的含义，包括二级学术词汇和三级学科词汇。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Consider the impact of word choices on meaning and tone.
items.zh: 考虑用词选择对意义和语气的影响。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Analyze the structures of several texts to determine how structures create meaning and influence style; then, compare and contrast the texts, considering the impact on meaning and style each structure has.
items.zh: 分析若干文本的结构，确定结构如何创造意义并影响风格；然后比较和对照这些文本，考量每种结构对意义和风格的影响。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Evaluate in detail how sentences cooperate in paragraphs to build and organize key ideas, key concepts, and key details (versus extraneous information) and, in turn, how paragraphs cooperate to build ideas and organize information in texts.
items.zh: 详细评估句子如何在段落中配合以构建和组织核心观点、关键概念和关键细节（而非无关信息），进而评估段落如何在文本中配合以构建观点和组织信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Explore the advantages and disadvantages of various media, such as books or other printed materials, videos, digital photography, or recordings, to convey ideas or explore a topic.
items.zh: 探究各种媒介（如书籍或其他印刷材料、视频、数码摄影或录音）在传达思想或探讨主题方面的优缺点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Compare and contrast different texts with the same topic, themes, or genre.
items.zh: 比较和对比主题、题材或体裁相同的不同文本。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Analyze analogies, allusions to other texts, and figurative language, such as metaphors and similes, to determine meaning.
items.zh: 分析类比、对其他文本的典故引用以及比喻性语言（如隐喻和明喻），以确定其含义。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Determine connotative meanings of words in literary texts.
items.zh: 确定文学文本中词语的引申义（内涵义）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Consider the function of dialogue in stories and plays, focusing on how it moves a story forward, reveals aspects of a character’s personality, causes characters to take action, influences how characters interact with each other, or otherwise affects the events of the plot.
items.zh: 思考对话在故事和戏剧中的作用，重点分析它如何推动情节发展、揭示人物性格、促使人物采取行动、影响人物之间的互动，或以其他方式影响情节事件。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Compare and contrast a script or written version of a story to a filmed version or live performance, analyzing the extent of the departures from the original or faithfulness to it and the effectiveness of the artistic choices made by the director or actors.
items.zh: 将故事的剧本或文字版本与拍成电影的版本或现场演出进行比较和对照，分析其对原作的偏离或忠实程度，以及导演或演员所作艺术选择的效果。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Explore how authors use dramatic irony to
items.zh: 探究作者如何运用戏剧性反讽来

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: create a different point of view for the audience or reader than the point of view of the characters in a story or drama.
items.zh: 为观众或读者营造不同于故事或戏剧中人物视角的另一种视角。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: create differing points of view and levels of awareness among characters in the same story or drama.
items.zh: 在同一故事或戏剧中的人物之间营造不同的视角和认知程度。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: involve or affect the reader or audience by creating differing points of view and levels of awareness for characters in the same story or drama.
items.zh: 通过为同一故事或戏剧中的人物设置不同的视角和认知程度，使读者或观众产生代入感或受到影响。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: build suspense or humor by contrasting points of view and levels of awareness among characters or between the reader/audience and the characters in a story or drama.
items.zh: 通过对比人物之间、或读者／观众与人物之间的视角和认知程度，营造悬念或幽默。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Analyze archetypal plot patterns, themes, and character types and other literary devices and allusions from foundational literary works used in modern fiction.
items.zh: 分析现代小说中所借鉴的经典文学作品里的原型情节模式、主题、人物类型以及其他文学手法和典故。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Compare modern fiction with the sources it draws from for inspiration, such as traditional stories, epic poetry, mythology, and religious works (e.g., the Bible), with a focused discussion on how stories from the past are modernized.
items.zh: 将现代小说与其汲取灵感的来源（如传统故事、史诗、神话和宗教作品，例如《圣经》）进行比较，重点讨论古老故事如何被现代化改写。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Effectively summarize all types of informational texts.
items.zh: 有效地概括各类信息类文本。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Analyze technical meanings, analogies, and allusions to other texts to determine meaning.
items.zh: 分析术语含义、类比以及对其他文本的典故引用，以确定词义。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and explain the relationships and interactions between two or more individuals, events, or ideas in a text and how the author integrates them.
items.zh: 理解并解释文本中两个或更多人物、事件或观点之间的关系与相互作用，以及作者如何将它们整合起来。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify the structure of a text at the sentence and paragraph level and how it helps develop and hone big ideas and key concepts.
items.zh: 识别文本在句子和段落层面上的结构，以及该结构如何帮助展开和精炼核心思想与关键概念。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify an author’s point of view and purpose in a text.
items.zh: 识别作者在文本中的观点和写作目的。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Explain how an author distinguishes their own point of view from that of others in a text, focusing on how an author responds to evidence and/or viewpoints that conflict.
items.zh: 说明作者如何在文本中区分自己的观点与他人的观点，重点分析作者如何应对相互冲突的证据和／或观点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of various mediums’ (print, digital, video, and multimedia) ability to relate information to the reader or viewer about a particular topic or idea.
items.zh: 分析各种媒介（印刷、数字、视频和多媒体）在向读者或观众传达特定主题或观点信息方面的优缺点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Explain how an author supports arguments in a text by giving reasons (opinions) and evidence, such as facts, examples, and expert opinions from reliable sources.
items.zh: 说明作者如何通过给出理由（看法）和证据（如事实、实例以及来自可靠来源的专家意见）来支撑文本中的论证。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Distinguish between claims that are supported and those that are not.
items.zh: 区分有证据支持的主张和没有证据支持的主张。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Examine the overall soundness of the reasoning in an argument and the quality of the evidence supporting it; identify unnecessary, unrelated, or inappropriate evidence.
items.zh: 审视论证中推理的整体可靠性以及支持它的证据质量；找出不必要、不相关或不恰当的证据。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Compare and contrast texts containing conflicting information or arguments, identifying the conflict precisely and distinguishing whether the conflicting information is a matter of disparate facts, interpretations, or opinion/viewpoint.
items.zh: 比较和对照含有相互冲突信息或论证的文本，准确指出冲突所在，并区分冲突信息是源于事实分歧、解读差异还是观点／看法不同。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Students should be given opportunities to compose narratives, persuasive essays, and expository writing. Students should examine their work with attention to unity, coherence, and emphasis. Narratives should present a logical sequence of events, and include concrete details. Persuasive pieces should incorporate credible sources, support claims, and consider counter arguments. Expository essays should have a main point and stick to it, and have a coherent structure, typically following the pattern of introduction, body, and conclusion. Paragraphs should have a unified focus, be developed with evidence and examples, and have transitions between them. Essays should have appropriate tone and diction, as well as correct spelling and grammar in their final form. Standards for writing apply across the disciplines.
items.zh: 应给学生提供写作记叙文、议论文和说明文的机会。学生应审视自己的作品，注意统一性、连贯性和重点突出。记叙文应按逻辑顺序呈现事件，并包含具体细节。议论文应引用可信来源、支撑主张并考虑反驳论点。说明文应有明确的中心并紧扣中心，结构连贯，通常遵循开头、正文、结尾的模式。各段落应焦点统一，用证据和事例展开，段落之间有过渡。文章应有恰当的语气和措辞，定稿时拼写和语法正确。写作标准适用于各个学科。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose, and Task
items.en: Write routinely, clearly, and coherently, completing both short-term and long-term assignments focused on a range of different tasks, purposes, and audiences.
items.zh: 定期、清晰且连贯地写作，完成短期和长期作业，这些作业围绕各种不同的任务、目的和读者对象展开。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose, and Task
items.en: Strengthen existing writing skills (sentences, paragraphs, transitions, introductions, and conclusions) by applying them to longer and genre-specific writing assignments.
items.zh: 通过将这些技能应用于更长、更具体裁特点的写作任务，巩固已有的写作技能（句子、段落、过渡、开头和结尾）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose, and Task
items.en: Use the steps of the writing process to develop and strengthen writing: plan, draft, share, evaluate, revise, edit, and publish.
items.zh: 运用写作过程的各个步骤来发展和强化写作能力：计划、起草、分享、评价、修订、编辑和发表。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose, and Task
items.en: Use conventional language standards when editing.
items.zh: 编辑时遵循规范的语言标准。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose, and Task
items.en: Maintain a consistent style and tone appropriate to the genre of writing and audience.
items.zh: 保持与写作体裁和读者对象相适应的统一风格和语气。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose, and Task
items.en: Use keyboards, tablets, the Internet, and other technologies to produce and publish writing and collaborate and communicate with others.
items.zh: 使用键盘、平板电脑、互联网及其他技术来创作和发布作品，并与他人协作和交流。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Reflect Audience, Purpose, and Task
items.en: Use the Internet to research and cite sources.
items.zh: 利用互联网进行研究并引用来源。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Analyze literature in writing: trace archetypal plot patterns, character types, and themes in modern fiction and compare and contrast them with the sources they draw on, such as epic poetry, the Bible and other religious works, traditional stories, and myths.
items.zh: 以书面形式分析文学作品：追溯现代小说中的原型情节模式、人物类型和主题，并将其与所借鉴的来源（如史诗、《圣经》及其他宗教作品、传统故事和神话）进行比较和对照。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Discuss and analyze, in writing, how authors modernize the archetypal source material they use for inspiration.
items.zh: 以书面形式讨论并分析作者如何将其汲取灵感的原型素材现代化。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Use literary elements as evidence for analyzing literature to strengthen reflection and analysis skills.
items.zh: 运用文学要素作为分析文学作品的证据，以增强思考和分析能力。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Describe an analysis of informational texts in writing:
items.zh: 以书面形式描述对说明性文本的分析：

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Explain how authors make and support their points or claims with reasons and factual evidence.
items.zh: 解释作者如何提出观点或主张，并用理由和事实证据加以支持。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Explain how specific pieces of evidence support specific claims.
items.zh: 解释具体的证据如何支持具体的主张。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Discuss, in writing, whether the reasoning and evidence in an argument are valid and adequate.
items.zh: 以书面形式讨论论证中的推理和证据是否有效且充分。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Discuss, in writing, why evidence is invalid (e.g., unnecessary, unrelated, or inappropriate).
items.zh: 以书面形式讨论证据为何无效（例如不必要、不相关或不恰当）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.subtopic: Writing to Analyze and Understand Text
items.en: Use details and facts as evidence for analyzing informational texts to strengthen research and analysis skills.
items.zh: 将细节和事实作为分析信息类文本的证据，以增强研究和分析能力。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Conduct short research projects focused on answering a specific research question, especially one posed by the student.
items.zh: 开展小型研究项目，聚焦于回答某个具体的研究问题，尤其是学生自己提出的问题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Gather relevant information from several different print and digital sources and use it to support research.
items.zh: 从多种不同的纸质和数字来源收集相关信息，并用于支持研究。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Adjust the research question as appropriate throughout the information-gathering process.
items.zh: 在信息收集过程中酌情调整研究问题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use the information-gathering process to pose related questions and explore additional topics and avenues of inquiry requiring further research.
items.zh: 利用信息收集过程提出相关问题，并探索需要进一步研究的其他主题和探究途径。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Determine the credibility of information gathered from print and digital sources.
items.zh: 判断从纸质和数字来源收集的信息的可信度。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Accurately quote or paraphrase from sources without plagiarizing.
items.zh: 准确地引用或转述来源内容，避免抄袭。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Practice honing keywords and key phrases to produce more effective online searches.
items.zh: 练习打磨关键词和关键短语，以进行更有效的在线搜索。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Cite sources and provide a basic bibliography.
items.zh: 标注引用来源，并提供基本的参考文献书目。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Produce narrative pieces that reflect real-life or imagined experiences.
items.zh: 写出反映真实生活或想象经历的记叙文。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Introduce a narrator, a situation, and characters, and develop them through dialogue, pacing, and exposition, including actions, thoughts, feelings, and reactions to events in the plot.
items.zh: 介绍叙述者、情境和人物，并通过对话、节奏和说明加以展开，包括动作、思想、情感以及对情节中事件的反应。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Organize a well-structured logical or natural sequence of plot events following from the situation, using time-order and transitional words, phrases, and clauses to indicate and manage the event order.
items.zh: 围绕情境组织结构良好、符合逻辑或自然的情节事件顺序，使用时间顺序词以及过渡词、短语和从句来标示和掌控事件顺序。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Incorporate shifts in time and multiple settings, interconnecting them with events and experiences that move character development forward.
items.zh: 融入时间转换和多个场景，并通过推动人物发展的事件和经历将它们联系起来。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Include concrete and sensory details to make writing vivid and precise; convey a sense of experiences and/or the sensations that accompany experiences.
items.zh: 加入具体和感官细节，使写作生动准确；传达体验感及伴随体验的感受。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Provide a sense of closure that follows logically or artfully from the situation, character responses, and sequence of events.
items.zh: 给出合乎逻辑或巧妙的结尾，与情境、人物反应和事件顺序相呼应。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write reports and other types of informational texts that clearly focus ideas and information.
items.zh: 撰写报告和其他类型的信息类文本，清晰地聚焦观点和信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Introduce a topic with information organized in related sections or paragraphs and developed with well-curated facts, definitions, quotations, examples, and details.
items.zh: 引入一个主题，信息按相关部分或段落组织，并用精选的事实、定义、引文、事例和细节加以展开。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Organize ideas, concepts, and information using broad categories.
items.zh: 用大类来组织观点、概念和信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Group related information logically and incorporate formatting features, such as headings, graphics, charts, and other multimedia.
items.zh: 按逻辑将相关信息分组，并加入标题、图形、图表等格式元素。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Include visual elements such as photos, drawings, or diagrams to help explain or present ideas or information when appropriate.
items.zh: 在适当的时候加入照片、图画或图表等视觉要素，以帮助解释或呈现观点和信息。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use a variety of transitions to connect ideas and concepts from distinct categories and to clarify relationships; use transitions to create an overall sense of cohesion.
items.zh: 使用多种过渡手段连接不同类别的观点和概念并厘清关系；运用过渡使文章具有整体连贯感。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Establish and maintain a formal style.
items.zh: 建立并保持正式的文体风格。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use Tier 2 and/or Tier 3 domain-specific vocabulary to explain or elaborate topics.
items.zh: 使用二级和/或三级学科词汇来解释或详述主题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write a conclusion that wraps up ideas in the text.
items.zh: 写出总结全文观点的结论。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write persuasive essays with well-defined theses and arguments that use clear reasons, examples, and relevant evidence to support claims.
items.zh: 撰写论点明确的说服性文章，用清晰的理由、实例和相关证据支持主张。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Follow through with an organizational structure that supports the purpose of the text, grouping ideas, reasons, counterclaims, and evidence in a logical way.
items.zh: 采用有助于实现写作目的的结构，按逻辑组织观点、理由、反驳论点和证据。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate the use of logical reasoning to support claims throughout the essay.
items.zh: 在整篇文章中运用逻辑推理来支持主张。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Demonstrate a clear understanding of the topic and argument.
items.zh: 表现出对主题和论证的清晰理解。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Anticipate and answer counterarguments.
items.zh: 预判并回应反面论点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Distinguish evidence from opinion and claims from counterclaims.
items.zh: 区分证据与看法、主张与反驳论点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use linking words, phrases, and clauses to connect opinions with reasons and evidence, distinguish a counterclaim, and create an overall sense of cohesion.
items.zh: 使用连接词、短语和从句将看法与理由和证据联系起来，标明反驳论点，并使文章具有整体连贯感。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Establish and maintain a formal style and reasonable tone.
items.zh: 建立并保持正式的文体和合理的语气。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Identify and use accurate, credible sources.
items.zh: 识别并使用准确、可信的来源。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Write a conclusion that effectively and logically wraps up the argument.
items.zh: 写出有效且合乎逻辑地收束论证的结论。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use knowledge of language conventions when reading, writing, speaking, and listening.
items.zh: 在阅读、写作、口语和倾听中运用语言规范知识。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use active and passive verbs and voice to portray the conditional and subjunctive mood—that is, states and actions tied to hypothetical scenarios (e.g., if . . . then, wish, would) of varying degrees of possibility.
items.zh: 使用主动和被动的动词及语态来表现条件语气和虚拟语气，即与不同可能性程度的假设情境（例如“如果……那么”、希望、会）相联系的状态和动作。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use the conditional and subjunctive mood to create desired effects, express uncertainty, or communicate the fantastical.
items.zh: 运用条件语气和虚拟语气来营造预期效果、表达不确定性或传达奇幻的想象。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use the conditional and subjunctive mood to emphasize both the person hypothesizing and the ideas being hypothesized.
items.zh: 运用条件语气和虚拟语气来强调进行假设的人以及被假设的观点。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Apply known spelling strategies when writing.
items.zh: 写作时运用已知的拼写策略。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Apply known morphology skills (roots, prefixes, suffixes, and spelling changes) to correctly spell words.
items.zh: 运用已掌握的构词法知识（词根、前缀、后缀和拼写变化）正确拼写单词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Continue work with spelling, with special attention to commonly misspelled words. C. Grammar Teachers: Students should have a working understanding of the following terms and be able to use them to discuss and analyze writing.
items.zh: 继续学习拼写，特别关注常见拼写错误词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and apply the basic rules of English grammar and conventions when writing or speaking.
items.zh: 在写作或口语中理解并运用英语语法和语言规范的基本规则。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Know the function of verbals generally and how they are used in sentences, including:
items.zh: 了解非谓语动词的一般功能及其在句子中的用法，包括：

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Participles
items.zh: 分词
details: Identify past, and present participles.
Identify participial phrases.
Find the noun modified.
Correctly use commas with participial phrases.

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Gerunds and gerund phrases
items.zh: 动名词及动名词短语
details: Identify and tell its use in the sentence (subject, direct object, indirect object, appositive, predicate nominative, or object of preposition).

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Infinitives and infinitive phrases
items.zh: 不定式及不定式短语
details: Adjective and adverb: find the word it modifies.
Noun: tell its use in the sentence.

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Form cohesive sentences using both passive and active verbs and voice.
items.zh: 运用被动和主动的动词及语态写出连贯的句子。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Form and use verbs in the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional, and subjunctive mood.
items.zh: 构成并使用陈述语气、祈使语气、疑问语气、条件语气和虚拟语气的动词。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Correct erroneous shifts in verb voice and mood.
items.zh: 纠正动词语态和语气上的错误转换。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Understand and apply the basic rules of capitalization and punctuation when writing or speaking.
items.zh: 在写作或口语中理解并运用大小写和标点的基本规则。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use punctuation (comma, dash, and ellipsis) to indicate a pause or break.
items.zh: 使用标点（逗号、破折号和省略号）表示停顿或中断。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.
items.zh: 使用省略号表示省略内容。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Figure out the meaning of Grade 8 words and phrases, using a variety of strategies such as the following:
items.zh: 运用以下多种策略推断八年级单词和短语的含义：

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: context clues
items.zh: 上下文线索

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: examples
items.zh: 例子

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: definitions
items.zh: 定义

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: cause-and-effect relationships
items.zh: 因果关系

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: comparisons
items.zh: 比较

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use the overall meaning of a sentence as a clue to the meaning of words within the sentence.
items.zh: 利用句子的整体意思作为线索，推断句中单词的含义。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Figure out the meaning of words based on the word’s position and function within a sentence, such as part of speech, subject, predicate, object, etc.
items.zh: 根据单词在句子中的位置和作用来判断其含义，如词性、主语、谓语、宾语等。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use a dictionary, thesaurus, or glossary—print or digital—to answer questions about the meanings and usage of unfamiliar words.
items.zh: 使用词典、同义词词典或词汇表（纸质或数字版）来回答有关生词含义和用法的问题。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Know how to use a dictionary—print or digital—to pronounce words correctly and determine a word’s part of speech.
items.zh: 知道如何使用词典（纸质或数字版）正确发音并确定单词的词性。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use a dictionary to find the precise meaning of words and phrases.
items.zh: 使用词典查找单词和短语的确切含义。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Infer the meaning of words by using context, and then confirm the meaning in a dictionary.
items.zh: 利用上下文推断词义，然后在词典中确认。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Make accurate interpretations of similes and metaphors and other types of figurative language, such as personification, based on context.
items.zh: 根据上下文准确理解明喻、暗喻以及其他修辞手法（如拟人）的含义。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Interpret figures of speech based on context, especially verbal irony and puns.
items.zh: 根据上下文理解修辞格，尤其是言语反讽和双关语。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Discern nuances in word meanings.
items.zh: 辨别词义的细微差别。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Recognize and use word relationships to better understand words, such as
items.zh: 识别并运用词与词之间的关系来更好地理解单词，例如

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: cause/effect
items.zh: 原因／结果

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: item/category
items.zh: 个体／类别

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: part/whole
items.zh: 部分／整体

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: synonym/antonym
items.zh: 同义词／反义词

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: analogies
items.zh: 类比

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Distinguish connotations, or shades of meaning, among words with similar denotations (e.g., picky, fickle, discerning, sophisticated, fastidious, persnickety).
items.zh: 区分外延意义相近词语之间的内涵或语义细微差别（例如 picky、fickle、discerning、sophisticated、fastidious、persnickety）。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Acquire grade-level Tier 2 general academic and Tier 3 domain-specific words and phrases and use them with accuracy.
items.zh: 掌握符合年级水平的第二层通用学术词汇和第三层学科专业词汇及短语，并准确使用。

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.en: Use knowledge of Greek and Latin roots and affixes to figure out the meaning of a new word, such as Latin /Greek Word Meaning Examples aequus \[L\] equal equal, equation ago, acta \[L\] do, things done agent, enact, transact anthropos \[G\] man, human being anthropology, misanthrope ars \[L\] art artist, artifact brevis \[L\] short brevity, abbreviate canto \[L\] sing chant, cantor caput \[L\] head captain, decapitate clino \[L\] to lean, bend incline, decline cognito \[L\] know cognizant, recognize copia \[L\] plenty copy, copious credo \[L\] believe credible, incredulous culpa \[L\] blame culpable, culprit dominus \[L\] a lord, master dominate, dominion duco \[L\] lead abduct, introduce fido \[L\] to trust, believe confide, infidel fundo, fusum \[L\] pour, thing poured effusive, transfusion genus \[L\] kind, origin generic, congenital holos \[G\] whole holistic, catholic jungo \[L\] join junction, conjugal lego, lectum \[L\] read, thing read intellect, legible locus \[L\] a place local, dislocate loquor \[L\] speak eloquent, loquacious medius \[L\] middle mediate, mediocrity missio \[L\] a sending emissary, mission morior \[L\] die mortal nego \[L\] deny negate nihil \[L\] nothing nihilism, annihilate occido \[L\] kill homicide, suicide pathos \[G\] suffering, feeling sympathy, apathy pendo \[L\] weigh, hang depend, pendant per \[L\] through perceive, persist, persevere phobos \[G\] fear phobia, claustrophobia positum \[L\] placed position, opposite porto \[L\] carry transport, export possum \[L\] be able possible, potent pugno \[L\] to fight impugn, pugnacious Note: More Latin and Greek words and roots are listed in grades 6 and 7. In the listings here, L = Latin, G = Greek. No single form of the Latin or Greek words is consistently used here, but rather the form that is most similar to related English words. Latin /Greek Word Meaning Examples punctum \[L\] point punctual, punctuation rego \[L\] to rule regular, regency sanguis \[L\] blood sanguine satis \[L\] enough satisfy scio \[L\] know science, conscious solus \[L\] alone solo, desolate sonus \[L\] a sound unison, consonant sophos \[G\] wise philosophy, sophomore spiritus \[L\] breath inspire, spirit totus \[L\] whole totalitarianism tractum \[L\] drawn, pulled distract, tractor usus \[L\] use abuse, utensil vacuus \[L\] empty evacuate, vacuum verbum \[L\] word verbal verto \[L\] turn avert, convert, anniversary via \[L\] way, road deviate, viaduct
items.zh: 运用希腊语和拉丁语词根及词缀的知识推断新词的含义。下表列出拉丁语／希腊语词根、含义和例词（L＝拉丁语，G＝希腊语；表中采用的是与相关英语单词最相近的形式）：aequus [L] 相等的——equal, equation；ago, acta [L] 做、已做之事——agent, enact, transact；anthropos [G] 人、人类——anthropology, misanthrope；ars [L] 艺术——artist, artifact；brevis [L] 短的——brevity, abbreviate；canto [L] 唱——chant, cantor；caput [L] 头——captain, decapitate；clino [L] 倾斜、弯曲——incline, decline；cognito [L] 知道——cognizant, recognize；copia [L] 丰富——copy, copious；credo [L] 相信——credible, incredulous；culpa [L] 责备——culpable, culprit；dominus [L] 主人、主宰——dominate, dominion；duco [L] 领导——abduct, introduce；fido [L] 信任、相信——confide, infidel；fundo, fusum [L] 倾倒、倒出之物——effusive, transfusion；genus [L] 种类、起源——generic, congenital；holos [G] 整体——holistic, catholic；jungo [L] 连接——junction, conjugal；lego, lectum [L] 读、读物——intellect, legible；locus [L] 地点——local, dislocate；loquor [L] 说话——eloquent, loquacious；medius [L] 中间——mediate, mediocrity；missio [L] 派遣——emissary, mission；morior [L] 死——mortal；nego [L] 否认——negate；nihil [L] 无、虚无——nihilism, annihilate；occido [L] 杀——homicide, suicide；pathos [G] 痛苦、情感——sympathy, apathy；pendo [L] 称量、悬挂——depend, pendant；per [L] 穿过——perceive, persist, persevere；phobos [G] 恐惧——phobia, claustrophobia；positum [L] 放置——position, opposite；porto [L] 携带——transport, export；possum [L] 能够——possible, potent；pugno [L] 战斗——impugn, pugnacious；punctum [L] 点——punctual, punctuation；rego [L] 统治——regular, regency；sanguis [L] 血——sanguine；satis [L] 足够——satisfy；scio [L] 知道——science, conscious；solus [L] 单独——solo, desolate；sonus [L] 声音——unison, consonant；sophos [G] 智慧——philosophy, sophomore；spiritus [L] 呼吸——inspire, spirit；totus [L] 整体——totalitarianism；tractum [L] 拉、拖——distract, tractor；usus [L] 使用——abuse, utensil；vacuus [L] 空——evacuate, vacuum；verbum [L] 词——verbal；verto [L] 转——avert, convert, anniversary；via [L] 路、道路——deviate, viaduct。注：六年级和七年级还列出了更多拉丁语和希腊语单词及词根。

items.en: Note: The poems listed here constitute a selected core of poetry for this grade. You are encouraged to expose students to more poetry, old and new, and to have students write their own poems. Students should examine some poems in detail, discussing what the poems mean as well as asking questions about the poet’s use of language.

items.subject: English Language Arts
items.topic: Foreign Phrases Commonly Used in English
items.en: Students should learn the meaning of the following French words and phrases that are commonly used in English speech and writing. au revoir - goodbye, until we see each other again avant-garde - a group developing new or experimental concepts, a vanguard bête noire - a person or thing especially dreaded and avoided \[literally, “black beast”\] c’est la vie - that’s life, that’s how things happen carte blanche - full discretionary power \[literally, “blank page”\] cause célèbre - a very controversial issue that generates fervent public debate \[literally, a “celebrated case”\] coup de grâce - a decisive finishing blow coup d’état - overthrow of a government by a group déjà vu - something overly familiar \[literally, “already seen”\] enfant terrible - one whose remarks or actions cause embarrassment, or someone strikingly unconventional \[literally, “terrible child”\] fait accompli - an accomplished fact, presumably irreversible faux pas - a social blunder \[literally, “false step”\] Madame, Mademoiselle, Monsieur - Mrs., Miss, Mr. merci - thank you pièce de résistance - the principal part of the meal, a showpiece item raison d’être - reason for being savoir-faire - the ability to say or do the right thing in any situation, polished sureness in society \[literally, “to know (how) to do”\] tête-à-tête - private conversation between two people \[literally, “head to head”\]
items.zh: 学生应学习以下常用于英语口语和书面语中的法语词语及短语的含义：au revoir——再见，直到再相见；avant-garde——提出新观念或实验性概念的群体，先锋派；bête noire——特别令人畏惧和回避的人或事物〔字面义“黑兽”〕；c’est la vie——这就是生活，事情就是这样；carte blanche——完全的自由处置权〔字面义“空白页”〕；cause célèbre——引发激烈公众辩论的极具争议的问题〔字面义“著名案件”〕；coup de grâce——决定性的最后一击；coup d’état——政变（某一集团推翻政府）；déjà vu——似曾相识〔字面义“已经见过”〕；enfant terrible——言行令人尴尬的人，或极其标新立异的人〔字面义“可怕的孩子”〕；fait accompli——既成事实，大致不可逆转；faux pas——社交失礼〔字面义“错步”〕；Madame, Mademoiselle, Monsieur——夫人、小姐、先生；merci——谢谢；pièce de résistance——正餐的主菜，引申为最出彩的重头戏；raison d’être——存在的理由；savoir-faire——在任何场合都能恰当地说话或做事的能力，社交中的老练自信〔字面义“知道（如何）做”〕；tête-à-tête——两人之间的私下交谈〔字面义“头对头”〕。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Artifacts
items.zh: 人工制品（文物）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Priest-kings and eventual hereditary rule
items.zh: 祭司王以及最终的世袭统治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Civil servants
items.zh: 文职官员（公务员）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Southern Sumerian city-states including Ur, Kish, and Uruk
items.zh: 苏美尔南部城邦，包括乌尔、基什和乌鲁克

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: King Sargon, ruler of Akkad in northern Mesopotamia, conquered and joined together Sumerian city-states.
items.zh: 萨尔贡王是美索不达米亚北部阿卡德的统治者，他征服并统一了苏美尔各城邦。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Amorites, founders of Babylon
items.zh: 阿摩利人，巴比伦的建立者

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Code of Hammurabi, early code of laws inscribed on stone and publically displayed; “an eye for an eye”
items.zh: 《汉谟拉比法典》：早期法典，刻在石头上并公开展示；“以眼还眼”

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Assyrian Empire, army included skilled engineers
items.zh: 亚述帝国，其军队中包括技术娴熟的工程师

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: City of Nineveh, seat of Assyrian power
items.zh: 尼尼微城，亚述权力的中心

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Assyrian King Ashurbanipal built one of world’s first libraries.
items.zh: 亚述王亚述巴尼拔建造了世界上最早的图书馆之一。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Epic of Gilgamesh, a surviving treasure from library of Nineveh
items.zh: 《吉尔伽美什史诗》，尼尼微图书馆留存下来的瑰宝

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: King Nabopolassar and the Neo-Babylonian Empire
items.zh: 那波帕拉萨尔王与新巴比伦帝国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nebuchadnezzar, son of King Nabopolassar, rebuilt Babylon, including the Ishtar Gate
items.zh: 尼布甲尼撒是那波帕拉萨尔之子，他重建了巴比伦，包括伊什塔尔城门

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Nile begins as two rivers—the White Nile and the Blue Nile
items.zh: 尼罗河由两条河流汇成——白尼罗河和青尼罗河

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sahara Desert
items.zh: 撒哈拉沙漠

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Importance of Nile River as highway for trade
items.zh: 尼罗河作为贸易要道的重要性

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Nile meets the Mediterranean and branches into a delta, an area of fertile marshland.
items.zh: 尼罗河汇入地中海，并形成三角洲，这是一片肥沃的沼泽地带。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Flooding brought silt onto land, allowed for farming crops such as wheat, barley, and flax
items.zh: 洪水将淤泥带到土地上，使得种植小麦、大麦和亚麻等作物成为可能

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Intensive farming began after 6000 BCE; plows and irrigation canals, and the shadoof
items.zh: 公元前6000年后开始集约化耕作；出现了犁、灌溉渠以及桔槔（shadoof）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Egyptians named their territory Kemet
items.zh: 埃及人称自己的领土为“凯麦特”（Kemet）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: 4000 BCE two large settled areas of Egypt—Upper Egypt (south), Lower Egypt (north); Upper and Lower unified around 3000 BCE
items.zh: 公元前4000年，埃及有两个大型定居区——上埃及（南部）和下埃及（北部）；约公元前3000年上下埃及统一

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Memphis, the capital of unified kingdom
items.zh: 孟菲斯，统一王国的首都

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Unified Egypt ruled by pharaohs
items.zh: 统一的埃及由法老统治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Over 3000 years of dynasties; historians group this into three major periods—Old Kingdom, Middle Kingdom, and New Kingdom; 1600s BCE Middle Kingdom weakened
items.zh: 三千多年的王朝历史；历史学家将其分为三个主要时期——古王国、中王国和新王国；公元前17世纪中王国衰落

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Pharaoh Hyksos established a new dynasty, beginning Egypt’s New Kingdom
items.zh: 希克索斯法老建立了新王朝，开启了埃及新王国时期

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hatshepsut, woman pharaoh, ruled Egypt from 1479 to 1458 BCE
items.zh: 哈特谢普苏特，女法老，公元前1479年至前1458年统治埃及

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tutankhamun (1300s BCE) ruled for ten years; his tomb discovered in 1922
items.zh: 图坦卡蒙（公元前14世纪）在位十年；其陵墓于1922年被发现

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ramses II and the Golden Age; Ramses held power between 1279–1213 BCE
items.zh: 拉美西斯二世与黄金时代；拉美西斯于公元前1279年至前1213年执政

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ramses II built new capital city, temples, statues
items.zh: 拉美西斯二世建造了新都城、神庙和雕像

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ramses II, an expansionist ruler; conflict with Hittites
items.zh: 拉美西斯二世是一位扩张主义统治者；与赫梯人发生冲突

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Egyptians believed pharaohs chosen by the gods; pharaohs had a duty to uphold order, peace, and justice, a concept known as ma’at
items.zh: 埃及人相信法老由众神选定；法老有责任维护秩序、和平与正义，这一观念被称为“玛特”（ma’at）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ma’at was the concept of harmony and the name of the goddess who oversaw this concept
items.zh: “玛特”既是和谐的概念，也是掌管这一概念的女神之名

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Belief in judgment after death; dead person’s heart weighed on scale against Ma’at’s feather of truth; a harmonious life earned a good afterlife
items.zh: 相信死后有审判：将死者的心脏放在天平上与“玛特”的真理之羽称量；和谐的一生可换来美好的来世

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Belief that gods and goddesses were active in the human world; gods sometimes depicted with human bodies and animal heads
items.zh: 相信男女众神活跃于人间；神有时被描绘成人的身体、动物的头

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Osiris and Set
items.zh: 奥西里斯与赛特

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Belief that a person’s soul could not pass to the afterlife without its body; bodies preserved by mummification
items.zh: 相信人的灵魂若没有身体就无法进入来世；遗体通过木乃伊制作得以保存

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Societal social structure developed with a powerful ruling class; priests were part of powerful ruling class; the enslaved were bottom of social structure
items.zh: 社会结构逐渐形成，出现了强大的统治阶级；祭司属于统治阶级；奴隶处于社会底层

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Role of women in Egyptian society
items.zh: 埃及社会中女性的角色

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Priests maintained temples to the gods and performed mummification; gained understanding of human anatomy; not all Egyptians mummified
items.zh: 祭司维护神庙并制作木乃伊，由此增进了对人体解剖的了解；并非所有埃及人都被制成木乃伊

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Royal and upper-class Egyptians built monuments and tombs to preserve their remains and their riches
items.zh: 王室和上层埃及人修建纪念碑和陵墓，以保存遗体和财富

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Imhotep the architect; the pyramid structure
items.zh: 建筑师伊姆霍特普；金字塔结构

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Great Pyramid and the Great Sphinx
items.zh: 大金字塔与大狮身人面像

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Pictorial writing system—hieroglyphics; over time developed into three broad types
items.zh: 象形文字体系——圣书体；随时间发展出三大类型

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Egyptians wrote on stone, clay, and papyrus
items.zh: 埃及人在石头、黏土和纸莎草上书写

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rosetta Stone
items.zh: 罗塞塔石碑

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Egyptian decline; invasions
items.zh: 埃及的衰落；外族入侵

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: During time of Hyksos, Kush expanded northwards
items.zh: 希克索斯统治时期，库什向北扩张

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Around 745 BCE Kush invaded and defeated Egypt
items.zh: 约公元前745年，库什入侵并击败埃及

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kushite King Piye became a pharaoh
items.zh: 库什王皮耶成为法老

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kushites, under pressure from Assyrians, retreat to the south; established new capital, Meroë, which became a center for iron production
items.zh: 库什人在亚述人的压力下南撤；建立新都麦罗埃，该城成为铁器生产中心

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kushites established thriving trade network
items.zh: 库什人建立了繁荣的贸易网络

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 350 BCE Axum invaded and conquered Kush
items.zh: 公元前350年，阿克苏姆入侵并征服库什

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Israelites lived in a historic region sometimes called the Levant; area corresponds to modern-day Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria; today is called Near East or Middle East
items.zh: 以色列人居住在一个有时被称为“黎凡特”的历史地区；该地区大致相当于今天的以色列、约旦、黎巴嫩和叙利亚；如今称为近东或中东

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Originally a nomadic people, the Israelites settled in area called Canaan
items.zh: 以色列人原本是游牧民族，后来定居在称为“迦南”的地区

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Over time, the city of Jerusalem became center of Jewish culture
items.zh: 随着时间的推移，耶路撒冷城成为犹太文化的中心

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Monotheism
items.zh: 一神教

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Early collection of Jewish holy writings in work known as Tanakh or Hebrew Bible
items.zh: 早期犹太教圣典汇编，称为《塔纳赫》或《希伯来圣经》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Abraham and his descendants; covenant
items.zh: 亚伯拉罕及其后裔；盟约

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Roots of three religions: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam
items.zh: 三大宗教的根源：犹太教、基督教和伊斯兰教

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Israelites in Egypt
items.zh: 在埃及的以色列人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Moses, Exodus, Ten Commandments
items.zh: 摩西、出埃及记、十诫

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Promised land of Canaan
items.zh: 应许之地迦南

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Joshua and Jericho
items.zh: 约书亚与耶利哥

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tribes of Israel
items.zh: 以色列十二支派

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: House of David
items.zh: 大卫王室（大卫之家）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Solomon and the First Temple
items.zh: 所罗门与第一圣殿

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Development of monotheistic society based on God’s laws
items.zh: 以上帝律法为基础的一神教社会的发展

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Phoenicians came into area by 3000 BCE; lived along eastern Mediterranean, in coastal areas of present-day Syria, Lebanon, and northern Israel
items.zh: 腓尼基人在公元前3000年前进入该地区；居住在地中海东部沿岸，即今天的叙利亚、黎巴嫩和以色列北部沿海地区

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Phoenician sailors, navigators, and trade
items.zh: 腓尼基水手、航海家与贸易

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Phoenicians developed an alphabet
items.zh: 腓尼基人创造了字母表

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Philistines settle in region around 1200 BCE
items.zh: 非利士人约于公元前1200年定居该地区

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Assyrians
items.zh: 亚述人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar conquered Jerusalem
items.zh: 巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒征服耶路撒冷

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nebuchadnezzar destroys Jerusalem and the temple
items.zh: 尼布甲尼撒摧毁耶路撒冷和圣殿

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Babylonian captivity
items.zh: 巴比伦之囚

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Babylon conquered by Persian Empire
items.zh: 巴比伦被波斯帝国征服

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Persian king Cyrus II allows Jews of Babylon to return to Judah
items.zh: 波斯王居鲁士二世允许巴比伦的犹太人返回犹地亚

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Diaspora and the Second Temple
items.zh: 犹太人大流散与第二圣殿

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Queen Esther
items.zh: 以斯帖王后

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Persians defeated by Alexander the Great
items.zh: 波斯被亚历山大大帝击败

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Greek culture spreads throughout eastern Mediterranean
items.zh: 希腊文化传播到整个地中海东部

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: 164 BCE Jewish leader Judas Maccabeus leads revolt
items.zh: 公元前164年，犹太领袖犹大·马加比领导起义

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Judas and followers known as Maccabees take power in Judah
items.zh: 犹大及其追随者（被称为马加比人）在犹地亚掌权

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hanukkah and the menorah
items.zh: 光明节与九枝烛台

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Roman Rule in Judaea
items.zh: 罗马对犹地亚的统治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Dead Sea Scrolls
items.zh: 死海古卷

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Mainland of Greece is a peninsula surrounded by water on three sides; beyond mainland much of Greece is an archipelago; Crete is largest island
items.zh: 希腊大陆是一个三面环水的半岛；大陆之外，希腊大部分地区由群岛组成；克里特岛是最大的岛屿

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Mainland has two major zones—central and northern zone is mountainous; southwest is the Peloponnese, a peninsula connected to rest of mainland by a narrow strip of land, or isthmus
items.zh: 希腊本土分为两大区域——中部和北部为山区；西南部是伯罗奔尼撒半岛，它是一条狭长陆地（即地峡）与本土其余部分相连的半岛

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Eighty percent of land taken up by mountains
items.zh: 百分之八十的土地为山地所占据

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Mediterranean and Aegean Seas
items.zh: 地中海与爱琴海

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: First civilizations in region were not Greek
items.zh: 该地区最早的文明并非希腊文明

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Minoans flourished on island of Crete between 2700 and 1500 BCE
items.zh: 米诺斯文明于公元前2700年至1500年间在克里特岛兴盛

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Minoan palace at Knossos on Crete; frescoes
items.zh: 克里特岛克诺索斯的米诺斯宫殿；壁画

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: King Minos
items.zh: 米诺斯国王

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Mycenaean Civilization, named for city of Mycenae; dominant culture in the Peloponnese and several islands between 1700 and 1100 BCE
items.zh: 迈锡尼文明，以迈锡尼城命名；公元前1700年至1100年间在伯罗奔尼撒半岛和若干岛屿上占主导地位的文化

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Mycenaean settlements included Sparta, Thebes, Argos, Athens, and Tiryns
items.zh: 迈锡尼人的聚居地包括斯巴达、底比斯、阿尔戈斯、雅典和提林斯

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Mycenaean civilization influenced Greek civilization
items.zh: 迈锡尼文明影响了希腊文明

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Around 750 BCE, inhabitants of Greece known as Hellenes; ancient Greek culture came to be called Hellenic
items.zh: 约公元前750年，希腊的居民被称为赫伦人（Hellenes）；古希腊文化被称为希腊化文化（Hellenic）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Greeks established small kingdoms; traded with Egyptians and Phoenicians
items.zh: 希腊人建立了小型王国；与埃及人和腓尼基人进行贸易

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Ancient Greeks and Greek Civilization
items.en: Adapted Phoenician alphabet to create a Greek alphabet
items.zh: 改造腓尼基字母，创造出希腊字母

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Greeks practiced polytheism, belief in many gods
items.zh: 希腊人信奉多神教，即信仰众多神灵

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mount Olympus, home of most powerful and influential gods; court of Zeus, king of the gods
items.zh: 奥林匹斯山，是权力最大、最有影响力的诸神的居所；众神之王宙斯的宫廷所在地

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Olympic Games, held at Olympia in honor of Zeus
items.zh: 奥林匹克运动会，在奥林匹亚举行，以纪念宙斯

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Establishment of city-states including Athens, Sparta, Corinth, Thebes, Syracuse, and Rhodes; polis
items.zh: 建立城邦，包括雅典、斯巴达、科林斯、底比斯、叙拉古和罗得岛；城邦（polis）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tyrants and Oligarchs
items.zh: 僭主与寡头

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Concept of citizenship and citizens
items.zh: 公民身份与公民的概念

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Solon’s reforms and the development of Athenian democracy
items.zh: 梭伦改革与雅典民主政治的发展

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Athenian culture; education, debate, philosophy, literature, and music; symposia
items.zh: 雅典文化；教育、辩论、哲学、文学和音乐；会饮（symposia）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Assembly
items.zh: 公民大会

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Cleisthenes increased power of Assembly; enabled men over eighteen who owned property to participate in government
items.zh: 克利斯提尼增强了公民大会的权力；使年满十八岁且拥有财产的男子得以参与政事

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sparta’s military might; all men served in military
items.zh: 斯巴达的军事力量；所有男子都服兵役

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sparta led by two kings who ruled together
items.zh: 斯巴达由两位国王共同统治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rivalry between Athens and Sparta
items.zh: 雅典与斯巴达之间的争霸

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Persian wars; Marathon, Thermopylae, and Salamis
items.zh: 希波战争；马拉松、温泉关和萨拉米斯战役

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Herodotus, early historian
items.zh: 希罗多德，早期的历史学家

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Golden Age of Athens; Delian League
items.zh: 雅典的黄金时代；提洛同盟

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Pericles, a strong military commander; oversaw construction of Parthenon
items.zh: 伯里克利，一位强有力的军事统帅；主持帕特农神庙的建造

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Peloponnesian War: Sparta defeats Athens in 405 BCE
items.zh: 伯罗奔尼撒战争：斯巴达于公元前405年击败雅典

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Greek Literature and Drama; Greek tragedies; the Iliad and the Odyssey; Aesop’s fables; Sophocles, Aeschylus, and Euripides
items.zh: 希腊文学与戏剧；希腊悲剧；《伊利亚特》与《奥德赛》；《伊索寓言》；索福克勒斯、埃斯库罗斯和欧里庇得斯。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Philosophers of Athens; Socrates and Socratic method; Plato and Plato’s Republic; Plato’s Academy; Aristotle
items.zh: 雅典的哲学家；苏格拉底与苏格拉底法；柏拉图及《理想国》；柏拉图学园；亚里士多德

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Alexander the Great and the spread of Greek (“Hellenistic”) culture
items.zh: 亚历山大大帝与希腊（“希腊化”）文化的传播

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: India lies on a peninsula called a subcontinent; relative separation from rest of Asia; part of separation created by Himalayas which stretch across northern part of region— highest mountains in world; Hindu Kush mountain range to the west; subcontinent also includes Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, and Bhutan
items.zh: 印度位于一个被称为次大陆的半岛上；与亚洲其他地区相对隔绝；这种隔绝部分由横跨该地区北部的喜马拉雅山脉造成——世界最高的山脉；西侧为兴都库什山脉；该次大陆还包括巴基斯坦、尼泊尔、孟加拉国和不丹

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Indus River and Ganges River
items.zh: 印度河与恒河

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mountains and plateau
items.zh: 山脉与高原

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Indus civilization arose in northwest part of subcontinent around 2600 BCE
items.zh: 印度河文明约于公元前2600年在次大陆西北部兴起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Covered much of area now known as Pakistan
items.zh: 覆盖了今巴基斯坦的大部分地区

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Farming and livestock; crops included rice, grains, dates, lentils, and sesame; fruit trees
items.zh: 农业与畜牧业；农作物包括水稻、谷物、椰枣、扁豆和芝麻；果树

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Farming methods, including crop rotation and irrigation; plow
items.zh: 耕作方法，包括轮作和灌溉；犁

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Numerous organized settlements, including Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa
items.zh: 众多有组织的聚居地，包括摩亨佐-达罗和哈拉帕

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Cities designed on a grid system; courtyards; granaries, public baths, drains, and sewers
items.zh: 城市按网格系统规划；庭院；粮仓、公共浴池、排水沟和下水道

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Trade with other parts of the subcontinent
items.zh: 与次大陆其他地区的贸易

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Developed standardized weight system, written language called Indus or Harappan
items.zh: 发展了标准化的度量衡体系，以及称为印度河文字或哈拉帕文字的书写语言

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Many modern languages grew out of the Indo-European language group, including Hindi
items.zh: 许多现代语言源自印欧语系，包括印地语。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Vedic Period; small kingdoms; farming; agriculture around Ganges River Valley
items.zh: 吠陀时期；小型王国；农耕；恒河流域周边的农业

items.subject: History and Geography
