items.en: Sanskrit
items.zh: 梵语

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Vedas, some of the oldest religious texts in the world; texts are considered to reflect divine truth and sacred knowledge; first transmitted orally, later written down; the four Vedas are called Rig Veda, Yagur Veda, Sama Veda, Atharva Veda; Rig Veda is the oldest
items.zh: 《吠陀》，世界上最古老的宗教文本之一；这些文本被认为反映了神圣的真理与知识；最初以口头传承，后来才被记录下来；四部吠陀分别为《梨俱吠陀》《耶柔吠陀》《娑摩吠陀》《阿闼婆吠陀》；《梨俱吠陀》最为古老

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Varnas and Jatis
items.zh: 瓦尔纳与贾提（种姓与亚种姓）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hinduism Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva; avatars
items.zh: 印度教：梵天、毗湿奴和湿婆；化身（avatars）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Epic poems—Ramayana and Mahabharata
items.zh: 史诗——《罗摩衍那》与《摩诃婆罗多》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Reincarnation; karma
items.zh: 轮回；业（karma）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Buddhism and Prince Siddhartha Gautama; Buddha, “enlightened one
items.zh: 佛教与悉达多·乔达摩王子；佛陀，意为“觉悟者”

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nirvana
items.zh: 涅槃

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path
items.zh: 四圣谛与八正道

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Jainism
items.zh: 耆那教

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Mauryan Empire and Chandragupta Maurya
items.zh: 孔雀王朝与旃陀罗笈多·孔雀

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: King Ashoka (also spelled Asoka)
items.zh: 阿育王（亦拼作 Asoka）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Gupta Empire
items.zh: 笈多王朝

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: China’s eastern border at the edge of the Pacific Ocean; to the north lies the Gobi Desert; to the southwest, China’s border with India is formed by the Himalayas; geographical factors provide China with formidable physical borders
items.zh: 中国东部边界位于太平洋边缘；北面是戈壁沙漠；西南部，中国与印度的边界由喜马拉雅山脉构成；地理因素为中国提供了坚固的天然边界

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Huang He (Yellow River) and Yangzi (Yangtze, Chang Jiang) River
items.zh: 黄河（Huang He）与长江（Yangzi，亦称 Yangtze、Chang Jiang）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Early civilization arose in valley around the Huang He
items.zh: 早期文明兴起于黄河周边的河谷

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Farming methods; grains, rice, soybeans, tea, mulberry trees
items.zh: 耕作方法；谷物、水稻、大豆、茶叶、桑树

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Developed one or world’s oldest writing system; at first, symbols represented objects
items.zh: 发展了世界上最古老的书写体系之一；起初，符号代表实物

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Early Chinese civilization shaped by several dynasties with sophisticated political states
items.zh: 早期中国文明由若干个拥有成熟政治体制的王朝塑造

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Xia dynasty; Yu the Great
items.zh: 夏朝；大禹

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Shang dynasty rose to power around 1766 BCE; King Tang
items.zh: 商朝约于公元前1766年崛起；商汤王

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Daoism
items.zh: 道家思想（道教）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Zhou dynasty 1046 BCE; promoted idea of divine right; first Zhou king, Wen; feudal system
items.zh: 周朝，公元前1046年；倡导君权神授的思想；首位周王为周文王；封建制度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spring and Autumn Period 770 BCE; semi-independent states
items.zh: 春秋时期，公元前770年；半独立的诸侯国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Confucianism, influential product of Spring and Autumn period; named for Chinese philosopher Kong Qiu; Golden Rule; five basic relationships; filial piety
items.zh: 儒家思想，春秋时期极具影响力的产物；以中国哲学家孔丘（孔子）命名；黄金法则；五种基本人伦关系；孝道

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Warring states period lasted from 481 to 221 BCE; first known military manual written at this time, known as The Art of War
items.zh: 战国时期从公元前481年持续到公元前221年；已知最早的军事著作写于此时，即《孙子兵法》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Qin Empire; Yeng Zheng, took title Shihuangdi, meaning first emperor; tried to unify China; Lingqu Canal; begins construction of Great Wall; Terracotta Warriors
items.zh: 秦帝国；嬴政，采用“始皇帝”称号，意为第一位皇帝；试图统一中国；灵渠；开始修筑长城；兵马俑

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Han dynasty ruled for more than four hundred years, from 202 BCE to 220 CE; Xiang Yu; Emperor Wu; trade in silk and spices, the Silk Road, invention of paper
items.zh: 汉朝统治长达四百多年，从公元前202年至公元220年；项羽；汉武帝；丝绸与香料贸易、丝绸之路、造纸术的发明

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Increased trade, and contact with foreigners, enabled spread of Buddhism into China
items.zh: 贸易的增长以及与外国人的接触使佛教得以传入中国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Region where city of Rome established called Latium
items.zh: 罗马城建立的地区称为拉丁姆（Latium）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Mediterranean Sea, Aegean Sea, Adriatic Sea
items.zh: 地中海、爱琴海、亚得里亚海

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Apennine Mountains, Alps
items.zh: 亚平宁山脉、阿尔卑斯山脉

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Greece, Italy (peninsula), France, Spain
items.zh: 希腊、意大利（半岛）、法国、西班牙

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: North Africa, Asia Minor (peninsula), Turkey
items.zh: 北非、小亚细亚（半岛）、土耳其

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Bosporus (strait), Black Sea, Istanbul (Constantinople)
items.zh: 博斯普鲁斯海峡、黑海、伊斯坦布尔（君士坦丁堡）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Red Sea, Tiber River, Persian Gulf
items.zh: 红海、台伯河、波斯湾

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Etruscans
items.zh: 伊特鲁里亚人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Greek ruler Pyrrhus defeated by Romans in Southern Italy
items.zh: 希腊统治者皮洛士在意大利南部被罗马人击败

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: The Republic: Senate, Consuls, Patricians, Plebeians
items.zh: 罗马共和国：元老院、执政官、贵族、平民

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Plebeian Council
items.zh: 平民会议

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Punic Wars: Carthage, Hannibal, Battle of Cannae, 216 BCE
items.zh: 布匿战争：迦太基、汉尼拔、坎尼战役，公元前216年

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Rome: Republic to Empire and Roman Civilization
items.en: Scipio
items.zh: 西庇阿

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Forum: temples, marketplaces, etc.
items.zh: 罗马广场：神庙、市场等

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Colosseum: circuses, gladiator combat, chariot races
items.zh: 罗马斗兽场：竞技表演、角斗士搏斗、战车竞赛

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Theater and Poetry
items.zh: 戏剧与诗歌

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Roads, bridges, sewer system, public toilets, public baths and aqueducts
items.zh: 道路、桥梁、排水系统、公共厕所、公共浴场和引水渠

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Worship of gods and goddesses, largely based on Greek religion
items.zh: 对男女诸神的崇拜，主要基于希腊宗教

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Most Romans spoke a version of Latin; Greek spoken also
items.zh: 大多数罗马人使用某种形式的拉丁语；也讲希腊语

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Greek philosophy, especially Stoicism and Epicureanism, influential in the Republic
items.zh: 希腊哲学，尤其是斯多葛学派和伊壁鸠鲁学派，在共和国时期影响深远

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Cicero, Seneca, Pliny the Elder
items.zh: 西塞罗、塞内加、老普林尼

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Conflicting interests of optimates and populares
items.zh: 贵族派（optimates）与平民派（populares）的利益冲突

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Gaius Julius Caesar, Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus (Pompey), Marcus Licinius Crassus held power as the First Triumvirate
items.zh: 盖乌斯·尤利乌斯·恺撒、格奈乌斯·庞培·马格努斯（庞培）、马库斯·李锡尼·克拉苏以“前三头同盟”之名掌权

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Caesar elected Consul, given command of Roman armies, aligned with populares
items.zh: 恺撒当选执政官，被授予罗马军队的指挥权，与平民派结盟

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Caesar crosses Rubicon, declares war on Pompey
items.zh: 恺撒渡过卢比孔河，向庞培宣战

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Defeats Pompey
items.zh: 击败庞培

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Pompey in Egypt
items.zh: 庞培在埃及

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Caesar in Egypt
items.zh: 恺撒在埃及

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Caesar becomes Dictator for life in 44 BCE
items.zh: 恺撒于公元前44年成为终身独裁官

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Cleopatra of Egypt
items.zh: 埃及的克利奥帕特拉（克娄巴特拉）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Ides of March, Caesar assassinated in the Senate, Brutus, Cassius
items.zh: 三月十五日（Ides of March），恺撒在元老院遇刺，布鲁图斯、卡西乌斯

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Marcus Antonius and Octavian defeat Brutus and Cassius
items.zh: 马克·安东尼与屋大维击败布鲁图斯和卡西乌斯

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Octavian becomes Augustus Caesar; imperator; period of peace and stability (Pax Romana) with integration of non-Romans into Roman society; reorganization of tax system
items.zh: 屋大维成为奥古斯都·恺撒；最高统帅（imperator）；进入和平与稳定的时期（罗马和平，Pax Romana），非罗马人被融入罗马社会；重组税收制度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Virgil and the Aeneid
items.zh: 维吉尔与《埃涅阿斯纪》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Ovid and Metamorphoses
items.zh: 奥维德与《变形记》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Expansion of empire, challenges the old Republican form of government
items.zh: 帝国扩张，对旧的共和政体形成挑战

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Management and defense challenges of vast Roman empire; millions of inhabitants
items.zh: 庞大罗马帝国的治理与防御挑战；数以百万计的居民

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Emperor Diocletian (284 to 305 CE) split empire into two halves, each with its own emperor; western half ruled from Rome, eastern half ruled from Asia Minor
items.zh: 戴克里先皇帝（公元284年至305年）将帝国分为两半，各由一位皇帝统治；西半部从罗马治理，东半部从小亚细亚治理

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Corruption and conflict over political power
items.zh: 腐败与政治权力之争

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Constantine rises to power in 312 CE; moves capital to Byzantium
items.zh: 君士坦丁于公元312年掌权；将首都迁至拜占庭

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Constantine adopts Christianity; makes Christianity Rome’s official religion, ending persecution of Christians
items.zh: 君士坦丁皈依基督教；将基督教定为罗马国教，结束了对基督徒的迫害

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Weakened by outside attacks, particularly Germanic tribes
items.zh: 因外部袭击而削弱，尤其是日耳曼部落的入侵

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: City of Rome sacked in 410 CE
items.zh: 公元410年罗马城遭洗劫

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Western Roman emperor defeated by Germanic chieftain, Odoacer
items.zh: 西罗马皇帝被日耳曼首领奥多亚塞击败

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: The rise of the Eastern Roman Empire, known as the Byzantine Empire
items.zh: 东罗马帝国的兴起，即拜占庭帝国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Trading Center
items.zh: 贸易中心

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Constantinople (now called Istanbul) merges diverse influences and cultures.
items.zh: 君士坦丁堡（今称伊斯坦布尔）融合了多种影响与文化。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Justinian (527 to 565 CE), Justinian’s Code
items.zh: 查士丁尼（公元527年至565年），《查士丁尼法典》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Outbreak of plague, depleting population
items.zh: 瘟疫爆发，导致人口锐减

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Decline of the Republic and Fall of Western Empire
items.en: Rise of Islamic Rulerss
items.zh: 伊斯兰统治者的兴起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Arabian Peninsula is the largest peninsula in the world; it is surrounded by the Red Sea; it is part of the continent of Asia
items.zh: 阿拉伯半岛是世界上最大的半岛；红海环绕其周围；它属于亚洲大陆

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Persian Gulf, Arabian Sea, Mediterranean Sea
items.zh: 波斯湾、阿拉伯海、地中海

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Plateau, Sandy Deserts, Dry Plains, Oases
items.zh: 高原、沙漠、干旱平原、绿洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Part of trade network linking ancient civilizations including Egypt, Kush, Mesopotamia, Persia, China, India, Greece, Rome
items.zh: 贸易网络的一部分，连接包括埃及、库什、美索不达米亚、波斯、中国、印度、希腊、罗马在内的古代文明。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Trees produced resins, frankincense and myrrh; Silk Road; Gold, Ivory, Silks, Spices
items.zh: 树木产出树脂、乳香和没药；丝绸之路；黄金、象牙、丝绸、香料

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Introduction of camels
items.zh: 骆驼的引入

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Growth of trading centers Mecca and Medina
items.zh: 贸易中心麦加和麦地那的兴起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nomadic herdsmen
items.zh: 游牧牧民

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Nabataeans ruled for a time; built Petra; managed water with cisterns
items.zh: 纳巴泰人曾一度统治此地；建造了佩特拉；用蓄水池管理水资源

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Much of the story of Muhammad, and early Islamic customs and practices come from the Hadith and the Sunna
items.zh: 关于穆罕默德的大量事迹以及早期伊斯兰教的习俗和做法都来自《圣训》（Hadith）和《逊奈》（Sunna）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Quran is Islam’s most holy book.
items.zh: 《古兰经》是伊斯兰教最神圣的经典。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muhammad: the last prophet, thought to have been born in Mecca, in present day Saudi Arabia around 570 CE; family part of Quraish tribe
items.zh: 穆罕默德：最后一位先知，据认为约于公元570年出生在麦加（今沙特阿拉伯境内）；其家族属于古莱氏部落

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Orphaned and raised by relatives; traveled with uncle’s trading caravan
items.zh: 幼年丧亲，由亲属抚养长大；曾随叔父的商队出行

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Married Khadija; became a merchant
items.zh: 迎娶赫蒂彻；成为商人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sought spiritual understanding at age forty; went to a cave
items.zh: 四十岁时寻求精神领悟；前往一个山洞

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muhammad believed God and angel Gabriel spoke to him through visions; instructed to spread Islam, a word meaning surrender or submission to God
items.zh: 穆罕默德相信真主和天使加百列通过异象向他说话；受命传播伊斯兰教，该词意为顺从或臣服于真主

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muhammad shares revelations; meets opposition, especially in Mecca
items.zh: 穆罕默德传播启示；遭遇反对，尤其是在麦加

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muhammad and followers go to Medina (the Hijarah)
items.zh: 穆罕默德及其追随者前往麦地那（希吉拉，Hijarah）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muhammad receives more revelations in Medina; begins new Islamic society
items.zh: 穆罕默德在麦地那获得更多启示；开始建立新的伊斯兰社会

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Many Jewish residents leave Medina
items.zh: 许多犹太居民离开麦地那

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muhammad organizes fighting force; takes over Mecca; rejects pagan gods; Mecca becomes important site of Islamic worship
items.zh: 穆罕默德组织武装力量；占领麦加；摒弃异教诸神；麦加成为伊斯兰教重要的礼拜圣地

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Main tenets of Islam called the five pillars: Profession of Faith; Prayer; Alms: Fasting; Pilgrimage
items.zh: 伊斯兰教的主要信条称为“五功”：信仰的表白（念）；礼拜（礼）；施舍（课）；斋戒（斋）；朝觐（朝）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After Muhammad’s death around 632 CE, the first caliph was Abu Bakr; the second caliph was Umar; the third caliph was Osman
items.zh: 穆罕默德约于公元632年去世后，第一任哈里发是阿布·伯克尔；第二任哈里发是欧麦尔；第三任哈里发是奥斯曼

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Umar and Osman expand territory under Islamic control
items.zh: 欧麦尔和奥斯曼扩大了伊斯兰控制的领土

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Osman creates administrative divisions of Islamic state; overseas official version of Quran
items.zh: 奥斯曼设立伊斯兰国家的行政区划；审定《古兰经》的官方版本

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Osman killed; Muhammad’s cousin Ali becomes caliph
items.zh: 奥斯曼遇刺身亡；穆罕默德的堂弟阿里成为哈里发

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Civil War breaks out with two opposing factions; Muslims become divided into two main groups—Shia, who followed Ali’ Sunni who rejected Ali
items.zh: 内战爆发，形成两个敌对阵营；穆斯林分裂为两大主要群体——追随阿里的什叶派（Shia），以及拒绝阿里的逊尼派（Sunni）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Islam expands into Africa, Asia, and Southern Spain
items.zh: 伊斯兰教扩展到非洲、亚洲和西班牙南部

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spread of Arabic culture, including language, art and architecture
items.zh: 阿拉伯文化的传播，包括语言、艺术和建筑

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Cities throughout Islamic Empire become centers of learning, including Damascus and Baghdad
items.zh: 伊斯兰帝国境内的城市成为学术中心，包括大马士革和巴格达。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Conflict with external enemies; clashes with Christian leaders in Europe; the Crusades
items.zh: 与外部敌人的冲突；与欧洲基督教领袖的冲突；十字军东征

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Islamic Golden Age; trade; banking; universities; scholars; mathematics, including algebra and calculus; medical knowledge
items.zh: 伊斯兰黄金时代；贸易；银行业；大学；学者；数学，包括代数和微积分；医学知识

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Avicenna (Ibn Sina); Five-volume medical encyclopedia—The Canon of Medicine; The Book of Healing
items.zh: 阿维森纳（伊本·西那）：五卷本医学百科全书《医典》；以及《治疗之书》。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Baghdad site of House of Wisdom
items.zh: 巴格达，智慧宫（House of Wisdom）所在地

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Works of literature such as The Thousand and One Nights
items.zh: 文学作品，如《一千零一夜》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Emergence of Ottoman Empire
items.zh: 奥斯曼帝国的崛起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mesoamerica—a historical region stretching from northwest of modern Mexico southward into isthmus connecting North and South America
items.zh: 中美洲——一个历史区域，从今墨西哥西北部向南延伸，直至连接南北美洲的地峡

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Gulf of Mexico, Pacific Ocean
items.zh: 墨西哥湾、太平洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Yucatán Peninsula
items.zh: 尤卡坦半岛

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Amazon River; river basin
items.zh: 亚马逊河；流域

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Andes Mountains
items.zh: 安第斯山脉

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Altiplano
items.zh: 阿尔蒂普拉诺高原（Altiplano）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, Mexico, Peru, Bolivia, Brazil, Columbia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Chile, Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana
items.zh: 危地马拉、伯利兹、萨尔瓦多、洪都拉斯、墨西哥、秘鲁、玻利维亚、巴西、哥伦比亚、厄瓜多尔、委内瑞拉、智利、阿根廷、巴拉圭、乌拉圭、圭亚那、苏里南、法属圭亚那

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rainforest
items.zh: 雨林

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Atacama Desert
items.zh: 阿塔卡马沙漠

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Olmec civilization arose around 1200 BCE along Mexico’s Gulf Coast; name Olmec comes from Aztec language, Nahuatl
items.zh: 奥尔梅克文明约于公元前1200年在墨西哥湾沿岸兴起；“奥尔梅克”一词来自阿兹特克语言纳瓦特尔语

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Olmecs extracted latex from rubber trees
items.zh: 奥尔梅克人从橡胶树中提取乳胶

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Inhabited large settlements such as the now called San Lorenzo
items.zh: 居住在大型聚居地，如现今所称的圣洛伦索

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Trade goods such as obsidian, jade, rubber, skins, pottery found at San Lorenzo, Las Limas, island of La Venta
items.zh: 在圣洛伦索、拉斯利马斯、拉文塔岛发现的黑曜石、玉石、橡胶、兽皮、陶器等贸易物品。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Constructed pyramids; large, carved stone heads; Olmec cave art
items.zh: 建造金字塔；大型雕刻石首；奥尔梅克洞穴艺术

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Zapotec civilization centered in Valley of Oaxaca dates back to 1600 BCE
items.zh: 萨波特克文明以瓦哈卡谷地为中心，可追溯至公元前1600年

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: City of Monte Albán founded in 500 BCE
items.zh: 蒙特阿尔班城建于公元前500年

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Use of water diversion and irrigation
items.zh: 引水与灌溉的使用

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Declined due to outside invasion
items.zh: 因外族入侵而衰落

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Large, prosperous realm of linked cities prior to Europeans
items.zh: 在欧洲人到来之前，由相互连接的城市组成的大型繁荣国度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sophisticated architecture; advances in astronomy, mathematics
items.zh: 精湛的建筑；天文学和数学的进步

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Writing system; Classic Period writing system contains more than eight hundred symbols
items.zh: 书写系统；古典时期的书写系统包含八百多个符号

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Cities contained palaces, temples, public spaces
items.zh: 城市中有宫殿、神庙和公共空间

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Main cities in late Classical Period include Chichén Itzá, on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula; Palenque and Calakmul, in Mexico; Caracol, in Belize; Copán, in Honduras; and several large centers in Guatemala, including Tikal
items.zh: 古典晚期的主要城市包括：墨西哥尤卡坦半岛的奇琴伊察；墨西哥的帕伦克和卡拉克穆尔；伯利兹的卡拉科尔；洪都拉斯的科潘；以及危地马拉的几处大型中心，包括蒂卡尔

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Construction of pyramids
items.zh: 金字塔的建造

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Religious beliefs—three distinct but linked realms—sky, earth, underworld
items.zh: 宗教信仰——三个不同但相互关联的领域——天空、大地、地下世界

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Popol Vuh collection of Maya religious stories
items.zh: 《波波尔·乌》，玛雅宗教故事的合集

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Human sacrifice
items.zh: 人祭

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Maya planned rituals on a regular schedule, using a calendar called the Tzolkin (the count of days)
items.zh: 玛雅人按固定日程安排祭祀仪式，使用一种名为卓尔金历（Tzolkin，意为“日子的计数”）的历法

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Used astronomical observation to plan buildings
items.zh: 利用天文观测来规划建筑

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Decline began around 800 CE; unclear as to why
items.zh: 约公元800年开始衰落；原因不明

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After Maya Classic Period ended around 900 CE, Mesoamerica underwent transitions as new population centers arose
items.zh: 玛雅古典时期约于公元900年结束后，随着新的人口中心出现，中美洲经历了变迁

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After several centuries, a new civilization arose in Central Mexico
items.zh: 几个世纪后，一个新的文明在墨西哥中部兴起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: From around 1300 CE, the Aztec rose in power through military successes; united most of northern region of Mesoamerica into an empire containing millions of people
items.zh: 从约公元1300年起，阿兹特克人凭借军事胜利崛起；将中美洲北部大部分地区统一为一个拥有数百万人口的帝国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Aztec built an empire centered in capital city of Tenochtitlán, where Mexico City stands today; Templo Mayor
items.zh: 阿兹特克人建立了一个以首都特诺奇蒂特兰为中心的帝国，即今墨西哥城所在地；大神庙（Templo Mayor）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Lake Texcoco site of Tenochtitlán
items.zh: 特斯科科湖，特诺奇蒂特兰的所在地

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Aztec believed in Pantheon of gods
items.zh: 阿兹特克人信奉万神殿般的众神

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Like the Maya, the Aztec had a calendar system
items.zh: 与玛雅人一样，阿兹特克人也有历法系统

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Aztec army contained skilled soldiers
items.zh: 阿兹特克军队拥有技艺高超的士兵

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sophisticated taxation system
items.zh: 完善的税收制度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Human sacrifice
items.zh: 人祭

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Montezuma came to power in 1502 CE; expanded Aztec empire
items.zh: 蒙特祖马于公元1502年掌权；扩张了阿兹特克帝国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spanish arrive in 1519 CE led by Hernán Cortés
items.zh: 西班牙人于公元1519年在埃尔南·科尔特斯率领下到来

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Montezuma taken hostage; submits to Cortés; Montezuma killed
items.zh: 蒙特祖马被扣为人质；向科尔特斯屈服；蒙特祖马遇害

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spanish conquer Tenochtitlán
items.zh: 西班牙人征服特诺奇蒂特兰

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spread of European diseases causes decline in Aztec population
items.zh: 欧洲疾病的传播导致阿兹特克人口减少

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Inca—one of several groups who lived in the Andes region
items.zh: 印加人——生活在安第斯地区的若干族群之一

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In late 1300s CE, they began to conquer neighbors.
items.zh: 公元14世纪末，他们开始征服周边邻族。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Between 1400 and 1533 CE they established largest empire in the Americas.
items.zh: 公元1400年至1533年间，他们建立了美洲最大的帝国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Heart of Inca Empire was city of Cuzco, in modern Peru.
items.zh: 印加帝国的核心是现代秘鲁的库斯科城。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Inca rulers used labor of those conquered to build infrastructure—roads and bridges that connected the empire
items.zh: 印加统治者利用被征服者的劳动力修建基础设施——连接帝国的道路和桥梁

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Highly skilled stoneworkers
items.zh: 技艺高超的石匠

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Macchu Picchu
items.zh: 马丘比丘

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Social structure; empire divided into four parts with four governors
items.zh: 社会结构；帝国分为四个部分，由四位总督治理

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tax system
items.zh: 税收制度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Use of a quipu used for communicating information
items.zh: 使用奇普（quipu）来传递信息

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Distinctive art style; geometric shapes
items.zh: 独特的艺术风格；几何图案

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ruler Atahualpa held hostage and then killed.
items.zh: 统治者阿塔瓦尔帕被扣为人质，随后被杀。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spanish invaders led by Francisco Pizarro killed thousands of Inca.
items.zh: 弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗率领的西班牙入侵者杀害了数千名印加人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Conquered Cuzco in 1533
items.zh: 公元1533年征服库斯科

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: European diseases weakened the Inca.
items.zh: 欧洲疾病削弱了印加人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Last Inca ruler captured and killed by Spanish in 1572; Inca realm absorbed by Spanish crown
items.zh: 最后一位印加统治者于1572年被西班牙人俘获并杀害；印加领土被西班牙王室吞并

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: North and south finally united by northern general, Yang Jian, who became Emperor Wendi
items.zh: 北方将领杨坚最终统一南北，成为隋文帝。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rise of Sui dynasty in 581 CE
items.zh: 隋朝于公元581年兴起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: China united and ruled once again from old capital, Chang’an
items.zh: 中国再度统一，并以旧都长安为统治中心

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Emperor Wendi establishes new administrative bureaucracy; exam based placement in civil service
items.zh: 隋文帝建立新的行政官僚体系；以考试选拔文官

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sui dynasty falls due to failed military campaigns and financial excess
items.zh: 隋朝因军事征讨失败和财政挥霍而灭亡

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Emperor Wendi’s son, Emperor Yangdi, killed by government official in 618 CE
items.zh: 隋文帝之子隋炀帝于公元618年被朝廷官员所杀

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Chang’an captured by general Li Yuan; Li Yuan becomes known as Gaozu; first emperor of new Tang dynasty
items.zh: 长安被将领李渊攻占；李渊被称为高祖；成为新唐朝的第一位皇帝

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Gazozu creates new legal code.
items.zh: 高祖（Gaozu）制定新的法典。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Tang rule from 618 to 907 CE.
items.zh: 唐朝统治时期为公元618年至907年。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Empress Wu Zhao a Tang ruler; only woman to have ruled China
items.zh: 武则天（武曌），唐朝统治者；中国历史上唯一一位女皇帝

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Golden age in China, particularly during reign of Emperor Xuanzong; cultural achievements; woodblock printing; poets Li Bai and Du Fu
items.zh: 中国的黄金时代，尤其在唐玄宗统治时期；文化成就；雕版印刷；诗人李白和杜甫

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tea merchants gain great wealth.
items.zh: 茶商积累了巨额财富。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: World’s first paper money and gunpowder
items.zh: 世界上最早的纸币和火药

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Period after the Tang is called the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period.
items.zh: 唐朝之后的时期称为五代十国时期。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Zhao Kuangyin establishes Song dynasty; becomes Emperor Taizu
items.zh: 赵匡胤建立宋朝；成为宋太祖

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Increasing use of machinery and advances in agriculture
items.zh: 机械使用日益增多，农业取得进步

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New technologies such as magnetic compass, sternpost ship rudders, and movable type printing press
items.zh: 新技术，如指南针、船尾舵和活字印刷机

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Temüjin was born in the 1160s to nomads who lived on the steppe north of China, in the region now called Mongolia; better known as Genghis Khan; elected as ruler of all Mongolia
items.zh: 铁木真于1160年代出生于生活在中国北方草原的游牧家庭，该地区今称蒙古；他更为人熟知的名字是成吉思汗；被推举为整个蒙古的统治者

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Genghis Khan creates a law code; has Mongol language written down
items.zh: 成吉思汗制定法典；命人将蒙古语记录下来

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mongols traveled, hunted, and fought on horseback.
items.zh: 蒙古人骑马出行、狩猎和作战。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Launched successful assaults on cities in northern China; attacked Korean peninsula, and lands in modern-day Russia, Ukraine, and Poland
items.zh: 成功攻打中国北方城市；进攻朝鲜半岛以及今俄罗斯、乌克兰和波兰的土地

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Genghis Khan died in 1227; sons inherited parts of his empire; most powerful part inherited by grandson Kublai Khan
items.zh: 成吉思汗于1227年去世；诸子继承了帝国的一部分；最强大的部分由孙子忽必烈继承

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Between 1260 and 1271 CE, Kublai Khan’s forces conquered Song Empire in south China
items.zh: 公元1260年至1271年间，忽必烈的军队征服了中国南方的宋帝国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kublai Khan declares himself emperor of China; establishes capital at Beijing; adopts imperial name Shizu; his dynasty known as Yuan
items.zh: 忽必烈宣布自己为中国皇帝；定都北京；采用帝号世祖；其王朝称为元朝

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Expansion of trade
items.zh: 贸易扩张

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Marco Polo (c.1254–1324) visits China; later wrote of his adventures Il milione (The million)
items.zh: 马可·波罗（约1254–1324）访问中国；后来在《马可·波罗游记》（Il milione，意为“百万”）中记述了他的冒险经历

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Yuan dynasty declines after death of Kublai Khan
items.zh: 忽必烈去世后，元朝开始衰落

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New emperor, Hongwu, establishes Ming dynasty; distinctive style of pottery
items.zh: 新皇帝洪武建立明朝；独具特色的瓷器风格

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Great Wall construction
items.zh: 长城的修筑

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Construct new palace complex in Beijing, known as Forbidden City
items.zh: 在北京修建新的宫殿建筑群，即紫禁城

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Zheng He’s fleet
items.zh: 郑和的船队

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ming dynasty taken over by the Manchu; they establish China’s final dynasty as the Qing.
items.zh: 明朝被满族接管；他们建立了中国最后一个王朝——清朝。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: East Asia and Southeast Asia includes China and lands to the north, south, and east; present-day Korea and Japan typically considered part of East Asia, as well as Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Laos, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines
items.zh: 东亚和东南亚包括中国及其以北、以南和以东的土地；现今的韩国和日本通常被视为东亚的一部分，越南、柬埔寨、泰国、老挝、马来西亚、印度尼西亚和菲律宾亦然

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: East and Southeast Asia lie in and along the coast of Pacific Ocean.
items.zh: 东亚和东南亚位于太平洋及其沿岸。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Peninsulas and archipelagos; western curve of Ring of Fire
items.zh: 半岛与群岛；环太平洋火山带的西侧弧线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Tsunamis; typhoons
items.zh: 海啸；台风

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Mount Fuji
items.zh: 富士山

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Many early settlements emerged on or near coastline
items.zh: 许多早期聚居地出现在海岸线上或附近

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Agriculture developed in river valleys and limited plains regions.
items.zh: 农业在河谷和有限的平原地区发展起来。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: 2000 BCE, people began to live in more concentrated farming villages; dolmens
items.zh: 公元前2000年，人们开始生活在更为集中的农耕村落；支石墓（dolmens）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: 700 BCE rice is grown as a staple; 300s BCE bronze metalwork given way to iron; jade and pottery Timeline
items.zh: 公元前700年，水稻成为主要作物；公元前300年代，青铜铸造让位于铁器；玉器与陶器 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: 700s to 400s BCE, some towns united into first complex state in the peninsula, Gojoseon
items.zh: 公元前700年至400年间，一些城镇联合成为半岛上第一个复杂的国家——古朝鲜

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: 108 BCE north of Korea conquered by Han dynasty of China; later, four rival states emerged (18 BCE to 660 CE); referred to as Three Kingdoms period
items.zh: 公元前108年，朝鲜北部被中国汉朝征服；后来出现四个敌对政权（公元前18年至公元660年）；称为三国时期

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Societal class system
items.zh: 社会等级制度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Korea unified by Silla kingdom in late 600s CE, aided by Chinese Tang dynasty; called Unified Silla kingdom
items.zh: 公元7世纪末，朝鲜在中国唐朝帮助下由新罗王国统一，称为统一新罗王国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Unified Silla monarchs came from Kim clan; organized kingdom into nine provinces run by governors appointed by the king
items.zh: 统一新罗的君主出自金氏家族；将王国划分为九个州，由国王任命的总督治理

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Civilizations of Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia
items.en: Unified Silla kingdom declines in 900s CE; replaced by Goryeo (or Koryo) dynasty
items.zh: 统一新罗王国于公元10世纪衰落；被高丽王朝（Goryeo 或 Koryo）取代

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Yayoi began in 300 BCE
items.zh: 弥生时代始于公元前300年

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Increased rice and vegetable production due to introduction of irrigation
items.zh: 由于灌溉的引入，水稻和蔬菜产量增加

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Yayoi divided among clans
items.zh: 弥生时代的人群分为各个氏族

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kofun period lasted from 250 to 538 CE; burial mounds; introduction of Shinto beliefs; kami
items.zh: 古坟时代从公元250年持续到538年；墓葬土丘；神道信仰的引入；神（kami）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Yamato clan establishes power in regions around present-day Kyoto, Nara, and Osaka
items.zh: 大和氏族在现今京都、奈良和大阪周边地区确立权势

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Emperor Kimmei, 539 to 571 CE; beginning of Asuka period
items.zh: 钦明天皇，公元539年至571年；飞鸟时代的开始

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Japanese emperors believed to be direct descendants of sun goddess, Amaterasu
items.zh: 日本天皇被认为是太阳女神天照大神的直接后裔

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Prince Shotoku ruled as regent when Empress Suiko was on throne
items.zh: 推古天皇在位时，圣德太子以摄政身份执政

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Well organized bureaucratic government cap system
items.zh: 组织严密的官僚政府；冠位制度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Emperors ruled from city of Nara from 710 to 794 CE
items.zh: 公元710年至794年间，天皇从奈良城进行统治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Emperor Shomu (724 to 749 CE), established Buddhist temple in every province in Japan
items.zh: 圣武天皇（公元724年至749年），在日本每个藩国建立佛教寺庙

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Heian period established major central rule at city now called Kyoto
items.zh: 平安时代在现今称为京都的城市建立了重要的中央统治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Heian nobility and cultural achievements including establishment of Japanese writing system; The Tale of Genji by Murasaki Shikibu
items.zh: 平安时代的贵族与文化成就，包括日本文字体系的建立；紫式部的《源氏物语》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Regional landlords raise private armies of warriors, called samurai
items.zh: 地方领主组建私人武士军队，称为武士（samurai）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Samurai bound to serve regional lords, called daimyo
items.zh: 武士必须效忠地方领主，称为大名（daimyo）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Genpei War (1180 to 1185 CE); clash between rival daimyo
items.zh: 源平合战（公元1180年至1185年）；敌对大名之间的冲突

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Minamoto Yoritomo declares himself shogun; Kamakura period, improvements to infrastructure
items.zh: 源赖朝自称征夷大将军（shogun）；镰仓时代，基础设施得到改善

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Samurai develop code of ethics and cultural practices known as bushido.
items.zh: 武士形成了被称为武士道（bushido）的道德准则和文化习俗。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tea ceremony and ink-brush calligraphy developed in this period
items.zh: 茶道和毛笔书法在这一时期发展起来

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mongols and dynastic changes
items.zh: 蒙古人与王朝更迭

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Japan entered warring states period between 1467 to 1615 CE; ongoing civil war
items.zh: 日本于公元1467年至1615年间进入战国时期；内战持续不断

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Portuguese trade; firearms; Christianity
items.zh: 葡萄牙贸易；火器；基督教

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tokugawa clan take power in early 1600s; ruled from Edo, present-day Tokyo
items.zh: 德川氏族于17世纪初掌权；从江户（今东京）进行统治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tokugawa shogunate closed off Japan to rest of world
items.zh: 德川幕府使日本与世界其他地区隔绝

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Modern country of Vietnam located on Indochinese peninsula
items.zh: 现代越南位于中南半岛（印度支那半岛）上

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Khmer ethnic group built an empire; Angkor Wat
items.zh: 高棉族建立了一个帝国；吴哥窟

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Khmer empire ended when capital Angkor captured by Thai people in 1432 CE
items.zh: 公元1432年，都城吴哥被泰族人攻占，高棉帝国灭亡

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: 1350 CE, Thai kingdom called Ayutthaya rose to power; capital Bangkok
items.zh: 公元1350年，名为阿瑜陀耶的泰国王国崛起；首都曼谷

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ayutthaya kingdom ruled over large area of Southeast Asia for four centuries
items.zh: 阿瑜陀耶王国统治东南亚大片地区达四个世纪

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Malay people emerged in Malay peninsula, now modern country of Indonesia; eventually rule of Java and Sumatra Timeline
items.zh: 马来人出现在马来半岛，即今印度尼西亚所在地；最终统治了爪哇和苏门答腊 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Continent of Europe
items.zh: 欧洲大陆

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Russia
items.zh: 俄罗斯

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Atlantic Ocean, Mediterranean Sea
items.zh: 大西洋、地中海

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Middle East; north Africa
items.zh: 中东；北非

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Eastern Europe
items.zh: 东欧

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Moscow
items.zh: 莫斯科

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Novgorod and Kyiv
items.zh: 诺夫哥罗德和基辅

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Dnieper River
items.zh: 第聂伯河

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Also called the medieval period, the Middle Ages lasted from about 500 CE to 1500 CE
items.zh: 中世纪又称中古时期，大约从公元500年延续到公元1500年

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The term Middle Ages designates an era of European history between the classical period of ancient Greece and Rome and the Renaissance
items.zh: “中世纪”一词指欧洲历史上介于古希腊罗马古典时期与文艺复兴之间的时代

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Historians generally break the Middle Ages into three periods: the early Middle Ages (500 CE to 1000 CE), the High Middle Ages (1000 CE to 1300 CE), and the late Middle Ages (1300 CE to 1500 CE)
items.zh: 历史学家一般将中世纪分为三个时期：早期中世纪（公元500年至1000年）、盛期中世纪（公元1000年至1300年）和晚期中世纪（公元1300年至1500年）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Aristocracy originated from Roman nobles
items.zh: 贵族阶层起源于罗马的贵族

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Aristocratic status was largely hereditary.
items.zh: 贵族身份基本上是世袭的。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Aristocracy held most of the land, and virtually all military and political power.
items.zh: 贵族占有大部分土地，并几乎掌握了全部军事和政治权力。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Roman Empire had established many aspects of social structure which largely fell apart after fall of Rome
items.zh: 罗马帝国确立的社会结构在许多方面于罗马灭亡后基本瓦解

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Groups such as the Alemanni, Franks, Angles, Saxons, Vandals, Visigoths, and others began to migrate into the empire’s territory in the third century CE, establishing their own regional cultures.
items.zh: 公元三世纪，阿勒曼尼人、法兰克人、盎格鲁人、撒克逊人、汪达尔人、西哥特人等部落开始迁入帝国领土，建立起自己的地域文化。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: With the decline of the Western Roman Empire, the only European-wide system was the Christian Church.
items.zh: 随着西罗马帝国的衰落，基督教教会成为全欧洲唯一的广泛体系。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Constantine made Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire in 380 CE.
items.zh: 公元380年，君士坦丁将基督教定为罗马帝国的国教。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Most important bishop within the hierarchy of the Church was the bishop of Rome (pope).
items.zh: 教会等级体系中最重要的主教是罗马主教（教皇）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In the eighth century CE, the kingdom of the Franks was one of the strongest in Europe; one of its kings rose to power—Charles the Great or Charlemagne.
items.zh: 公元八世纪，法兰克王国是欧洲最强大的王国之一；其一位国王崛起掌权——即查理大帝（查理曼）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Under Charlemagne, monastic libraries grew.
items.zh: 在查理曼统治下，修道院图书馆得到了发展。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Growth of Charlemagne’s empire
items.zh: 查理曼帝国的扩张

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Parts of Charlemagne’s lands eventually became lands of Germany and France.
items.zh: 查理曼的部分领土最终成为德国和法国的土地。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New period of greater calm began in Europe in 1000 CE.
items.zh: 公元1000年，欧洲开始了一段更为安定的新时期。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Population increased, as did life expectancy.
items.zh: 人口增长，预期寿命也提高了。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Growth of towns and economy
items.zh: 城镇与经济的发展

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: High Middle Ages saw development of organized feudal system
items.zh: 盛期中世纪出现了有组织的封建制度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Feudalism evolved into complex hierarchy dominated by royals and nobles
items.zh: 封建制度演变为由王室和贵族主导的复杂等级体系

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Europe was politically divided into kingdoms (ruled by a king) and principalities (ruled by a prince, duke, or count).
items.zh: 欧洲在政治上分为王国（由国王统治）和公国（由亲王、公爵或伯爵统治）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Gatherings of political advisors evolved into parliaments.
items.zh: 政治顾问的集会逐渐演变为议会。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Bond of loyalty a defining feature of feudalism
items.zh: 忠诚的纽带是封建制度的一个决定性特征

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Distribution of land, and expansion of agricultural lands
items.zh: 土地的分配与农业用地的扩张

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Development of a new plow, and changing farming methods; three-field rotation
items.zh: 新式犁的发明与耕作方法的改变；三圃轮作制

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Military structure of the High Middle Ages dominated by mounted, armored knights and infantry
items.zh: 盛期中世纪的军事结构以骑马披甲的骑士和步兵为主

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Castle strongholds
items.zh: 城堡要塞

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The English introduced longbows into warfare.
items.zh: 英格兰人将长弓引入战争。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Introduction of gunpowder
items.zh: 火药的引入

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By the end of the thirteenth century there were over a dozen universities in Europe.
items.zh: 到十三世纪末，欧洲已有十几所大学。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: A manor was a rural, self-contained farming unit.
items.zh: 庄园是一个自给自足的乡村农业单位。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Peasants worked on the manorial lands and were bound to the manorial lands by contract
items.zh: 农民在庄园土地上劳作，并通过契约被束缚于庄园土地

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Peasants had little social power (serfs).
items.zh: 农民几乎没有社会权力（农奴）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Inhabited by trades people, artisans, craftspeople
items.zh: 居住着商人、工匠和手艺人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By 1100s, many towns had established guilds.
items.zh: 到12世纪，许多城镇已建立了行会。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Apprenticeship system
items.zh: 学徒制

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Merchants and expanded trade links across Europe
items.zh: 商人与遍及欧洲的贸易网络的扩展

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Silk road continued to be an important trade route for goods and ideas.
items.zh: 丝绸之路仍然是货物与思想交流的重要贸易路线。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Church reached its greatest influence in the High Middle Ages.
items.zh: 教会在盛期中世纪达到了最大的影响力。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nearly everyone’s life revolved around the Church.
items.zh: 几乎所有人的生活都围绕着教会展开。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Clergy were the main source of education and held great social and political power.
items.zh: 神职人员是教育的主要来源，并拥有巨大的社会和政治权力。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Church architecture began to change during this period; abbey church of Saint-Denis
items.zh: 这一时期教会建筑开始发生变化；圣但尼修道院教堂

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mechanical clock developed for the Church in second half of thirteenth century
items.zh: 十三世纪下半叶为教会研制了机械钟

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In High Middle Ages Europeans had expanded interest in the Holy Land.
items.zh: 盛期中世纪，欧洲人对圣地的兴趣日益增加。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rise of Islam
items.zh: 伊斯兰教的兴起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1096 CE, the pope called for a crusade to take back the Holy Land for Christianity.
items.zh: 公元1096年，教皇号召发动十字军东征，为基督教夺回圣地。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Christians captured Jerusalem in 1099 CE.
items.zh: 公元1099年，基督徒攻占了耶路撒冷。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Knights Templars were a Christian military order founded around 1118 CE.
items.zh: 圣殿骑士团是约公元1118年成立的基督教军事修会。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Europe’s population began to slow around 1300 CE.
items.zh: 公元1300年前后，欧洲人口增长开始放缓。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Crop failure, famine, and population decline
items.zh: 庄稼歉收、饥荒与人口下降

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Black Death, 1347 CE; drastic decline in population
items.zh: 黑死病，公元1347年；人口急剧下降

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Social and Political upheaval
items.zh: 社会与政治动荡

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hundred Year’s War (1337–1453 CE); Peasant’s Revolt, 1381 CE
items.zh: 百年战争（公元1337–1453年）；农民起义，公元1381年

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: System of feudalism began to decline.
items.zh: 封建制度开始衰落。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Johannes Gutenberg printing press 1440 CE
items.zh: 约翰内斯·古腾堡印刷机，公元1440年

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Some of the patterns that defined medieval Europe were also part of medieval Russia, but there were ways in which Russia was quite different.
items.zh: 定义中世纪欧洲的一些模式也存在于中世纪俄罗斯，但俄罗斯在某些方面截然不同。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: While many peoples lived in the region in and around Russia, the Slavs and the Rus were two groups that became important.
items.zh: 虽然有许多民族生活在俄罗斯及其周边地区，但斯拉夫人和罗斯人成为两个重要的族群。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Byzantine missionaries brought Christianity to Russia around 900 CE.
items.zh: 公元900年前后，拜占庭传教士将基督教带入俄罗斯。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By the eleventh century Russia incorporated more long-distance trade than the West, and the cultural touchstones of art, literature, and architecture were more developed.
items.zh: 到十一世纪，俄罗斯的长途贸易比西方更为发达，艺术、文学和建筑等文化标志也更成熟。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mongols defeated Rus in 1223 CE.
items.zh: 公元1223年，蒙古人击败了罗斯人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mongols created the largest contiguous empire the world has ever known.
items.zh: 蒙古人建立了有史以来最大的连绵帝国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus in 1223 CE left Russia with only a few small areas, such as Novgorod, remaining outside of Mongol control.
items.zh: 公元1223年蒙古人入侵基辅罗斯，使俄罗斯仅剩下诺夫哥罗德等少数小地区未受蒙古控制。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The prince of Novgorod, Alexander Nevsky, maintained independence by negotiating with the Mongols. From this arose a new country, the Grand Principality of Moscow, or Muscovy.
items.zh: 诺夫哥罗德公爵亚历山大·涅夫斯基通过与蒙古人谈判维持了独立。由此产生了一个新的国家——莫斯科大公国（Muscovy）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: A strong ruler named Ivan became the grand prince of Muscovy in 1462 CE (Ivan the Great).
items.zh: 公元1462年，一位强有力的统治者伊凡成为莫斯科大公国的君主（伊凡大帝）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ivan the Great demonstrated military and political strength; developed strong central government; foundations of modern Russia
items.zh: 伊凡大帝展现出军事和政治实力；建立了强大的中央政府；奠定了现代俄罗斯的基础

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Continent of Africa
items.zh: 非洲大陆

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Great diversity of climate and geographical zones across the continent of Africa including grassy savannas
items.zh: 非洲大陆气候和地理区域极为多样，包括草木茂盛的热带稀树草原

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Mediterranean Sea, Red Sea
items.zh: 大西洋、印度洋、地中海、红海

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Middle East
items.zh: 中东

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sahara Desert; Kalahari Desert; Sahel
items.zh: 撒哈拉沙漠；卡拉哈里沙漠；萨赫勒地区

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sinai Peninsula
items.zh: 西奈半岛

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nile, Niger, and Congo Rivers
items.zh: 尼罗河、尼日尔河和刚果河

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Atlas Mountains
items.zh: 阿特拉斯山脉

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mount Kilimanjaro
items.zh: 乞力马扎罗山

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Madagascar (fourth largest island on earth) B. Background The vast continent of Africa has a great diversity of landscapes, resources, and cultures. Between the sixth and sixteenth centuries CE, several civilizations in North and West Africa served as important centers of trade and cultural exchange. The three great West African empires of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai rose to power in part because they controlled gold mines, salt mines, and the trade routes that linked these valuable resources to the rest of the world.
items.zh: 马达加斯加（世界第四大岛）B. 背景 广袤的非洲大陆拥有极其多样的景观、资源和文化。公元六世纪至十六世纪间，北非和西非的若干文明成为重要的贸易与文化交流中心。西非三大帝国——加纳、马里和桑海——之所以崛起，部分原因在于它们控制了金矿、盐矿以及将这些宝贵资源与世界其他地区连接起来的贸易路线。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Several African civilizations enjoyed incredible prosperity, growing trade, and cross cultural connections.
items.zh: 一些非洲文明享有令人难以置信的繁荣、不断增长的贸易以及跨文化联系。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: This growth was helped by greater contact between Africans and the empires that ruled the regions surrounding Africa.
items.zh: 这种增长得益于非洲人与统治非洲周边地区的帝国之间更密切的接触。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spread of Christianity and Islam
items.zh: 基督教与伊斯兰教的传播

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Trans-Saharan trade fueled the rise of three mighty empires in West Africa. The Ghana, Mali, and Songhai Empires emerged in succession between the 400s and the 1400s CE
items.zh: 跨撒哈拉贸易推动了西非三个强大帝国的崛起。加纳、马里和桑海帝国在公元5世纪至15世纪间相继出现

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: West Africa was an important regional trade center that connected different parts of Africa as well as China, India, Arabia, and Europe
items.zh: 西非是重要的区域贸易中心，连接非洲不同地区以及中国、印度、阿拉伯和欧洲。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Each of the three empires benefited from the region’s deposits of gold and salt
items.zh: 这三个帝国都受益于该地区的金矿和盐矿资源

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Situated south of the Sahara in the relatively less arid region of the Sahel, the Ghana Empire began as a regional kingdom of the Soninke people, who were part of a larger ethnic and language group called the Mande. Timeline
items.zh: 加纳帝国位于撒哈拉以南相对干旱程度较低的萨赫勒地区，最初是索宁克人的一个地区性王国，索宁克人属于一个更大的族群和语言群体——曼德人。时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Most of what is known about the Ghana Empire has been passed down through either oral tradition or texts written by Arab merchants.
items.zh: 关于加纳帝国的大多数已知信息，都是通过口述传统或阿拉伯商人撰写的文献流传下来的。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: It is likely that the main city was Koumbi Saleh (located in present-day Mauritania), which was home to thousands of people.
items.zh: 其主要城市很可能是库姆比萨莱赫（位于今天的毛里塔尼亚），那里居住着数千人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The people of the Ghana Empire originally practiced an animist religion, as was common throughout West Africa.
items.zh: 加纳帝国的人民最初信奉万物有灵论宗教，这在整个西非都很常见。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: As Islamic civilization began to spread in the 700s CE, more and more Muslim merchants, diplomats, and others made their way to the Ghana Empire.
items.zh: 随着伊斯兰文明在公元8世纪开始传播，越来越多的穆斯林商人、外交官和其他人来到加纳帝国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By the end of the twelfth century CE, the Ghana Empire was an Islamic society.
items.zh: 到十二世纪末，加纳帝国已成为一个伊斯兰社会。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Conflict with various external groups weakened the empire, as did a change in climate and weather patterns.
items.zh: 与各种外部群体的冲突削弱了帝国，气候和天气模式的变化也造成了同样的后果。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rise of West African kingdom of Mali began in 1235 CE when Mandinka leader called Sundiata Keita (Lion Prince or Hungering Prince) became the mansa, or emperor
items.zh: 西非马里王国的崛起始于公元1235年，当时曼丁卡人领袖松迪亚塔·凯塔（狮子王子或饥饿王子）成为“曼萨”（即皇帝）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sundiata Keita fortified trade routes and took control of the gold mines.
items.zh: 松迪亚塔·凯塔加固了贸易路线并控制了金矿。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: City of Timbuktu became an important cosmopolitan center of the Mali Empire.
items.zh: 廷巴克图城成为马里帝国重要的国际化中心。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mali Empire taxed the goods that came through Timbuktu and their other cities
items.zh: 马里帝国对经过廷巴克图及其他城市的货物征税

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Most powerful ruler of the Mali Empire was Mansa Musa, who reigned from 1312 to 1337 CE; doubled size of the empire; became one of the richest men in the world
items.zh: 马里帝国最强大的统治者是曼萨·穆萨，他在公元1312年至1337年在位；使帝国面积扩大了一倍；成为世界上最富有的人之一

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Around 1324 CE, Mansa Musa undertook a pilgrimage to Mecca.
items.zh: 约公元1324年，曼萨·穆萨前往麦加朝圣。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mansa Musa supported the construction of mosques, Islamic schools, libraries, and universities.
items.zh: 曼萨·穆萨支持修建清真寺、伊斯兰学校、图书馆和大学。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: A combination of factors led to the eventual decline of Mali’s power. F. Songhai Empire: Background The vast continent of Africa has a great diversity of landscapes, resources, and cultures. Between the sixth and sixteenth centuries CE, several civilizations in North and West Africa served as important centers of trade and cultural exchange. The three great West African empires of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai rose to power in part because they controlled gold mines, salt mines, and the trade routes that linked these valuable resources to the rest of the world.
items.zh: 多种因素共同导致了马里势力的最终衰落。F. 桑海帝国：背景 广袤的非洲大陆拥有极其多样的景观、资源和文化。公元六世纪至十六世纪间，北非和西非的若干文明成为重要的贸易与文化交流中心。西非三大帝国——加纳、马里和桑海——之所以崛起，部分原因在于它们控制了金矿、盐矿以及将这些宝贵资源与世界其他地区连接起来的贸易路线。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Songhai kings attacked and raided Mali cities.
items.zh: 桑海国王们袭击并劫掠了马里的城市。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: One king, named Sunni Ali, used his strong army and naval force to control travel on the Niger.
items.zh: 一位名叫桑尼·阿里的国王利用其强大的陆军和水军控制了尼日尔河上的通行。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By 1468, Sunni Ali had conquered most of the territory once held by the Mali Empire.
items.zh: 到1468年，桑尼·阿里已征服了曾属于马里帝国的大部分领土。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By 1500, the Songhai Empire stretched even farther to the north and east than Mali had.
items.zh: 到1500年，桑海帝国的疆域向北和向东延伸得比马里还要远。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Askia Muhammad, the first Songhai emperor, developed more trade with Asia and Europe.
items.zh: 桑海第一位皇帝阿斯基亚·穆罕默德发展了与亚洲和欧洲的更多贸易。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Askia Muhammad sought to increase the influence of Islam in the empire; he supported the building of mosques and brought many Arab scholars to the university in Timbuktu, which created a golden age of learning in the region.
items.zh: 阿斯基亚·穆罕默德力图扩大伊斯兰教在帝国中的影响力；他支持修建清真寺，并将许多阿拉伯学者带到廷巴克图的大学，从而在该地区创造了学术的黄金时代。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Tomb of Askia, a grand structure that is part of the Great Mosque of Gao, is said to be his place of burial. It is the largest historical monument in West Africa.
items.zh: 阿斯基亚陵墓是一座宏伟的建筑，属于加奥大清真寺的一部分，据说是他的安葬之地。它是西非最大的历史古迹。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In the late 1500s, internal strife, drought, and disease began to fray the Songhai Empire.
items.zh: 16世纪后期，内乱、干旱和疾病开始削弱桑海帝国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New influences entered West Africa as Portuguese and other European traders and explorers gained the ability to travel to the region in the 1400s.
items.zh: 15世纪，葡萄牙和其他欧洲商人与探险家获得了前往该地区的能力，新的影响力随之进入西非。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The arrival of Europeans changed the form and scale of the African slave trade.
items.zh: 欧洲人的到来改变了非洲奴隶贸易的形式和规模。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Portuguese explorers and traders began to set up trading posts on the African coast in the 1440s.
items.zh: 15世纪40年代，葡萄牙探险家和商人开始在非洲海岸设立贸易站。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Portuguese traded in goods that the local trading networks produced; included trade of enslaved people
items.zh: 葡萄牙人交易当地贸易网络生产的商品；包括奴隶贸易

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: A geographer and avid traveler, Ibn Battuta was a fourteenth-century Muslim scholar from Morocco; his travels in West Africa took place from 1349 to 1354 CE.
items.zh: 伊本·白图泰是一位地理学家和热衷的旅行者，是来自摩洛哥的14世纪穆斯林学者；他在西非的旅行发生在公元1349年至1354年。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: He wrote detailed accounts about his experiences and drew maps of his voyages.
items.zh: 他详细记录了自己的经历，并绘制了旅行地图。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: Griots are important figures in West African cultures.
items.zh: 格里奥特（说书人）是西非文化中的重要人物。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: Griots serve as historians, genealogists, storytellers, poets, musicians, praise singers, and authority figures.
items.zh: 格里奥特充当历史学家、谱系学家、说书人、诗人、音乐家、赞颂歌手和权威人物。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: The role of griot was hereditary and a position of honor.
items.zh: 格里奥特的角色是世袭的，也是受人尊敬的职位。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: Griots told social and family histories that were passed down from one generation to the next through stories and songs.
items.zh: 格里奥特讲述社会史和家族史，这些历史通过故事和歌曲代代相传。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: Instruments such as the kora (similar to a harp) and the balafon (similar to a xylophone) accompanied the words and lyrics.
items.zh: 科拉琴（类似竖琴）和巴拉丰琴（类似木琴）等乐器为说唱和歌词伴奏。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: The tale of Sundiata Keita was preserved by griots for centuries.
items.zh: 松迪亚塔·凯塔的故事由格里奥特保存了数百年。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Ibn Battuta, Griots and Oral Traditions
items.en: Griots also functioned as record keepers for births, deaths, and marriages.
items.zh: 格里奥特还负责记录出生、死亡和婚姻。

items.en: Europe
items.zh: 欧洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Africa
items.zh: 非洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Asia
items.zh: 亚洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Arabia
items.zh: 阿拉伯

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Persia
items.zh: 波斯

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spain, Italy, England
items.zh: 西班牙、意大利、英格兰

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Atlantic Ocean, Mediterranean Sea, Arabian Sea, Adriatic Sea B. Background The word Renaissance means rebirth. It is used to describe the years 1300 to 1600 CE in Italy and 1450 to 1650 CE in northern Europe. This era was a “rebirth” because it involved the rediscovery of things learned in centuries past, particularly in ancient Greece and Rome. The government of the Western Roman Empire fell apart in the fifth century CE. Its education system also collapsed. The new rulers of western Europe were warriors and warlords. After the fall of Rome, western Europe fell out of contact with the Greek speaking Eastern Roman Empire. Greek was read and spoken less and less in the western part of the empire, and the knowledge of many subjects formerly taught in Greek faded. The Catholic Church was the main institution that survived the fall of Rome, and learning was preserved by Catholic monks in monasteries. By the twelfth century, the increasing wealth and power of European kingdoms had led to a new demand for learning.
items.zh: 大西洋、地中海、阿拉伯海、亚得里亚海 B. 背景 “文艺复兴”一词意为“重生”。它用来描述意大利公元1300年至1600年以及北欧公元1450年至1650年的时期。这个时代之所以被称为“重生”，是因为它涉及对过去几个世纪所学知识的重新发现，尤其是古希腊和罗马的知识。西罗马帝国的政府在公元五世纪垮台，其教育体系也随之崩溃。西欧新的统治者是武士和军阀。罗马灭亡后，西欧与讲希腊语的东罗马帝国失去联系。希腊语在帝国西部被阅读和使用的越来越少，许多过去用希腊语教授的学科知识逐渐失传。天主教会是罗马灭亡后幸存下来的主要机构，知识由修道院中的天主教修士保存下来。到十二世纪，欧洲王国日益增长的财富和权力引发了对知识的新需求。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Monks in western Europe had preserved Latin writing; Greek texts were copied, read, and studied widely in areas under Muslim rule.
items.zh: 西欧的修士保存了拉丁文著作；在穆斯林统治的地区，希腊文献被广泛抄写、阅读和研究。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Followers of Islam conquered most of the Eastern Roman Empire in the seventh and eighth centuries CE; they absorbed the Greek-speaking upper class of East Rome.
items.zh: 公元七、八世纪，伊斯兰教信徒征服了东罗马帝国的大部分地区；他们吸纳了东罗马讲希腊语的上层阶级。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muslims prized Greek texts for their contributions to medicine, philosophy, and science. Schools flourished for centuries in the Islamic Middle East, North Africa, and Iberia.
items.zh: 穆斯林珍视希腊文献，因为它们对医学、哲学和科学做出了贡献。学校在伊斯兰中东、北非和伊比利亚繁荣了数百年。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muslim scholars translated the writings of Aristotle, Euclid, Ptolemy, and more into Arabic.
items.zh: 穆斯林学者将亚里士多德、欧几里得、托勒密等人的著作翻译成阿拉伯语。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Muslim scholars also wrote new works that advanced knowledge beyond that of the Greeks. Timeline
items.zh: 穆斯林学者还撰写了新的著作，将知识推进到超越希腊人的水平。时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: European scholars traveled to places such as Córdoba in search of Greek texts; also impressed and influenced by Muslim thinkers and their texts
items.zh: 欧洲学者前往科尔多瓦等地寻找希腊文献；同时也受到穆斯林思想家及其著作的打动和影响

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: European scholars brought texts from the Muslim world to European centers of learning (universities).
items.zh: 欧洲学者将穆斯林世界的文献带回欧洲的学术中心（大学）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Europe’s economy had begun to grow quickly during the eleventh century. Italian cities, especially the port cities of Venice and Genoa, were among the first to display this new wealth, which came from trade.
items.zh: 11世纪，欧洲经济开始快速增长。意大利的城市，尤其是威尼斯和热那亚等港口城市，最先展现出这种来自贸易的新财富。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Italy comprised of several kingdoms or states; each Italian city had its own government
items.zh: 意大利由若干王国或城邦组成；每个意大利城市都有自己的政府

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Trade caused more Italian cities to grow. Florence began to produce high-quality woolen fabric, often using wool from English sheep; rise of merchant class
items.zh: 贸易促使更多意大利城市成长。佛罗伦萨开始生产高质量的羊毛织物，通常使用英国绵羊的羊毛；商人阶层崛起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Venetians excelled in trade; dominated ports of eastern and southern Mediterranean Sea
items.zh: 威尼斯人擅长贸易，主导了地中海东部和南部的港口。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Florence developed an international trade in woolen cloth.
items.zh: 佛罗伦萨发展了毛织品的国际贸易。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Florentines and other Italian bankers developed international banking networks.
items.zh: 佛罗伦萨人和其他意大利银行家建立了国际银行业网络。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Guilds were organizations formed by skilled laborers called artisans. The guilds of Florence were wealthy and influential.
items.zh: 行会是由被称为工匠的熟练劳动者组成的组织。佛罗伦萨的行会富有且有影响力。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rome remained capital of the Catholic Church administration; papacy was part of European politics
items.zh: 罗马仍是天主教会行政中心；教皇制度是欧洲政治的一部分。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Italy was the home of a new movement in literature and learning that transformed European thought.
items.zh: 意大利是一场改变欧洲思想的文学与学术新运动的发源地。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Humanists began reading, collecting, and translating ancient Greek texts. Works by Homer, Sophocles, Thucydides, and more became more available to readers across Europe.
items.zh: 人文主义者开始阅读、收集和翻译古希腊文献。荷马、索福克勒斯、修昔底德等人的作品逐渐为全欧洲的读者所更易获得。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Francis Petrarch (1304–74) was an important early humanist.
items.zh: 弗朗西斯·彼特拉克（1304–1374）是一位重要的早期人文主义者。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Humanist study of languages extended to Hebrew and, by the late fifteenth century, included new scholarship on the Bible.
items.zh: 人文主义者的语言研究扩展到希伯来语，到十五世纪末，还包括对《圣经》的新研究。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Renaissance is famous for its artistic developments, which were the product of wealth and growth in the Italian cities.
items.zh: 文艺复兴以其艺术成就而闻名，这些成就是意大利城市财富与发展的产物。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Humanists influenced the development of new architectural styles based on ancient buildings.
items.zh: 人文主义者影响了基于古代建筑的新建筑风格的发展。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Painters of this era worked in shops and were members of guilds; learned by working as apprentices to a master painter
items.zh: 这一时期的画家在作坊里工作，并且是行会成员；通过给大师画家当学徒来学习

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Introduction of perspective in art
items.zh: 艺术中透视法的引入

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Banking made Cosimo de’ Medici (1389–1464) the wealthiest and most powerful man in Florence.
items.zh: 银行业使科西莫·德·美第奇（1389–1464）成为佛罗伦萨最富有、最有权势的人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Medici family dominated politics in Florence
items.zh: 美第奇家族主导了佛罗伦萨的政治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Cosimo de’ Medici (1389–1464) a patron of the arts
items.zh: 科西莫·德·美第奇（1389–1464），艺术赞助人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Lorenzo de’ Medici (1449–1492) patron to Sandro Botticelli (1445–1510), Andrea del Verrocchio (1435–88), Michelangelo Buonarotti (1475–1564), and Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519)
items.zh: 洛伦佐·德·美第奇（1449–1492）是桑德罗·波提切利（1445–1510）、安德烈亚·德尔·韦罗基奥（1435–1488）、米开朗基罗·博纳罗蒂（1475–1564）和列奥纳多·达·芬奇（1452–1519）的赞助人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Last Supper, Mona Lisa
items.zh: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇创作了《最后的晚餐》和《蒙娜丽莎》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Michelangelo Buonarroti (1475–1564) carved the Pietà and marble statue of David
items.zh: 米开朗基罗·博纳罗蒂（1475–1564）雕刻了《圣殇》和大理石雕像《大卫》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Niccolò Machiavelli (1469–1527) known for his work the The Prince
items.zh: 尼可罗·马基雅维利（1469–1527）以其著作《君主论》而闻名

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Johannes Gutenberg (d. 1468), a German goldsmith by trade, began to print with movable type during the 1440s.
items.zh: 约翰内斯·古腾堡（卒于1468年）是一位德国金匠，于15世纪40年代开始使用活字印刷。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The new printing process spread quickly to other cities; humanists welcomed the chance to print copies of ancient texts.
items.zh: 新的印刷工艺迅速传播到其他城市；人文主义者欣然接受印刷古籍副本的机会。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Printing made all types of writing available to more people and enabled writers to profit from book sales.
items.zh: 印刷术使各类著作能为更多人所获得，并使作家能够从图书销售中获利。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The most famous and influential religious reformer was Martin Luther (1483–1546); challenged the Roman Catholic Church
items.zh: 最著名、最有影响力的宗教改革家是马丁·路德（1483–1546）；他挑战了罗马天主教会

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Luther composed a list of ninety-five disagreements with Church doctrine (ninety-five theses); attached to church door October, 1517
items.zh: 路德列出了对教会教义的九十五条异议（九十五条论纲）；于1517年10月将其贴在教堂门上

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Luther condemned by Catholic Church as a heretic, someone who preaches heresy, in 1521
items.zh: 1521年，路德被天主教会谴责为异端，即宣扬异端邪说的人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Luther translated the New Testament into German and wrote works that were printed and widely read.
items.zh: 路德将《新约》翻译成德语，并撰写了被印刷且广为阅读的著作。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Some of the princes who ruled areas of the Holy Roman Empire supported Luther’s reforms.
items.zh: 统治神圣罗马帝国部分地区的一些诸侯支持路德的改革。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In the cities of northern Europe, other religious leaders preached reform and sought to change their regional church practices with the help of their local governments.
items.zh: 在北欧的城市中，其他宗教领袖宣扬改革，并寻求在当地政府的帮助下改变本地区的教会习俗。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: John Calvin (1509–64) was the most important of the next generation of reformers.
items.zh: 约翰·加尔文（1509–1564）是下一代改革家中最重要的一位。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Era in which European religion was dominated by a single united church was over, allowing dozens of religious beliefs to emerge.
items.zh: 欧洲宗教由单一统一教会主导的时代结束了，使得数十种宗教信仰得以出现。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: During and after the Reformation, periods of unrest and violence ensued.
items.zh: 在宗教改革期间及之后，出现了动荡和暴力的时期。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Each Christian group often viewed others as heretical
items.zh: 每个基督教团体常常将其他团体视为异端

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In order to obtain a divorce, Catholic monarch Henry VIII of England, declared himself head of the Church of England; Protestantism arose in England.
items.zh: 为了获得离婚许可，英格兰的天主教君主亨利八世宣布自己为英格兰教会的领袖；新教由此在英格兰兴起。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: As part of his reforms, Henry VIII dissolved England’s monasteries and seized Church land and wealth.
items.zh: 作为改革的一部分，亨利八世解散了英格兰的修道院，并没收了教会的土地和财富。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Astronomer and physicist, Galileo Galilei (1564–1642), supported theories held by Nicolaus Copernicus (1473–1543); confirming the Sun, not the Earth at the center of Solar System, conflicting with Roman theologians
items.zh: 天文学家和物理学家伽利略·伽利雷（1564–1642）支持尼古拉·哥白尼（1473–1543）的理论；证实太阳而非地球处于太阳系中心，与罗马神学家发生冲突

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Roman court condemned Galileo
items.zh: 罗马法庭谴责了伽利略

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Europe
items.zh: 欧洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Portugal
items.zh: 葡萄牙

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spain
items.zh: 西班牙

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: England
items.zh: 英格兰

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: France
items.zh: 法国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Netherlands
items.zh: 荷兰

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Africa
items.zh: 非洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mozambique, Kenya, Somalia
items.zh: 莫桑比克、肯尼亚、索马里

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Asia
items.zh: 亚洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: India
items.zh: 印度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Indonesia
items.zh: 印度尼西亚

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Malaysia
items.zh: 马来西亚

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tawain
items.zh: 台湾

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: South America, Brazil
items.zh: 南美洲，巴西

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: North America
items.zh: 北美洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mexico
items.zh: 墨西哥

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Bolivia
items.zh: 玻利维亚

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Isthmus of Panama
items.zh: 巴拿马地峡

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Atlantic Ocean, Pacific Ocean, Indian Ocean
items.zh: 大西洋、太平洋、印度洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Congo River
items.zh: 刚果河

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Cape of Good Hope
items.zh: 好望角

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The age of exploration that began in the 1400s is also sometimes called the age of sail.
items.zh: 始于15世纪的探索时代有时也被称为帆船时代。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New sailing ships (carrack, caravel) and advances in navigational technologies (compass) enabled explorers and traders to cross ever greater distances on the sea.
items.zh: 新型帆船（克拉克帆船、卡拉维尔帆船）和航海技术（指南针）的进步使探险家和商人能够在海上跨越越来越远的距离。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Portuguese were some of the most successful early European explorers; Henry the Navigator
items.zh: 葡萄牙人是最成功的早期欧洲探险者之一；航海家亨利。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Portuguese in search of sea route to China; explored coasts of Africa
items.zh: 葡萄牙人寻找通往中国的海上路线；探索了非洲海岸

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Portuguese outposts or colonies in parts of Africa; enslavement of Africans
items.zh: 葡萄牙在非洲部分地区的据点或殖民地；奴役非洲人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Bartolomeu Dias, first European to find and pass the Cape of Good Hope, the southern tip of the African continent; his expedition establishes way east to India and Cathay (China) by navigating around Africa
items.zh: 巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士，第一位发现并绕过非洲大陆南端好望角的欧洲人；他的探险开辟了绕行非洲向东前往印度和契丹（中国）的航路

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Vasco da Gama explored East Africa; arrived in Calicut, India, in 1498; Pedro Álvares Cabral follows, opens up trade in India for the Portuguese; aim to gain Portuguese control of all trade in the Indian Ocean
items.zh: 瓦斯科·达·伽马探索了东非；1498年抵达印度卡利卡特；佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔随后前往，为葡萄牙人开辟了在印度的贸易；目标是让葡萄牙控制印度洋的所有贸易

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Portuguese claim Brazil in South America.
items.zh: 葡萄牙宣称对南美洲的巴西拥有主权。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In search of Eastern sea route, Columbus sails west with three ships in 1492; Niña, the Santa Maria, and the Pinta
items.zh: 为寻找通往东方的海上航线，哥伦布于1492年率三艘船向西航行：尼尼亚号、圣玛丽亚号和平塔号。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Columbus landed on an island called Ayti—the root of the modern name Haiti; indigenous people—the Taino; Columbus assumes he is in or near India
items.zh: 哥伦布登上一个名为“艾蒂”的岛屿——这是现代名称“海地”的词源；当地原住民是泰诺人；哥伦布以为自己身处印度或印度附近

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spanish monarchs Ferdinand and Isabella declare sovereignty over lands and resources in the Americas.
items.zh: 西班牙君主斐迪南和伊莎贝拉宣布对美洲的土地和资源拥有主权。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1494, Spanish and Portuguese representatives met at the city of Tordesillas in Spain to divide the ‘new world’ between themselves; the Treaty of Tordesillas declared that everything to the west of a line drawn at the Cape Verde Islands belonged to Spain and everything to the east belonged to Portugal; treaty later amended to make Portugal’s claim to Brazil official
items.zh: 1494年，西班牙和葡萄牙代表在西班牙的托德西利亚斯城会面，瓜分“新世界”；《托德西利亚斯条约》宣布，以佛得角群岛为界所划定的线以西的一切归西班牙，以东的一切归葡萄牙；该条约后来经过修订，使葡萄牙对巴西的诉求正式化

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Spanish secure and extend control over further lands in the Americas; enslavement of indigenous peoples; European diseases devastate indigenous populations
items.zh: 西班牙确保并扩大对美洲更多土地的控制；奴役原住民；欧洲疾病使原住民人口锐减

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: First stable settlement on the South American continent, Santa María de la Antigua, established in the Isthmus of Panama by Vasco Núñez de Balboa
items.zh: 南美洲大陆上第一个稳定的定居点——圣玛丽亚·德·拉·安提瓜，由巴斯克·努涅斯·德·巴尔沃亚在巴拿马地峡建立

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hernán Cortés expedition to Mexico; brutal campaign, defeated the Aztec rulers, conquered capital of Tenochtitlán
items.zh: 埃尔南·科尔特斯远征墨西哥；通过残酷的战役击败了阿兹特克统治者，征服了首都特诺奇蒂特兰

items.subject: History and Geography
