items.en: Inca Empire of the Andes invaded and conquered by the Pizarro brothers; Conquistadors
items.zh: 安第斯山脉的印加帝国被皮萨罗兄弟入侵并征服；征服者（Conquistadors）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Exploitation of natural resources (silver, gold) in the Americas
items.zh: 开发美洲的自然资源（白银、黄金）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Bartolomé de Las Casas denounces abuse of indigenous populations in the Americas by Spanish; King Charles V of Spain enacts the New Laws of the Indies for the Good Treatment and Preservation of Indians
items.zh: 巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯谴责西班牙人对美洲原住民的虐待；西班牙国王查理五世颁布《关于善待和保全印第安人的西印度新法律》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Portuguese explorer, Fernão de Magalhães, or Ferdinand Magellan, led the first expedition (1519–1521) that successfully circumnavigated the globe.
items.zh: 葡萄牙探险家费尔南·德·麦哲伦（即斐迪南·麦哲伦）率领了第一支成功环球航行的探险队（1519–1521）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: England and France seek a “northwest passage” around the Americas through the Arctic Ocean.
items.zh: 英格兰和法国寻找绕过美洲、穿越北冰洋的“西北航道”。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: English king Henry VII funded expedition (1497) led by Giovanni Caboto, or John Cabot; landed in Newfoundland
items.zh: 英格兰国王亨利七世资助了由乔瓦尼·卡博托（即约翰·卡博特）率领的探险（1497年）；在纽芬兰登陆

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: French funded (1524) Italian explorer Giovanni da Verrazzano sailed to the Americas (Cape Fear, now North Carolina); sailed north along the east coast of continental North America
items.zh: 法国资助（1524年）的意大利探险家乔瓦尼·达·韦拉扎诺航行到美洲（费尔角，即现在的北卡罗来纳州）；沿北美大陆东海岸向北航行

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: French established a colony in North America, Gallia Nova, or New France, in the region that is now Quebec.
items.zh: 法国人在北美建立了一个殖民地——新法兰西（Gallia Nova），位于现在的魁北克地区。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: English established their first successful American colonies in lands they named Virginia.
items.zh: 英格兰人在他们命名为弗吉尼亚的土地上建立了第一个成功的美洲殖民地。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: English merchants established East India Company; by 1612 the company secured its own rights to trade with India; enslavement of people in East Africa and Indonesia
items.zh: 英国商人成立了东印度公司；到1612年，该公司获得了与印度贸易的权利；奴役东非和印度尼西亚的人民

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Expansion of Dutch naval power and Dutch East India Company in early 1600s; Dutch established base in Jakarta, Indonesia; expanded control to include modern Taiwan, Malaysia, and provinces in East India
items.zh: 17世纪初荷兰海军力量和荷兰东印度公司的扩张；荷兰人在印度尼西亚雅加达建立基地；将控制范围扩大到包括现代台湾、马来西亚和东印度的省份

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By 1645, the Dutch most powerful trading empire in Southeast Asia
items.zh: 到1645年，荷兰成为东南亚最强大的贸易帝国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: To secure trading routes, Dutch East India Company turned Cape of Good Hope, in present-day South Africa, into a Dutch colony.
items.zh: 为确保贸易路线，荷兰东印度公司将好望角（位于今天的南非）变成了荷兰殖民地。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Overtime, Dutch in South Africa become known as Afrikaners (a South African of Dutch descent who speaks Afrikaans) or Boers (after the Dutch word for farmer)
items.zh: 随着时间推移，南非的荷兰人被称为阿非利卡人（南非荷兰裔、讲南非荷兰语的人）或布尔人（源自荷兰语中“农民”一词）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Dutch seek northwest passage; in 1609, the Dutch fund English explorer Henry Hudson to look for such a route; Hudson sails to North America; Hudson River in New York State; surveys modern states of New Jersey, New York, Delaware, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Connecticut
items.zh: 荷兰人寻找西北航道；1609年，荷兰资助英国探险家亨利·哈德逊寻找这样的航线；哈德逊航行到北美；纽约州的哈德逊河；勘察了现在的新泽西州、纽约州、特拉华州、宾夕法尼亚州、马里兰州和康涅狄格州

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After conflict between the Netherlands and England, New Netherland taken over by the English; New Amsterdam, one of the largest and richest settlements of New Netherland, renamed New York
items.zh: 荷兰与英格兰发生冲突后，新尼德兰被英格兰接管；新尼德兰最大、最富有的定居点之一新阿姆斯特丹被改名为纽约

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Slave trading and transportation became a major transatlantic activity in the 1600s and 1700s.
items.zh: 17世纪和18世纪，奴隶贸易和贩运成为跨大西洋的主要活动。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Region of West Africa where many enslaved people were traded became known as the Slave Coast.
items.zh: 西非许多奴隶被交易的区域被称为“奴隶海岸”。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Demand for enslaved labor grew due to the rise of profitable plantation crops in the Americas; Europeans began to lead raids deeper into Africa to find and capture people who could be enslaved and sold.
items.zh: 由于美洲盈利的种植园作物兴起，对奴隶劳动的需求增长；欧洲人开始深入非洲腹地进行袭击，寻找并抓捕可以被奴役和贩卖的人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Over centuries, the slave trade was active; many millions of Africans were taken on what was called the Middle Passage from Africa to the Americas and the Caribbean.
items.zh: 数百年来，奴隶贸易一直活跃；数以百万计的非洲人经由所谓“中程航线”被从非洲运往美洲和加勒比地区。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Transatlantic trade in people and goods referred to as triangular trade; consisted of three directions of movement: Europeans took goods such as weapons, alcohol, and clothes to Africa; goods exchanged for enslaved people; enslaved people taken to colonies in the Americas; goods produced by enslaved labor on colonial plantations taken back to Europe
items.zh: 跨大西洋的人口和货物贸易被称为三角贸易；包括三个方向的流动：欧洲人将武器、酒精和衣物等货物运到非洲；用货物交换奴隶；将奴隶运往美洲的殖民地；再将殖民地种植园中奴隶劳动生产的货物运回欧洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Europe B. Background The 1500s, 1600s, and 1700s brought significant changes in the ways that Europeans thought of themselves and their place in the world. When historians look back at this period, they find an increased regard for the roles of science and human reason and growing efforts to use science and reason to address a wide variety of issues.
items.zh: 欧洲B. 背景 16世纪、17世纪和18世纪，欧洲人对自身及其在世界上的位置的看法发生了重大变化。历史学家回顾这一时期时，发现人们更加重视科学和人类理性的作用，并越来越多地努力运用科学和理性来解决各种各样的问题。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: 1500s and 1600s see dramatic changes in European politics as governments throughout Europe became more bureaucratic and more centralized
items.zh: 16世纪和17世纪，欧洲各国政府变得更加官僚化和集权化，欧洲政治发生巨变。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Europeans experiencing a breakdown of their traditional views of the universe.
items.zh: 欧洲人经历了传统宇宙观的瓦解。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Dutch astronomer Tycho Brahe and German astronomer Johannes Kepler further support Nicolaus Copernicus’s theories with more proof of this emerging sun-centered worldview.
items.zh: 荷兰天文学家第谷·布拉赫和德国天文学家约翰内斯·开普勒用更多证据进一步支持了尼古拉·哥白尼的理论，支持这一正在兴起的以太阳为中心的世界观。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: In 1609, Galileo’s telescope powerful enough to see that the moon is not a perfect sphere or a luminous object; reveals Moon has shadows, indicating valleys and mountains, just like on Earth; Jupiter has its own moons, similar to Earth’s
items.zh: 1609年，伽利略的望远镜功能强大，足以看到月球并非完美的球体，也不是发光体；它显示月球上有阴影，表明那里像地球一样有山谷和高山；木星也有自己的卫星，类似于地球的卫星

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Scientific Revolution did not just look upward to the stars, it also looked inward, at the human body.
items.zh: 科学革命不仅仰望星空，也向内审视人体。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: William Harvey develops own theory of circulation of the blood
items.zh: 威廉·哈维提出了自己的血液循环理论

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier discovered the role of oxygen in the respiration (breathing) system.
items.zh: 安托万-洛朗·拉瓦锡发现了氧气在呼吸系统中的作用。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Ambroise Paré improved the treatment of wounds.
items.zh: 安布鲁瓦兹·帕雷改进了伤口治疗。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek created his own microscope, which he used to observe and describe bacteria.
items.zh: 安东尼·范·列文虎克制作了自己的显微镜，并用它观察和描述细菌。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Francis Bacon, René Descartes, John Locke, Jean-Jacques Rousseau some of the influencers of the European Enlightenment (Bacon’s life preceded the Enlightenment by several decades, but his writings served as one of its primary intellectual sources).
items.zh: 弗朗西斯·培根、勒内·笛卡尔、约翰·洛克、让-雅克·卢梭是欧洲启蒙运动的一些影响者（培根的生活比启蒙运动早了几十年，但他的著作是启蒙运动的主要思想来源之一）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: The Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment
items.en: Isaac Newton reformulated the scientific method; provides first coherent theory of the entire physical universe; matter infused with active forces; gravity produces all the motion in the universe
items.zh: 艾萨克·牛顿重新阐释了科学方法；提出了第一个涵盖整个物质世界的连贯理论；物质充满作用力；引力产生了宇宙中所有的运动

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Enlightenment was an intellectual movement centered in Europe and its colonies during the 1700s.
items.zh: 启蒙运动是18世纪以欧洲及其殖民地为中心的思想运动。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Human institutions, including forms of government, came under increased scrutiny and analysis during the Enlightenment (Thomas Hobbes believed humans needed strong government; John Locke believed humans had right to create and direct governments; natural rights).
items.zh: 启蒙运动期间，包括政府形式在内的人类制度受到越来越多的审视和分析（托马斯·霍布斯认为人类需要强大的政府；约翰·洛克认为人类有权建立和掌控政府；自然权利）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Human nature increasingly the focus of scientific-like inquiry
items.zh: 人性越来越成为类似科学探究的焦点

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Emergence of the French philosophes, a group of thinkers and writers increasingly critical of the existing social, political, and cultural orders in France; the group included Voltaire, Denis Diderot, Baron de Montesquieu, and Jean-Jacques Rousseau
items.zh: 法国“哲人”（philosophes）的出现，这是一群日益批判法国现有社会、政治和文化秩序的思想家和作家；该群体包括伏尔泰、丹尼斯·狄德罗、孟德斯鸠男爵和让-雅克·卢梭

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Influence of the Enlightenment on form and structure of new government in the United States of America
items.zh: 启蒙运动对美国新政府形式与结构的影响。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Europe (France, Spain, England)
items.zh: 欧洲（法国、西班牙、英格兰）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Caribbean (Haiti)
items.zh: 加勒比地区（海地）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: North America
items.zh: 北美洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mexico
items.zh: 墨西哥

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Central America
items.zh: 中美洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: South America
items.zh: 南美洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The ideals of the American Revolution gained traction in France.
items.zh: 美国革命的理想在法国获得了支持。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Marquis de Lafayette (1757–1834), a member of the French royal court, pressed for the abolition, or end, of the slave trade, for toleration of different religious beliefs, and for France to become a constitutional monarchy.
items.zh: 拉法耶特侯爵（1757–1834）是法国王室宫廷的一员，他强烈主张废除奴隶贸易、容忍不同的宗教信仰，并主张法国成为君主立宪制国家。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Influence in France of Thomas Paine’s publications Common Sense and Rights of Man
items.zh: 托马斯·潘恩的著作《常识》和《人的权利》在法国的影响

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Louis XVI (1754–93) the king of France during the French Revolution; Louis’s family, the House of Bourbon, had ruled France since 1589
items.zh: 路易十六（1754–1793）是法国大革命期间的法国国王；路易的家族波旁王朝自1589年以来一直统治法国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Louis was the ruler of the old order—l’ancien regime in French; he was the last king of the old order.
items.zh: 路易是旧制度的统治者——法语称“l'ancien regime”（旧制度）；他是旧制度的最后一位国王。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The French population was divided into three “estates,” levels determined by status, wealth, and power; the majority of France’s population made up the third estate, but lacked power and representation.
items.zh: 法国人口被分为三个“等级”（estates），等级由身份、财富和权力决定；法国大多数人口构成第三等级，但缺乏权力和代表权。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: France’s population roughly doubled in size from the 1300s, from about twelve million people after the Black Death to about twenty-six million people just before the Revolution.
items.zh: 从14世纪起，法国人口大约翻了一番，从黑死病后的约1200万人增至革命前夕的约2600万人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Growing class of merchants, artisans, bankers, and others who lived in French towns and cities, known as the bourgeoisie; educated, wealthy, and attracted to the ideas of the Enlightenment
items.zh: 生活在法国城镇的商人、工匠、银行家等阶层不断壮大，被称为资产阶级（bourgeoisie）；他们受过教育、富有，并受启蒙思想吸引

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In need of revenue, Louis XVI and his government attempt to tax his subjects from the first and second estates (the ‘notables’) who had previously been exempt from taxation; the notables refuse
items.zh: 由于需要收入，路易十六及其政府试图向此前免税的第一和第二等级（“显贵”）征税；显贵们拒绝纳税

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: King Louis XVI agrees to call the Estates- General in 1789; representatives of the three estates meet
items.zh: 国王路易十六同意于1789年召开三级会议；三个等级的代表举行会议

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Declaration of formation of a National Assembly
items.zh: 宣布成立国民议会

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Members of the National Assembly force the king and the other two estates to recognize its authority.
items.zh: 国民议会成员迫使国王和其他两个等级承认其权威。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Louis XVI plans to send his troops to dissolve the National Assembly; the people of Paris revolt.
items.zh: 路易十六计划派军队解散国民议会；巴黎人民起义。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: On July 14, 1789, a crowd of angry Parisians capture a fortified prison in the city, called the Bastille.
items.zh: 1789年7月14日，一群愤怒的巴黎人攻占了城中一座设防的监狱——巴士底狱。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Across France peasants rise up against economic hardships and their landlords.
items.zh: 法国各地的农民起来反抗经济困境和他们的地主。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: National Assembly issues sweeping range of reforms; end of the old order; Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
items.zh: 国民议会颁布了一系列广泛的改革；旧制度终结；《人权与公民权宣言》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Marquis de Lafayette elected to lead a new armed force, the National Guard
items.zh: 拉法耶特侯爵当选为新武装力量——国民卫队的领导人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Crowd, led by women, march to the Palace of Versailles on October 5, 1789; force the king and his family back to Paris
items.zh: 1789年10月5日，由妇女带领的人群游行至凡尔赛宫；迫使国王及其家人返回巴黎

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Louis XVI attempts to escape in June, 1791.
items.zh: 路易十六于1791年6月试图出逃。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1792, Louis XVI put under arrest by the citizens of Paris; the National Assembly declares that France is a republic and no longer a monarchy
items.zh: 1792年，路易十六被巴黎市民逮捕；国民议会宣布法国为共和国，不再是君主国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: From 1792 to 1795, France governed by a new body, the National Convention
items.zh: 1792年至1795年，法国由一个新的机构——国民公会治理

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Louis XVI accused of treason; tried, and sentenced to death by the National Convention
items.zh: 路易十六被指控叛国；经审判后被国民公会判处死刑

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Louis XVI and his wife, Marie Antoinette, both executed by guillotine in 1793
items.zh: 路易十六及其妻子玛丽·安托瓦内特于1793年均被断头台处决

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Radical revolutionaries, including Robespierre (1758-94) embark on ambitious economic and social measures; heavy taxes on the rich; price controls; universal education
items.zh: 激进的革命者，包括罗伯斯庇尔（1758–1794），推行雄心勃勃的经济和社会措施；对富人征收重税；实行价格管制；推行普及教育

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Coalition of British, Prussian, and Austrian forces repeatedly defeat French forces in European wars. Timeline
items.zh: 由英国、普鲁士和奥地利军队组成的联军在欧洲战争中多次击败法军。时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New body, the Committee of Public Safety, founded in 1793 to organize the war effort and to defeat internal opposition to the Revolution; people accused of opposing the revolution tried and executed; Reign of Terror
items.zh: 1793年成立新机构——救国委员会，以组织战事并击败国内对革命的反对；被指控反对革命的人受到审判和处决；恐怖统治

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Creation of a vast army of more than a million soldiers committed to defending France and defeating its enemies; Napoleon Bonaparte
items.zh: 创建了一支由一百多万士兵组成的庞大军队，致力于保卫法国并击败敌人；拿破仑·波拿巴

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Napoleon Bonaparte (1769–1821) initially a strong supporter and defender of the Revolution; leads French armies to defeat attempt to reinstate a monarch
items.zh: 拿破仑·波拿巴（1769–1821）最初是革命的坚定支持者和捍卫者；率领法军击败了恢复君主制的企图

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Napoleon given command of armies fighting the Austrians and their allies; in 1796 and 1797, he forces Austrians to surrender
items.zh: 拿破仑被授予对阵奥地利及其盟军的军队指挥权；1796年和1797年，他迫使奥地利人投降

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1799, Napoleon seizes control of the government; assumes full control over France as a dictator; in 1804, Napoleon declared emperor of France
items.zh: 1799年，拿破仑夺取政府控制权；作为独裁者完全掌控法国；1804年，拿破仑称帝，成为法国皇帝

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Between 1804 and 1814, Napoleon’s French Empire involved in wars against Britain, Prussia, Portugal, and Spain; failed military effort in Russia
items.zh: 1804年至1814年间，拿破仑的法兰西帝国卷入了对英国、普鲁士、葡萄牙和西班牙的战争；在俄罗斯的军事行动失败

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: On April 6, 1814, Napoleon gave up rule as emperor; enters into exile on the island of Elba
items.zh: 1814年4月6日，拿破仑放弃皇帝统治；被流放到厄尔巴岛

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: On March 1, 1815, Napoleon returns to France; takes control of the nation and its armies
items.zh: 1815年3月1日，拿破仑返回法国；重新控制了国家及其军队

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: A combined army of British and Prussian troops fight French troops at Waterloo, in Belgium, on June 18, 1815; Napoleon defeated and removed from power
items.zh: 1815年6月18日，英国和普鲁士联军在比利时滑铁卢与法军交战；拿破仑战败并被剥夺权力

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1791, Haiti (western part of the island, Saint-Dominique) controlled by France
items.zh: 1791年，海地（该岛西部，即圣多明各）由法国控制

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Previously colonized by Spain (Hispaniola); under the Spanish, thousands of enslaved Africans and indigenous people forced to work in gold mines
items.zh: 先前被西班牙殖民（伊斯帕尼奥拉岛）；在西班牙人统治下，成千上万的非洲奴隶和原住民被迫在金矿劳作。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Saint-Domingue society based on classifying people by color and race
items.zh: 圣多明各社会以按肤色和种族对人进行分类为基础

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Enslaved people have no rights; people of mixed heritage called affranchise
items.zh: 奴隶没有任何权利；混血后裔被称为“自由有色人”（affranchise）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1791, following the overthrow of the French king, the new French government extends citizenship rights to some affranchise; ruling classes of Saint-Domingue ignore this order; large number of enslaved people revolt
items.zh: 1791年，法国国王被推翻后，新的法国政府将公民权扩展到部分自由有色人；圣多明各的统治阶级无视这一命令；大量奴隶起义

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: French government sends official to restore order.
items.zh: 法国政府派遣官员恢复秩序。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1794, French government agree to abolish slavery; rebelling enslaved population want independence; revolution
items.zh: 1794年，法国政府同意废除奴隶制；起义的奴隶希望获得独立；革命爆发

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Toussaint L’Ouverture (1743–1803) becomes leader of the revolutionaries; several victories over the French
items.zh: 杜桑·卢维杜尔（1743–1803）成为革命者的领袖；多次战胜法军

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By 1794, rebels supported by British and the Spanish on the eastern half of the island (which today is the Dominican Republic)
items.zh: 到1794年，叛军在岛屿东半部（即今天的多米尼加共和国）得到英国和西班牙的支持

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Toussaint makes a deal with the French; he becomes lieutenant-governor of Saint Domingue; slavery abolished in exchange for an end to the rebellion
items.zh: 杜桑与法国人达成协议；他成为圣多明各的副总督；以结束叛乱为代价废除奴隶制

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Agreement with Saint-Domingue broken by Napoleon Bonaparte; he tries to restore total French control between 1801 and 1803
items.zh: 拿破仑·波拿巴撕毁了与圣多明各的协议；他在1801年至1803年间试图恢复法国的完全控制

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Toussaint imprisoned by the French; died in 1803
items.zh: 杜桑被法国人监禁；于1803年去世

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: France eventually defeated; the nation of Haiti established in 1804
items.zh: 法国最终战败；海地国于1804年建立

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: France demands that the former colony pay 150 million francs in exchange for its independence—roughly 21 billion dollars in modern currency
items.zh: 法国要求这个前殖民地支付1.5亿法郎以换取独立——按现代货币计算约为210亿美元

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Beginning of the 1800s, independence movements sweep through the Spanish Empire in the Americas; events in Europe in the 1800s trigger revolutionary movements in the Americas
items.zh: 19世纪初，独立运动席卷美洲的西班牙帝国；19世纪欧洲的事件引发了美洲的革命运动

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Between 1808 and 1826, Spain loses control of all its possessions except Cuba and Puerto Rico.
items.zh: 1808年至1826年间，西班牙失去了除古巴和波多黎各之外的所有殖民地。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Brazil becomes independent of Portugal in 1822 with Dom Pedro (1798–1834) as its first emperor
items.zh: 1822年，巴西脱离葡萄牙独立，由佩德罗一世（1798–1834）担任首任皇帝

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Simón Bolívar (1783–1830), known as EL Libertador (the Liberator), and José de San Martín (1778–1850), successful leaders of the revolutions against Spanish rule
items.zh: 西蒙·玻利瓦尔（1783–1830），被称为“解放者”（EL Libertador），以及何塞·德·圣马丁（1778–1850），是反抗西班牙统治的革命的成功领袖

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: San Martín helped Argentina, Chile, and Peru achieve independence by 1821.
items.zh: 到1821年，圣马丁帮助阿根廷、智利和秘鲁获得独立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Between 1817 and 1819, Bolívar took control of the colony of New Granada, which was renamed Gran Colombia.
items.zh: 1817年至1819年间，玻利瓦尔控制了新格拉纳达殖民地，并将其改名为大哥伦比亚。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Bolívar dreamed of a large, independent state, but by 1830, Gran Colombia had fractured into smaller nations: Venezuela, Ecuador, Colombia, and Panama
items.zh: 玻利瓦尔梦想建立一个庞大的独立国家，但到1830年，大哥伦比亚已分裂为几个较小的国家：委内瑞拉、厄瓜多尔、哥伦比亚和巴拿马

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mexico was known as New Spain under Spanish rule.
items.zh: 墨西哥在西班牙统治下被称为新西班牙。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The push for Mexican independence was driven by political developments in Spain.
items.zh: 墨西哥独立运动的推动源于西班牙的政治局势变化。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New Mexican Empire became independent on August 24, 1821; lasts for two years
items.zh: 新墨西哥帝国于1821年8月24日独立；存续两年

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mexican revolutionaries such as, Antonio López de Santa Anna (1794–1876), believe Mexico should become a republic.
items.zh: 墨西哥革命者，如安东尼奥·洛佩斯·德·圣安娜（1794–1876），认为墨西哥应成为共和国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mexico adopts a new republican constitution.
items.zh: 墨西哥通过新的共和宪法。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Two factions compete to control the direction of the country: Centralists, who want a strong government and support the Catholic religion as central to Mexico’s identity; Federalists, who want Mexican states to have the power to rule themselves
items.zh: 两个派系争夺国家发展方向：中央集权派希望建立强有力的政府，并支持天主教作为墨西哥身份认同的核心；联邦派则希望墨西哥各州拥有自治权

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Santa Anna becomes president of Mexico for the first time in 1833.
items.zh: 圣安娜于1833年首次成为墨西哥总统。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Texas declared its independence from Mexico in 1835.
items.zh: 得克萨斯于1835年宣布脱离墨西哥独立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1836, Santa Anna leads a large army into Texas; he is defeated by smaller Texan forces.
items.zh: 1836年，圣安娜率大军进入得克萨斯；被人数较少的得克萨斯军队击败。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Santa Anna removed from power in Mexico
items.zh: 圣安娜在墨西哥被剥夺权力

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The United States declares war on Mexico.
items.zh: 美国向墨西哥宣战。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Benito Juárez rises to the forefront of Mexican politics.
items.zh: 贝尼托·华雷斯崛起，成为墨西哥政坛的领军人物。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: A new constitution put in place in Mexico in 1857, creating a representative democratic republic with a strong executive
items.zh: 墨西哥于1857年颁布新宪法，建立了代议制民主共和国，并设立强有力的行政机构

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Church and other conservatives oppose the new constitution; civil war breaks out.
items.zh: 教会和其他保守派反对新宪法；内战爆发。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Benito Juárez becomes president; United States supports Juárez.
items.zh: 贝尼托·华雷斯成为总统；美国支持华雷斯。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Juárez reelected in 1867 and 1871; political reform
items.zh: 华雷斯于1867年和1871年连任；推行政治改革

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1876, Porfirio Díaz becomes president of Mexico, beginning a thirty-five-year career of government domination; reinstates the power of the Church in Mexican affairs; economic reforms
items.zh: 1876年，波菲里奥·迪亚斯成为墨西哥总统，开始了长达35年的独裁统治；恢复了教会在墨西哥事务中的权力；推行经济改革

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The elite once again dominate in political and economic power; opposition to Díaz grows.
items.zh: 精英阶层再次主导政治和经济权力；反对迪亚斯的力量不断壮大。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: In 1910, Francisco Madero campaigns for the presidency against Díaz; Madero arrested and jailed
items.zh: 1910年，弗朗西斯科·马德罗竞选总统对抗迪亚斯；马德罗被捕入狱

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Pancho Villa and Emiliano Zapata lead revolutionary forces, eventually removing Díaz from power.
items.zh: 潘乔·比利亚和埃米利亚诺·萨帕塔领导革命力量，最终推翻了迪亚斯政权。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Madero named president; US opposes Madero.
items.zh: 马德罗被任命为总统；美国反对马德罗。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Madero overthrown when revolutionaries, including Villa, Zapata, and Venustiano Carranza, continue armed resistance.
items.zh: 比利亚、萨帕塔和贝努斯蒂亚诺·卡兰萨等革命者继续武装抵抗，马德罗被推翻。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Civil war continues until 1917; Carranza becomes president and oversees the rewriting of the constitution, making the president a dictator.
items.zh: 内战持续到1917年；卡兰萨成为总统并主持重写宪法，使总统成为独裁者。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Violence continues until 1920, when Carranza is overthrown; order and constitutional government restored under the presidency of Lázaro Cárdenas I. Revolutions in Industry, Agriculture, and New Technology: Background Political revolutions were just one of the forces transforming the world during the 1700s and 1800s. New developments in technology and the organization of labor also took place during this period in what is known as the Industrial Revolution. The Industrial Revolution is difficult to pin down to specific dates and events. In some ways, the name refers to long-term trends that developed over many decades.
items.zh: 暴力冲突持续到1920年，卡兰萨被推翻；在拉萨罗·卡德纳斯总统任内，秩序与宪政政府得以恢复。I. 工业、农业与新技术革命：背景 政治革命只是18—19世纪改变世界的力量之一。这一时期，技术与劳动组织也出现新发展，即所谓的工业革命。工业革命难以确定具体日期和事件；从某种意义上看，这个名称指的是数十年间形成的长期趋势。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: By the 1700s, new crops, techniques, and technologies were widely used to feed Europe’s population; new technologies improve the food supply.
items.zh: 到18世纪，新的作物、技术和技术手段已被广泛用于养活欧洲人口；新技术改善了食物供应。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: The new crops included staple goods like potatoes and corn from the Americas.
items.zh: 新作物包括来自美洲的马铃薯和玉米等主食。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: In Europe, older ways of organizing and owning land transformed by the process of enclosure
items.zh: 在欧洲，古老的土地组织和所有方式因圈地运动而发生改变

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Enclosure increased the power and wealth of landlords and limited that of peasants.
items.zh: 圈地运动增加了地主的权力和财富，限制了农民的权力和财富。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Improvements in both agriculture and industry were linked to developments in science and technology.
items.zh: 农业和工业的进步都与科学技术的发展相关。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Discoveries and inventions were applied to many different areas of economic activity— mining, production of goods, farming, and transport—by people who were focused on profit.
items.zh: 发现和发明被追求利润的人们应用到经济活动的许多领域——采矿、商品生产、农业和运输。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: The Industrial Revolution brought new means of generating power, such as the steam engine; Scottish engineer James Watt (1736–1819)
items.zh: 工业革命带来了新的动力产生方式，如蒸汽机；苏格兰工程师詹姆斯·瓦特（1736–1819）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Industrialization was the process of applying new technologies and processes to make the production of goods more efficient.
items.zh: 工业化是将新技术和新工艺应用于商品生产，以提高效率的过程。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: In the 1700s, several inventions and innovations were applied to the wool-and-cloth making industry to make it more efficient and maximize profits; Spinning Jenny invented by English inventor James Hargreaves (1721–78); American inventor, Eli Whitney (1765–1825), creates the cotton gin
items.zh: 18世纪，多项发明和创新被应用于毛纺和布料行业，以提高效率、实现利润最大化；英国发明家詹姆斯·哈格里夫斯（1721–78）发明珍妮纺纱机；美国发明家伊莱·惠特尼（1765–1825）发明轧棉机

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Establishment of the factory system and subsequent urbanization
items.zh: 工厂制度的建立及随后的城市化

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Rise of capitalism
items.zh: 资本主义的兴起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: Scottish Enlightenment philosopher and political economist Adam Smith (1723–90), one of the first theorists to describe the way free markets work; An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776)
items.zh: 苏格兰启蒙思想家和政治经济学家亚当·斯密（1723–90），最早描述自由市场运作方式的理论家之一；《国民财富的性质和原因的研究》（1776）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: The Mexican Revolution and Continuing Conflict
items.en: This revolutionary period led to transformation of much of the world’s political, social, and economic systems.
items.zh: 这一革命时期导致世界许多地区的政治、社会和经济体系发生转变。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Europe (France, Belgium, Italy, Austria, Germany, Great Britain, Hungary, Serbia, Bulgaria, Montenegro, Greece, Russia)
items.zh: 欧洲（法国、比利时、意大利、奥地利、德国、英国、匈牙利、塞尔维亚、保加利亚、黑山、希腊、俄罗斯）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Turkey
items.zh: 土耳其

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: India
items.zh: 印度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Africa (Egypt, South Africa, Algeria, Democratic Republic of Congo)
items.zh: 非洲（埃及、南非、阿尔及利亚、刚果民主共和国）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Southeast Asia (Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam)
items.zh: 东南亚（柬埔寨、老挝、越南）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Asia/East Asia (China, Japan, Korea)
items.zh: 亚洲/东亚（中国、日本、朝鲜）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: North America (California, Hawaii)
items.zh: 北美洲（加利福尼亚、夏威夷）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Atlantic Ocean
items.zh: 大西洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Pacific Ocean
items.zh: 太平洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Indian Ocean
items.zh: 印度洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mediterranean Sea
items.zh: 地中海

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Background In the late 1800s and early 1900s, nations around the globe were expanding. Sometimes this expansion was peaceful. Nations used trade and diplomacy to acquire resources
items.en: Nations built empires and engaged in imperialism.
items.zh: 各国建立帝国，推行帝国主义。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Background In the late 1800s and early 1900s, nations around the globe were expanding. Sometimes this expansion was peaceful. Nations used trade and diplomacy to acquire resources
items.en: Imperialism also driven by competition between rival nations and the rise of nationalism globally
items.zh: 帝国主义也受到敌对国家间竞争和全球民族主义兴起的推动

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Background In the late 1800s and early 1900s, nations around the globe were expanding. Sometimes this expansion was peaceful. Nations used trade and diplomacy to acquire resources
items.en: The drive for expansion of empire grew along with the Industrial Revolution and the need for raw materials such as rubber, timber, cotton, gold, diamonds.
items.zh: 随着工业革命和对橡胶、木材、棉花、黄金、钻石等原材料的需求，帝国扩张的驱动力不断增强。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Background In the late 1800s and early 1900s, nations around the globe were expanding. Sometimes this expansion was peaceful. Nations used trade and diplomacy to acquire resources
items.en: Countries that controlled trade routes could ensure they had buyers for their goods, both at home and in the lands they controlled.
items.zh: 控制贸易路线的国家能确保其商品在国内和所控制的地区都有买家。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Background In the late 1800s and early 1900s, nations around the globe were expanding. Sometimes this expansion was peaceful. Nations used trade and diplomacy to acquire resources
items.en: New methods of transportation, weapons, and communication changed how Europe interacted with other parts of the globe.
items.zh: 新的交通、武器和通信方式改变了欧洲与全球其他地区的互动方式。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Background In the late 1800s and early 1900s, nations around the globe were expanding. Sometimes this expansion was peaceful. Nations used trade and diplomacy to acquire resources
items.en: Religion played a role in this era of imperialism; Christian missionaries from Britain, France, Belgium, and the United States traveled throughout Africa and Asia with the aim of converting people to Christianity.
items.zh: 宗教在这一帝国主义时代发挥了作用；来自英国、法国、比利时和美国的基督教传教士走遍非洲和亚洲，旨在使人们皈依基督教。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Background In the late 1800s and early 1900s, nations around the globe were expanding. Sometimes this expansion was peaceful. Nations used trade and diplomacy to acquire resources
items.en: In Japan, nationalism grew among those who wanted Japan to industrialize and build its own empire.
items.zh: 在日本，希望日本实现工业化并建立自己帝国的人群中，民族主义情绪高涨。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Britain had the largest and richest empire in the world during the 1800s and well into the 1900s.
items.zh: 在19世纪乃至20世纪相当长一段时间里，英国拥有世界上最大、最富有的帝国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The British Empire was at the height of its power during the reign of Queen Victoria, which lasted sixty-three years, from 1837 to 1901; during this time India, South Africa, Hong Kong, Egypt, and large parts of West and East Africa were added to the British Empire.
items.zh: 大英帝国在维多利亚女王统治时期达到权力顶峰，其统治长达63年，从1837年至1901年；在此期间，印度、南非、香港、埃及以及西非和东非的大片地区被纳入大英帝国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: India most economically important part of the British Empire
items.zh: 印度是大英帝国经济上最重要的部分

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1857, people in India rebel against British attempt to expand control of India
items.zh: 1857年，印度人民反抗英国扩大对印度控制的企图

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rebellion fails and British government take direct control of India; established the Raj
items.zh: 起义失败，英国政府直接统治印度；确立了英属印度（Raj）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Raj was responsible for collecting taxes, enforcing laws, and ensuring that British rules about trade and agriculture were followed.
items.zh: 英属印度当局负责征税、执法，并确保英国关于贸易和农业的规定得到遵守。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: British traders and business owners founded plantations in India to grow tea, indigo, and cotton; large areas of land no longer available to Indian population to grow crops; famine
items.zh: 英国商人和企业主在印度建立种植园，种植茶叶、靛蓝和棉花；大片土地不再供印度民众种植作物；导致饥荒

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Raj created considerable wealth for Britain; wealth not shared by most Indians; construction of thousands of miles of railroad
items.zh: 英属印度为英国创造了大量财富；但财富并未为大多数印度人所共享；修建了数千英里的铁路

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: David Livingstone traveled back and forth across Africa; believed that by spreading Christianity, finding trade routes, he could help abolish slavery
items.zh: 戴维·利文斯通往返穿越非洲；相信通过传播基督教、开辟贸易路线，可以帮助废除奴隶制。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1869, journalist Henry Stanley went into Central Africa in search of Livingstone. Two years later, Stanley found Livingstone; “Dr. Livingstone, I presume?”
items.zh: 1869年，记者亨利·斯坦利深入中非寻找利文斯通。两年后，斯坦利找到了利文斯通；“我想您就是利文斯通博士吧？”

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1869 the Suez Canal, constructed and controlled by the British and French, was opened in Egypt; enabled ships to sail from the Mediterranean Sea to the Indian Ocean
items.zh: 1869年，由英国和法国修建并控制的苏伊士运河在埃及开通；使船只能够从地中海航行至印度洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Civil unrest in Egypt led by nationalists leads to new nationalist Egyptian government; British forces attack Egypt and force revolutionaries out of power; Britain takes direct control of Suez Canal
items.zh: 民族主义者领导的埃及内乱催生了新的民族主义政府；英军进攻埃及，迫使革命者下台；英国直接控制苏伊士运河

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: French invasion of Algeria begins a lengthy, violent conquest; France encourages Europeans to move to Algeria; French citizens have more rights than native Algerians
items.zh: 法国入侵阿尔及利亚，开始了漫长而暴力的征服；法国鼓励欧洲人移居阿尔及利亚；法国公民比阿尔及利亚本地人享有更多权利

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: First permanent European settlement in South Africa created by the Dutch East India Company in 1682; Dutch settlers known as Boers; soon joined by British settlers Timeline
items.zh: 1682年，荷兰东印度公司在南非建立了第一个永久性欧洲定居点；荷兰移民被称为布尔人；不久英国移民也加入进来。时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Diamonds were discovered in South Africa in 1867 and gold in 1886; gold deposits in area largely controlled by Boers
items.zh: 1867年在南非发现钻石，1886年发现黄金；该地区的金矿大多由布尔人控制

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: South African War (1899–1902), also known as the Anglo-Boer War, developed out of the competition for South Africa’s resources; British responded with harsh new tactics; burned the farmland of Boer settlers and put civilians into concentration camps
items.zh: 南非战争（1899–1902），又称英布战争，源于对南非资源的争夺；英国以残酷的新手段回应；烧毁布尔移民的农田，并将平民关进集中营

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1884, Germany hosted the Berlin Conference; conference designed to allow imperialist nations to decide how to divide Africa among themselves; no African nations invited to the conference
items.zh: 1884年，德国主办柏林会议；会议旨在让帝国主义国家决定如何瓜分非洲；没有邀请任何非洲国家参加

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Before the Berlin Conference, 80 percent of Africa was controlled by Africans; after the Berlin Conference, European powers expand their control
items.zh: 柏林会议之前，非洲80%的土地由非洲人控制；柏林会议之后，欧洲列强扩大了控制。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: European nations divided Africa into units that were easy for colonial governments to control; units often ignored the boundaries and divisions set by the African populations
items.zh: 欧洲国家将非洲划分为便于殖民政府控制的区域；这些划分往往忽视了非洲各族群原有的边界和分界

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: King Leopold II of Belgium created the Congo Free State in 1885 and turned it into a personal possession; Leopold’s rule brutalized the people of the Congo; resources of rubber and ivory were extracted using forced labor by the Congolese under Belgian direction
items.zh: 比利时国王利奥波德二世于1885年建立刚果自由邦，并将其变为个人领地；利奥波德的统治残酷对待刚果人民；在比利时人的指挥下，通过强迫刚果人劳动来掠夺橡胶和象牙资源

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The modern nation of Italy was created in the middle of the nineteenth century as a result of the desire for unification.
items.zh: 现代意大利国家于19世纪中叶因统一愿望而建立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1860, an Italian nationalist named Giuseppe Garibaldi (1807–82) led an army of Italian nationalists, the Thousand, on a march to Sicily; the Thousand conquered Sicily and marched on Naples; efforts of Garibaldi unified most of Italy
items.zh: 1860年，意大利民族主义者朱塞佩·加里波第（1807–82）率领一支名为“千人团”的意大利民族主义者军队向西西里进军；千人团征服西西里后进军那不勒斯；加里波第的努力统一了意大利大部分地区

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nationalist leaders elected a new parliament; made Victor Emmanuel II the first king of modern Italy in 1861
items.zh: 民族主义者领袖选举产生新议会；1861年拥立维克托·伊曼纽尔二世为现代意大利首位国王

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Between 1866 and 1870, Rome and Venice were added to the new Italian nation; Rome was made the nation’s capital shortly afterward.
items.zh: 1866年至1870年间，罗马和威尼斯并入新生的意大利；不久后罗马被定为意大利首都。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: The modern nation of Germany was created in the late 1800s.
items.zh: 现代德国于19世纪末建立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: The German Empire was formally established on January 18, 1871.
items.zh: 德意志帝国于1871年1月18日正式成立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: Unifying the states into one German nation was the goal of the Prussian prime minister, Otto von Bismarck (1815–98).
items.zh: 将各邦统一为一个德意志国家是普鲁士首相奥托·冯·俾斯麦（1815–98）的目标。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: To weaken France, Bismarck secretly formed the Triple Alliance with Austria-Hungary and Italy in 1882; the three nations pledged to help each other if invaded by France; Bismarck also reached agreements with Russian and Britain
items.zh: 为削弱法国，俾斯麦于1882年秘密与奥匈帝国和意大利结成三国同盟；三国承诺若遭法国入侵则相互援助；俾斯麦还与俄国和英国达成协议

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: Though Bismarck shaped German foreign policy, the German Empire was ruled by an unelected emperor, called the Kaiser; in 1888, a new emperor named Wilhelm II came to the throne.
items.zh: 尽管俾斯麦主导德国外交政策，但德意志帝国由未经选举产生的皇帝（Kaiser，即德皇）统治；1888年，新皇帝威廉二世登基。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: German social problems, desire for more democracy, leads to removal of Bismarck from power; change in Germany’s alliances
items.zh: 德国的社会问题以及对更多民主的诉求导致俾斯麦下台；德国的同盟关系随之改变

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: Wilhelm II does not renew the treaty with Russia; France and Russia create a military alliance in 1894
items.zh: 威廉二世未续签与俄国的条约；法国与俄国于1894年结成军事同盟

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: Wilhelm expands German colonial aims and German navy
items.zh: 威廉扩张德国的殖民目标并扩充德国海军

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: In 1907, Britain, France, and Russia form a new pact called the Triple Entente; the major powers in Europe now divided into two sides; the Triple Entente united Britain, France, and Russia; the Triple Alliance bound together Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy
items.zh: 1907年，英国、法国和俄国组成新协定，即三国协约；欧洲列强由此分为两大阵营；三国协约联合了英国、法国和俄国；三国同盟则把德国、奥匈帝国和意大利绑在一起

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: In 1853, American naval officer, Commodore Matthew Perry, sailed to Japan to open diplomatic relations with the nation; Perry claimed two of Japan’s southern islands for the United States; he sailed four warships into Tokyo Bay; presented a letter and gifts to the government of Japan
items.zh: 1853年，美国海军军官马修·佩里准将驶抵日本，要求与该国建立外交关系；佩里声称日本两座南部岛屿归美国所有；他率领四艘军舰驶入东京湾；向日本政府递交书信和礼物

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: Japanese government made new arrangements that opened Japan’s ports to American naval and trading ships.
items.zh: 日本政府作出新安排，向美国军舰和商船开放日本港口。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: Having annexed California and Hawaii, the United States wanted to increase trade with Asia; wanted access to Japan in order to refuel and repair their ships after long voyages across the Pacific Ocean
items.zh: 在吞并加利福尼亚和夏威夷后，美国希望增加与亚洲的贸易；希望进入日本，以便在横渡太平洋的长途航行后为船只补充燃料和维修

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: The opening of Japan to European and American trade motivated Japan to industrialize its economy and modernize its military.
items.zh: 日本向欧美贸易开放，促使日本实现经济工业化和军队现代化。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: In the late 1800s, Japan began building its empire in Asia, starting with with Korea, an important ally of China.
items.zh: 19世纪末，日本开始在亚洲建立帝国，首先是中国的重要盟友朝鲜。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: In 1875, Japan forced Korea to open its borders to Japanese trade.
items.zh: 1875年，日本迫使朝鲜向日本贸易开放国门。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: Between 1894 and 1895, Japan and China are at war; Japan’s modern military defeated the large Chinese army; China forced to give Korea its independence and offer special trade privileges to Japan
items.zh: 1894年至1895年间，日本与中国交战；日本的现代化军队击败了庞大的中国军队；中国被迫承认朝鲜独立，并给予日本特殊贸易特权

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: Russian treaty with China, promising to defend China’s independence
items.zh: 俄国与中国签订条约，承诺捍卫中国的独立

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Unification, the Triple Alliance, and the Triple Entente
items.en: In 1904, Japan attacked a Russian warship, starting the Russo-Japanese War; Russian naval fleet largely destroyed by Japanese navy; both sides sign a peace treaty to end the fighting in 1905; the Russo-Japanese War marked the first time in modern history that an Asian nation defeated a European nation
items.zh: 1904年，日本袭击俄国军舰，挑起日俄战争；俄国舰队基本被日本海军摧毁；双方于1905年签署和约结束战斗；日俄战争标志着近代史上亚洲国家首次战胜欧洲国家

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: In the late 1800s, Britain pressured the Qing dynasty for more access to China’s economy; the British used trade in an addictive drug, opium, to force open trade with China.
items.zh: 19世纪末，英国向清政府施压，要求进一步进入中国市场；英国利用令人成瘾的毒品鸦片贸易，迫使中国开放贸易。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: The opium trade increased dramatically in the 1820s after Britain took control of some Chinese ports by military force.
items.zh: 19世纪20年代，英国以武力控制中国部分港口后，鸦片贸易急剧增加。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: In 1839, Chinese officials destroyed a warehouse full of opium belonging to a British trader; the British reacted with force; this began the First Opium War; at end of war Britain has gained more control over China; gained control over Hong Kong
items.zh: 1839年，中国官员销毁了一座装满英国商人鸦片的仓库；英国以武力回应；第一次鸦片战争由此爆发；战争结束时英国获得了对中国的更多控制权；取得了香港

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: In control of Chinese ports, Britain opened them to American, French, German, and Japanese trade ships
items.zh: 英国控制中国港口后，向美国、法国、德国和日本的商船开放这些港口。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: China gave Christian missionaries access to the nation’s interior
items.zh: 中国允许基督教传教士进入内地

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: The Taiping Rebellion takes place between 1850 to 1864; rebels motivated by hunger and China’s economic problems, and religion; rebellion eventually defeated with help from British and American military leaders
items.zh: 太平天国运动发生于1850年至1864年；叛乱者受饥饿、中国经济问题和宗教因素驱动；起义最终在英美军事领导人的协助下被镇压

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Russia claims land in the north of China.
items.zh: 俄国攫取中国北方土地。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Second Opium War launched in 1856; Britain gains even more power in China; opium becomes legal
items.zh: 第二次鸦片战争于1856年爆发；英国在中国获得更多权力；鸦片合法化

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Boxer rebellion began in in 1899; leaders aimed to remove foreigners from China and preserve Chinese culture; opposed Christian missionaries
items.zh: 义和团运动始于1899年；其领导者旨在将外国人逐出中国并保护中国文化；反对基督教传教士

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Boxer rebels overwhelmed by foreign troops; peace treaty signed in 1901
items.zh: 义和团被外国军队镇压；1901年签订和约

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Revolutionary Alliance takes shape outside of China; led by Sun Yat-sen (1866–1925); Sun leads unsuccessful revolts in south of China
items.zh: 同盟会在中国境外成立；由孙中山（1866—1925）领导；孙中山在中国南方领导了多次未成功的起义。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: In 1908, the Qing rulers, Empress Cixi and Emperor Guangxu, died; control of the country was passed to three-year-old Emperor Puyi; Revolutionary Alliance continues to attack Qing government; in 1911 forces Qing dynasty to adopt a constitution; Emperor Puyi abdicates; Sun elected leader of new Republic of China J. French Indochina
items.zh: 1908年，清朝统治者慈禧太后和光绪皇帝去世；国家权力传给年仅三岁的宣统帝溥仪；同盟会继续攻击清政府；1911年迫使清廷颁布宪法；溥仪退位；孙中山被选为新中华民国的领导人。J. 法属印度支那

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: The present-day Southeast Asian countries of Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam were once called Indochina.
items.zh: 现今东南亚的柬埔寨、老挝和越南曾被称为印度支那。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: France took control of Indochina between 1858 and 1893.
items.zh: 法国于1858年至1893年间控制了印度支那。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Society during period of French rule in Indochina dominated by the French and small class of wealthy people; in Vietnam, land was primarily owned by French landlords
items.zh: 法国统治印度支那时期，社会由法国人和少数富裕阶层主导；在越南，土地主要由法国地主占有

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Nationalist movements grew in Vietnam in the late 1800s; in 1908, Vietnamese citizens protested taxes
items.zh: 19世纪末，越南民族主义运动兴起；1908年，越南民众抗议税收

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: French control of Vietnam did not end until 1954.
items.zh: 法国对越南的控制直到1954年才结束。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: At its height, the Ottoman Empire spanned eastern Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia; the empire’s center was present-day Turkey.
items.zh: 奥斯曼帝国鼎盛时期横跨东欧、北非和西亚；帝国中心位于今天的土耳其。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: In the 1800s, the Ottoman Empire was not as industrialized as its European neighbors.
items.zh: 19世纪，奥斯曼帝国的工业化程度不及欧洲邻国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: By the second half of the 1800s, Ottoman empire in debt to European powers; by the late 1800s, the Ottomans defaulted on their loans; loss of territory in eastern Europe to nationalist uprisings; Britain and other European nations took control of a large portion of the Ottoman financial system in 1881
items.zh: 到19世纪下半叶，奥斯曼帝国欠欧洲列强债务；19世纪末，奥斯曼人无力偿还贷款；因民族主义起义丧失东欧领土；1881年，英国和其他欧洲国家控制了奥斯曼金融体系的大部分

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Ottoman ruler Sultan Abdulhamid II (1842–1918) ruled from 1876 to 1909; he attempted modernization and reorganization of government; in 1908 Young Turks stage a revolt; demand a new constitution and more reforms
items.zh: 奥斯曼苏丹阿卜杜勒-哈米德二世（1842–1918）于1876年至1909年在位；他尝试推行现代化和政府重组；1908年青年土耳其党人发动起义；要求颁布新宪法并进行更多改革

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Opium Wars and Revolt in China
items.en: Ottoman empire loses territory in North Africa to Italy in 1912; between 1912 and 1913, an alliance of Serbia, Bulgaria, Montenegro, and Greece removed the Ottomans from the Balkans
items.zh: 1912年，奥斯曼帝国将北非领土割让给意大利；1912年至1913年间，塞尔维亚、保加利亚、黑山和希腊组成的联盟将奥斯曼势力逐出巴尔干

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tensions in the Balkans, located in southern Europe, led to the outbreak of the First World War
items.zh: 位于欧洲南部的巴尔干地区的紧张局势导致第一次世界大战爆发。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tension over whether Serbs living inside Austria-Hungary would become part of the neighboring small Serbian state; Austria-Hungary’s ruler opposed this; sent Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir of Austria-Hungary, to Sarajevo, Bosnia, to attend a military parade
items.zh: 围绕奥匈帝国境内的塞尔维亚人是否应并入邻国小塞尔维亚国家的紧张局势；奥匈帝国统治者反对这种做法；派奥匈帝国皇位继承人弗朗茨·斐迪南大公前往波斯尼亚萨拉热窝参加军事阅兵

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: On June 28, 1914, Serbian nationalist, Gavrilo Princip, shot and killed the archduke and his wife.
items.zh: 1914年6月28日，塞尔维亚民族主义者加夫里洛·普林西普枪杀了斐迪南大公夫妇。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: On July 28, 1914, Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia; sets off chain of alliances; Allied Powers fight against Central Powers.
items.zh: 1914年7月28日，奥匈帝国向塞尔维亚宣战；引发连锁同盟反应；协约国与同盟国交战。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Germany invaded Belgium and marched to within 30 miles of Paris; eventually halted at Marne River by French and British soldiers; the First Battle of the Marne marked the beginning of trench warfare
items.zh: 德国入侵比利时，进军至距巴黎30英里处；最终在马恩河被法军和英军阻止；第一次马恩河战役标志着堑壕战的开始

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Central Powers fought a two-front war; Eastern Front and Western Front
items.zh: 同盟国进行两线作战；东线和西线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In October 1914, Ottoman Empire joined the Central Powers
items.zh: 1914年10月，奥斯曼帝国加入同盟国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1915, Allied Forces engaged in sea and land assault on Ottoman controlled Gallipoli
items.zh: 1915年，协约国军队对奥斯曼帝国控制的加里波利发动海陆进攻

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1915, Italy agreed to join the Allies.
items.zh: 1915年，意大利同意加入协约国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Germany declared the waters around Britain to be a war zone; threatened to sink any ships that entered British waters; September 1915, German submarine fired torpedoes to sink the American passenger ship Lusitania, killing more than 1,200 people, including around 120 Americans
items.zh: 德国宣布英国周围海域为战争区；威胁击沉任何进入英国水域的船只；1915年9月，德国潜艇发射鱼雷击沉美国客轮卢西塔尼亚号，造成1200多人死亡，其中约120人为美国人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1916, Germany and Allied troops from France and Britain fought at the Battle of the Somme in France, one of the deadliest battles of the war.
items.zh: 1916年，德国与来自法国和英国的协约国军队在法国索姆河战役中交战，这是战争中最惨烈的战役之一。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1917, the United States entered the war, fighting on the side of the Allied Forces.
items.zh: 1917年，美国参战，站在协约国一方作战。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1917, Russian armed forces revolt and bring down the Czar of Russia and his government; second revolution in Russia occurs, resulting in Russia leaving the war
items.zh: 1917年，俄罗斯武装力量起义，推翻俄国沙皇及其政府；俄国爆发第二次革命，导致俄国退出战争

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Central Powers move troops to the Western Front; Allied Forces reinforced by American troops
items.zh: 同盟国调兵前往西线；协约国得到美军增援

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In July 1918, Germans began their final attack of the war in the Second Battle of the Marne.
items.zh: 1918年7月，德军在第二次马恩河战役中发动了战争中的最后进攻。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: On November 11, 1918, the war officially ended with an armistice agreement.
items.zh: 1918年11月11日，战争以停战协定正式结束。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: World War I was fought on land, sea, and in the air; when war declared, Britain had largest navy in the world
items.zh: 第一次世界大战在陆地、海洋和空中展开；战争爆发时，英国拥有世界上最大的海军

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: At the time, World War I (the Great War) was the largest and deadliest war ever fought; lasted from 1914 to 1918; sixteen million soldiers and civilians killed
items.zh: 当时，第一次世界大战（大战）是迄今规模最大、最致命的战争；从1914年持续到1918年；1600万士兵和平民丧生

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Treaty of Versailles, an agreement between the Allied Powers and Germany, officially ended World War I; treaty weakened and punished Germany; Germany forced to accept treaty terms on June 28, 1919; unable to pay vast reparations
items.zh: 《凡尔赛条约》是协约国与德国之间的协议，正式结束了第一次世界大战；该条约削弱并惩罚了德国；德国被迫于1919年6月28日接受条约条款；无力支付巨额赔款

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Full force of industrial economies used to supply massive armies; science, engineering, new technologies, modern weaponry used by both sides; Germany the first to use poison gas; British used a new armored vehicle called a tank
items.zh: 工业经济的全部力量被用于装备庞大军队；双方都使用科学、工程、新技术和现代武器；德国率先使用毒气；英国使用了一种名为坦克的新型装甲车辆

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: At the beginning of World War I, Russia not as industrialized as other powerful nations in Europe
items.zh: 第一次世界大战初期，俄国的工业化程度不如欧洲其他强国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Russia suffered more military deaths in World War I than any other nation.
items.zh: 俄国在第一次世界大战中的军人死亡人数超过任何其他国家。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Russian revolution began because of strikes in the city of Petrograd, (St. Petersburg), and a march led by women on International Women’s Day; Russians were hungry and tired of the war; Soldiers in the city refused to oppose the striking workers
items.zh: 俄国革命起因于彼得格勒（圣彼得堡）的罢工以及国际妇女节当天由妇女领导的游行；俄国人民饥寒交迫且厌倦战争；城中的士兵拒绝镇压罢工的工人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Bands of workers and soldiers formed self-governing groups called soviets; the soviet in Petrograd took over the city
items.zh: 工人和士兵组成名为“苏维埃”的自治团体；彼得格勒的苏维埃接管了该城。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Czar Nicholas II removed; new Provisional Government organized to rule Russia
items.zh: 沙皇尼古拉二世被废黜；新的临时政府成立以统治俄国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Government’s new leader, Aleksandr Kerensky (1881–1970), wrote new laws, including ones that protected freedom of speech and equal rights.
items.zh: 政府新领导人亚历山大·克伦斯基（1881–1970）制定新法律，包括保护言论自由和平等权利的法律。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Riots of hungry workers break out; discontent sparks Bolshevik Revolution on November 6 and 7, 1917.
items.zh: 饥饿的工人爆发骚乱；不满情绪引发了1917年11月6日至7日的布尔什维克革命。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Bolsheviks were a revolutionary communist party; Bolshevik leader, Vladmir Lenin (1870–1924), aimed to overthrow the czar’s regime.
items.zh: 布尔什维克是一个革命性的共产党；布尔什维克领袖弗拉基米尔·列宁（1870–1924）旨在推翻沙皇政权。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Bolsheviks believed in a communist society in which private property is abolished; all people work together to meet society’s needs; Bolsheviks overthrow Provisional Government
items.zh: 布尔什维克信奉消灭私有制的共产主义社会；所有人共同劳动以满足社会需求；布尔什维克推翻临时政府

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Lenin and the Bolsheviks turned the Russian Empire into the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR).
items.zh: 列宁和布尔什维克将俄罗斯帝国变为苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟（苏联）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The USSR became the world’s first communist nation.
items.zh: 苏联成为世界上第一个共产主义国家。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Lenin’s government made a peace deal with Germany in 1918; the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
items.zh: 列宁政府于1918年与德国达成和平协议；即《布列斯特-立陶夫斯克条约》

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Supporters of the czar, the Whites, take up arms; Bolsheviks form the Red Army; Russian Civil War (1918–20) resulted in victory for the Bolsheviks; Czar Nicholas, his wife, and their five children executed by the Bolsheviks in July, 1918; millions of Russians died in the Civil War
items.zh: 沙皇的支持者（白军）拿起武器；布尔什维克组建红军；俄国内战（1918–20）以布尔什维克胜利告终；1918年7月，沙皇尼古拉及其妻子和五个子女被布尔什维克处决；数百万俄国人在内战中丧生

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Europe (France, Belgium, Italy, Austria, Germany, Spain, Great Britain, Lithuania, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Finland, Denmark, Norway, Greece, Russia)
items.zh: 欧洲（法国、比利时、意大利、奥地利、德国、西班牙、英国、立陶宛、爱沙尼亚、波兰、捷克、芬兰、丹麦、挪威、希腊、俄罗斯）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: India
items.zh: 印度

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Pakistan
items.zh: 巴基斯坦

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Africa (Ethiopia, Algeria, Egypt, North Africa)
items.zh: 非洲（埃塞俄比亚、阿尔及利亚、埃及、北非）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Southeast Asia (Philippines)
items.zh: 东南亚（菲律宾）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Asia/East Asia (China, Japan, Korea)
items.zh: 亚洲/东亚（中国、日本、朝鲜）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: North America (California, Hawaii)
items.zh: 北美洲（加利福尼亚、夏威夷）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Atlantic Ocean
items.zh: 大西洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Pacific Ocean
items.zh: 太平洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Indian Ocean
items.zh: 印度洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: World War II and the Postwar World
items.en: Mediterranean Sea B. Globalization World War II (1939–45) was the largest and most destructive conflict in history. Fifty million people died during the war; millions of others were wounded or driven from their homes. Two opposing factions battled around the world for global supremacy. Great Britain and France led the Allied Powers until 1941, when they were joined by the Soviet Union and the United States. The Axis Powers were led by Germany, Italy, and Japan. The stakes of World War II were huge. The very existence of free, tolerant, and democratic nations was threatened, as were the lives of millions.
items.zh: 地中海 B. 全球化 第二次世界大战（1939–45）是历史上规模最大、破坏性最强的冲突。战争中有5000万人死亡；另有数百万人受伤或流离失所。两个敌对阵营在全球争夺世界霸权。英国和法国在1941年前领导协约国，此后苏联和美国加入。轴心国由德国、意大利和日本领导。二战的赌注巨大。自由、宽容和民主国家的生存受到威胁，数百万人的生命同样受到威胁。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Origins of World War II rooted in the ending of World War I; emperor of Germany, Kaiser Wilhelm II, forced to step down as the German leader on November 9, 1918
items.zh: 第二次世界大战的根源在于第一次世界大战的结束；1918年11月9日，德国皇帝威廉二世被迫退位

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: People of Germany proclaimed a new, democratic republic—the Weimar Republic.
items.zh: 德国人民宣布成立新的民主共和国——魏玛共和国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: German economy battered by World War I; new republic owed 132 billion marks to the Allies for damages; Germany’s inability to pay caused political and economic crisis; hyperinflation
items.zh: 德国经济受到一战重创；新共和国欠协约国1320亿马克赔款；德国无力支付引发政治和经济危机；恶性通货膨胀

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Economic and political crises prompted people to take extreme political options.
items.zh: 经济和政治危机促使人们采取极端的政治选择。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Far-right leader, Adolf Hitler (1889–1945) joined the German Worker’s Party in 1919; party name changed to the National Socialist German Worker’s Party; became known as Nazis; by 1921, Hitler leader of Nazis; saw real Socialists as enemies
items.zh: 极右翼领袖阿道夫·希特勒（1889–1945）于1919年加入德国工人党；该党改名为德国国家社会主义工人党；即纳粹党；到1921年，希特勒成为纳粹党领袖；将真正的社会主义者视为敌人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hitler and followers tried to seize control of the government of Bavaria; Hitler arrested, tried, and jailed for nine months; in jail Hitler writes Mein Kampf, or My Struggle; described his hatred of Jewish people; outlined the destiny of the “master race”
items.zh: 希特勒及其追随者试图夺取巴伐利亚政府的控制权；希特勒被捕、受审并监禁九个月；在狱中，希特勒写下《我的奋斗》（Mein Kampf）；描述了他对犹太人的仇恨；勾勒了“优等种族”的命运

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hitler wanted to reunite Germany with territories it had lost and with other German speaking nations; wanted Germany to expand eastward; called for Lebensraum, a country for “pure” Germans
items.zh: 希特勒希望将德国失去的领土和其他德语国家重新统一；希望德国向东扩张；呼吁建立“生存空间”（Lebensraum），即“纯种”德国人的国家

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hitler wanted to remove multiple groups from Germany, including Jews, Roma, people with disabilities, communists, and anyone considered the enemy of the state.
items.zh: 希特勒想将多个群体从德国清除，包括犹太人、罗姆人、残障人士、共产党人以及任何被视为国家敌人的人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The ideology of fascism, which Hitler followed, promotes the supremacy of the nation state and its primary ethnic group above all else.
items.zh: 希特勒奉行的法西斯主义意识形态，宣扬民族国家及其主要族群至高无上。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hitler elected to the parliament of the Weimar Republic, the Reichstag, in 1932
items.zh: 1932年，希特勒当选为魏玛共和国议会（帝国国会）议员

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: U.S. stock market crashed in October 1929; resulting global economic depression hit Germany hard; U.S. government demanded money owed by Germany be repaid; German banks failed and economy crumbled
items.zh: 1929年10月美国股市崩盘；由此引发的全球经济大萧条重创德国；美国政府要求德国偿还欠款；德国银行倒闭，经济崩溃

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1933, Hitler named chancellor of the Weimar Republic
items.zh: 1933年，希特勒被任命为魏玛共和国总理

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hitler put the constitution of the Weimar Republic on hold; stripped citizens of their legal rights; proclaimed Germany to be the Third Reich; took direct control of education, the economy, and the legal system
items.zh: 希特勒搁置魏玛共和国宪法；剥夺公民的法律权利；宣布德国为第三帝国；直接控制教育、经济和司法体系

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hitler proclaimed himself Führer (leader) of Germany in 1934.
items.zh: 1934年，希特勒自封为德国元首（Führer）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hitler’s government used a mixture of laws and direct intimidation and violence to attack Jewish people and strip them of their rights and property.
items.zh: 希特勒政府通过法律和直接恐吓、暴力相结合的方式攻击犹太人，剥夺他们的权利和财产。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: November 9–10, 1938, Kristallnacht
items.zh: 1938年11月9日至10日，水晶之夜（Kristallnacht）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Benito Mussolini (1853–1945) ruled Italy from 1922 until 1943; authoritarian dictatorship; political ideology of Fascism established in Italy
items.zh: 贝尼托·墨索里尼（1853–1945）于1922年至1943年统治意大利；实行威权独裁；在意大利建立了法西斯主义政治意识形态

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Armed gangs of Fascists, called Blackshirts, maintained order.
items.zh: 被称为“黑衫军”的法西斯武装团伙维持秩序。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Timeline
items.zh: 时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mussolini’s government shared several Nazi ideals; hatred of democracy; belief in strong nationalism; used propaganda and education to promote ideology
items.zh: 墨索里尼政府与纳粹有若干共同理念；憎恨民主；信奉强烈的民族主义；利用宣传和教育推广意识形态

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Italy invaded the African nation of Ethiopia.
items.zh: 意大利入侵非洲国家埃塞俄比亚。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1939, Mussolini and Hitler signed the Pact of Steel; Italy and Germany agreed to support one another in event of war
items.zh: 1939年，墨索里尼和希特勒签署《钢铁条约》；意大利和德国同意在战争爆发时相互支持

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Josef Stalin (1878–1953), leader of the Soviet Union before and during World War II
items.zh: 约瑟夫·斯大林（1878–1953），二战前及二战期间苏联的领导人

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Stalin wanted to end capitalism in the Soviet Union; wanted the Soviet Union to be an industrial power; ordered farms to be collectivized
items.zh: 斯大林希望在苏联消灭资本主义；希望苏联成为工业强国；下令将农场集体化

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: To build up industry, Stalin set high expectations for workers; those who failed, as well as political prisoners, sent to brutal work camps called gulags
items.zh: 为发展工业，斯大林对工人提出极高要求；未能达标者以及政治犯被送往名为古拉格的残酷劳改营

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Stalin understood the Nazi threat to Russia; to gain time and build up Soviet industry and armed forces, signed a peace deal with Germany
items.zh: 斯大林认识到纳粹对俄国的威胁；为争取时间发展苏联工业和武装力量，与德国签署和平协议

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Countries at War Before World War II
items.en: Spain, China, and Japan were already involved in their own wars when World War II began in September, 1939.
items.zh: 1939年9月二战爆发时，西班牙、中国和日本已卷入各自的战争。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Countries at War Before World War II
items.en: Spanish Civil War: Hitler and Mussolini supported Spanish nationalists; Stalin supported Spanish Republicans
items.zh: 西班牙内战：希特勒和墨索里尼支持西班牙民族主义者；斯大林支持西班牙共和派。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Countries at War Before World War II
items.en: Francisco Franco became dictator of Spain; ruled until his death in 1975.
items.zh: 弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥成为西班牙独裁者；统治至1975年去世。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: Countries at War Before World War II
items.en: Japan invaded China in 1931, taking control of Manchuria; by 1937, war had broken out between both countries.
items.zh: 日本于1931年入侵中国，控制满洲；到1937年，两国间全面战争爆发。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: German annexation of Austria in March, 1938
items.zh: 1938年3月德国吞并奥地利

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: Initial policy of appeasement in relation to German expansion
items.zh: 对德国扩张初期采取的绥靖政策

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: In 1938, Germany, Italy, Great Britain, and France agree that Czechoslovakia must give up the Sudetenland to Germany; Germany invades rest of Czechoslovakia in March, 1939
items.zh: 1938年，德国、意大利、英国和法国同意捷克斯洛伐克必须将苏台德地区割让给德国；1939年3月，德国入侵捷克斯洛伐克其余地区

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: Germany invades Poland from west on September 1, 1939
items.zh: 1939年9月1日，德国从西部入侵波兰

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: France and Great Britain declared war on Germany on September 3, 1939; Allied Powers (France, Great Britain, United States, Soviet Union, China); Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, Japan)
items.zh: 1939年9月3日，法国和英国对德国宣战；协约国（法国、英国、美国、苏联、中国）；轴心国（德国、意大利、日本）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: Soviet Union invaded Poland from east; Stalin and Hitler agree to divide Poland between their two nations; Hitler allows Soviet Union to claim Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, and occupation of southeastern Finland
items.zh: 苏联从东部入侵波兰；斯大林和希特勒同意两国瓜分波兰；希特勒允许苏联占领立陶宛、拉脱维亚、爱沙尼亚，并占领芬兰东南部

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: German invasions of western Europe used new equipment and tactics; fast armored tanks helped Germany employ a military tactic called Blitzkrieg (lightning war).
items.zh: 德国入侵西欧时使用了新装备和新战术；快速装甲坦克使德国得以采用一种名为闪电战（Blitzkrieg）的军事战术。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: France had largest army in Europe at start of World War II
items.zh: 二战开始时，法国拥有欧洲最大的军队

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: Germany invades and captures Denmark and Norway, April, 1940
items.zh: 1940年4月，德国入侵并占领丹麦和挪威

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: German forces invade France; enter Paris on June 14, 1940; French government surrenders; France divided into two territories
items.zh: 德军入侵法国；1940年6月14日进入巴黎；法国政府投降；法国被分为两个区域

items.subject: History and Geography
items.subtopic: German Expansion and Beginning of World War II
items.en: Battle of Britain
items.zh: 不列颠之战

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Germany invades Soviet Union in June, 1941.
items.zh: 1941年6月，德国入侵苏联。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Battle of Stalingrad (1942–1943); one of largest battles in history; ultimately first major defeat for Germany
items.zh: 斯大林格勒战役（1942–1943）；历史上规模最大的战役之一；最终成为德国的首次重大失败

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: British, French, German, and Italian forces engaged in battles in North Africa.
items.zh: 英国、法国、德国和意大利军队在北非交战。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In July, 1942, British and German forces clash in El Alamein, Egypt; Germans defeated
items.zh: 1942年7月，英军与德军在埃及阿拉曼交战；德军战败

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In November, 1942, Britain and US forces reclaim areas under German control; by summer 1943, German and Italian forces in Africa completely defeated
items.zh: 1942年11月，英美军收复德国控制区；到1943年夏，非洲的德意军队被彻底击败

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: At first, many Jewish people sent to labor camps; in 1942, Nazis leaders set in motion plan to kill Jewish people en masse; concentration camps set up to do so; “final solution”
items.zh: 起初，许多犹太人被送往劳改营；1942年，纳粹领导人启动大规模屠杀犹太人的计划；为此建立集中营；即“最终解决方案”

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Six million Jewish people killed in the Holocaust
items.zh: 600万犹太人在大屠杀中遇害

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1943, Great Britain, the Soviet Union, and the United States signed the Moscow Declaration of German Atrocities; the nations pledged to punish Germany for the crimes it committed during the Holocaust.
items.zh: 1943年，英国、苏联和美国签署《莫斯科关于德国暴行的宣言》；各国承诺惩治德国在大屠杀中所犯的罪行。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The United States entered World War II in December, 1941, after Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.
items.zh: 1941年12月日本袭击珍珠港后，美国加入第二次世界大战。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Allied leaders developed Operation Overlord, a plan to invade German-occupied France from Great Britain; Allied troops would cross the English Channel and land on French shores; U.S. general Dwight Eisenhower led the operation
items.zh: 盟军领导制定了“霸王行动”（Operation Overlord），即从英国进攻德占法国的计划；盟军将横渡英吉利海峡，在法国海岸登陆；美军将领德怀特·艾森豪威尔领导此次行动

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Allied troops invaded German-occupied France on June 6, 1944, also known as D-Day.
items.zh: 1944年6月6日，盟军进攻德占法国，即诺曼底登陆日（D-Day）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Paris liberated from Nazi occupation on August 25, 1944
items.zh: 1944年8月25日，巴黎从纳粹占领下解放

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Battle of the Bulge (1944–1945); Germany loses; Allied troops begin march to Berlin, Germany
items.zh: 阿登战役（1944—1945）；德国战败；盟军开始向德国柏林进军。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Stalin, Churchill, and Roosevelt meet at the Russian town of Yalta in February 1945; agree that Soviet Union could ensure eastern Europe establishes governments friendly to the Soviet Union; Soviet Union agrees to free elections in those countries; France to take part in German occupation
items.zh: 1945年2月，斯大林、丘吉尔和罗斯福在俄国小镇雅尔塔会晤；同意苏联可以确保东欧建立对苏友好的政府；苏联同意在这些国家举行自由选举；法国参与对德国的占领

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Soviet Union agrees to enter war in the Pacific to help defeat China in exchange for Japan’s territory in China.
items.zh: 苏联同意参加太平洋战争以帮助击败中国，以换取日本在中国的领土。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: With Allied troops closing in on Berlin, Hitler and his closest advisors fled to an underground bunker; on April 30, 1945, Hitler committed suicide.
items.zh: 随着盟军逼近柏林，希特勒及其最亲密的顾问逃入地下掩体；1945年4月30日，希特勒自杀。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Nazis finally surrendered to the Soviet army in Berlin on May 8, 1945; this date is celebrated as Victory in Europe Day, or V-E Day.
items.zh: 1945年5月8日，纳粹最终在柏林向苏军投降；这一天被定为欧洲胜利日（V-E Day）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In April 1942, American and Filipino soldiers on the Bataan Peninsula, Philippines, defeated by the Japanese; resulted in the Bataan Death March
items.zh: 1942年4月，菲律宾巴丹半岛上的美军和菲军被日军击败；导致巴丹死亡行军

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Battle of Midway, June 3–6, 1942, helped slow Japan’s takeover of the Pacific
items.zh: 1942年6月3日至6日的中途岛海战遏制了日本对太平洋的侵占

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Japan captured Guadalcanal on July 6, 1942, and began building an air force base.
items.zh: 1942年7月6日，日军占领瓜达尔卡纳尔岛，并开始修建空军基地。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: American troops landed on Guadalcanal on August 7; six-month battle resulted in American control of the island
items.zh: 美军于8月7日登陆瓜达尔卡纳尔岛；历时六个月的战斗使美军控制了该岛。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Allies attacked Iwo Jima, site of crucial Japanese military base, by air and by sea on February 19, 1945
items.zh: 1945年2月19日，盟军对日本重要军事基地所在地硫磺岛发动海空攻击

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: On August 6, 1945, the United States dropped a nuclear bomb on the Japanese city of Hiroshima; three days later, after the Japanese government refused to surrender, the United States dropped a nuclear bomb on the city of Nagasaki.
items.zh: 1945年8月6日，美国向日本广岛投下核弹；三天后，因日本政府拒绝投降，美国向长崎投下核弹。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Japan surrendered on September 2, 1945; the Second World War ended.
items.zh: 1945年9月2日，日本投降；第二次世界大战结束。

items.subject: History and Geography
