items.en: On August 1, 1945, the leaders of Great Britain, the Soviet Union, and the United States announced the Potsdam Agreement; Germany split into four occupation zones, with France, Great Britain, the Soviet Union, and the United States each overseeing one zone;
items.zh: 1945年8月1日，英国、苏联和美国领导人宣布《波茨坦协定》；德国被分为四个占领区，由法国、英国、苏联和美国各管辖一个区；

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The peacemaking process with Japan was led by the United States; Japan’s emperor allowed to remain in power, but he had to declare that he was not a god; the United States helped establish a democracy and put into place a new constitution that established a House of Representatives elected by both men and women
items.zh: 对日本的和平进程由美国主导；日本天皇被允许继续在位，但必须声明自己不是神；美国帮助建立民主制度，并颁布新宪法，设立由男女共同选举产生的众议院

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Led by U.S. president Franklin Roosevelt and British prime minister Winston Churchill, the Allied nations signed the Atlantic Charter in 1941; this document calls for nations to cooperate to ensure world peace; the organization known as the United Nations was born in 1945 with the UN Charter
items.zh: 在美国总统富兰克林·罗斯福和英国首相温斯顿·丘吉尔的领导下，同盟国于1941年签署《大西洋宪章》；该文件呼吁各国合作以确保世界和平；1945年，《联合国宪章》签署，联合国组织诞生

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The General Assembly created; a legislature made up of representatives from nations around the world; five most powerful Allied nations—China, France, Great Britain, the Soviet Union, and the United States—were made permanent members of the Security Council, which would also have rotating representation from smaller nations
items.zh: 设立联合国大会；由世界各国代表组成的立法机构；五个最强大的同盟国——中国、法国、英国、苏联和美国——成为安理会常任理事国，安理会还有来自小国的轮任代表

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1948, the UN created the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
items.zh: 1948年，联合国通过《世界人权宣言》。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mohandas Gandhi (1869–1948) leader of Indian Congress Party; Indian independence negotiated in 1947; resulted in creation of two nations—India and Pakistan
items.zh: 莫汉达斯·甘地（1869–1948），印度国大党领袖；1947年谈判达成印度独立；由此产生两个国家——印度和巴基斯坦

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1917, Great Britain issued the Balfour Declaration, which formalized the British government’s support for the creation of a national home for Jewish people in Palestine.
items.zh: 1917年，英国发表《贝尔福宣言》，正式表示英国政府支持在巴勒斯坦为犹太人建立民族家园。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Soviet Union and the United States emerged as the world’s superpowers.
items.zh: 苏联和美国成为世界超级大国。

items.zh: 东亚和东南亚

items.zh: 中国

items.zh: 太平洋

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: Sea of Japan (East Sea) B. Globalization Communist governments rose to power in several Southeast Asian countries after World War II. Communist ideals appealed to people who had experienced little opportunity under the colonial system in Southeast Asia. Others in those countries, however, rejected communism and actively fought against it. Wars in Southeast Asia became theaters of conflict in the Cold War.
items.zh: 日本海（东海）B. 全球化 二战后，东南亚数国的共产党政府上台执政。共产主义理想吸引了那些在东南亚殖民制度下几乎没有任何机会的人们。然而，这些国家中另一些人拒绝共产主义并积极与之抗争。东南亚的战争成为冷战的冲突舞台。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: Inspired by the ideas of Marx and Lenin, the Chinese Communist Party was formed; Mao Zedong was a leading member.
items.zh: 在马克思和列宁思想的启发下，中国共产党成立；毛泽东是主要成员之一。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: Outbreak of Chinese Civil War (1927–1949) in which National Party and Communist Party opposed each other
items.zh: 国共内战（1927–1949）爆发，国民党与共产党相互对抗

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: Jiang Jieshi leader of the Nationalist Party
items.zh: 蒋介石为国民党领袖

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: Mao became the leader of the Communist Party; led his army on the longest wartime military march ever recorded (the Long March).
items.zh: 毛泽东成为共产党领袖；率领军队进行了有记录以来最长的战时行军（长征）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: Chinese Civil War paused in 1937; Nationalists and Communists united to fight expansionist aggression from Japan. Timeline
items.zh: 国共内战于1937年暂停；国民党与共产党联合抗击日本的扩张侵略。时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: Major part of World War II in Asia, the Second Sino-Japanese War, began with attacks on Chinese cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, and Nanjing; alliance between Nationalists and Communists continued through World War II; the civil war resumed after 1945
items.zh: 二战在亚洲的主要部分——抗日战争（第二次中日战争）——以日军进攻北京、上海和南京等中国城市开始；国共联盟在二战期间持续；1945年后内战重启

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: After four years of post–World War II fighting, Mao’s forces won; declared China to be the People’s Republic of China
items.zh: 经过二战后四年的战斗，毛泽东的军队获胜；宣布中国为中华人民共和国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: East and Southeast Asia in the Second Half of Twentieth Century
items.en: Jiang’s Nationalists fled to the island of Taiwan; set up an anti-communist, authoritarian government and continued calling it the Republic of China
items.zh: 蒋介石的国民党逃往台湾岛；建立了反共的威权政府，并继续称其为中华民国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mao remakes China into a communist nation; seized lands from private ownership; collectivization; forced increase of coal mining and steel production.
items.zh: 毛泽东将中国改造为共产主义国家；没收私人土地；实行集体化；强制增加煤炭开采和钢铁生产。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Communist Party outlawed Confucianism, Buddhism, Christianity, and other religions.
items.zh: 共产党取缔儒教、佛教、基督教及其他宗教。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Implementation of the Great Leap Forward in late 1950s; five-year plan; use of untested methods in irrigation and farming; people forced to join communes; crop yields fell; millions of people died during period of famine; changes in industrial production also failed; five-year plan halted after three years
items.zh: 20世纪50年代末实施“大跃进”；五年计划；在灌溉和农业中采用未经检验的方法；人们被迫加入公社；粮食产量下降；数百万人在饥荒期间死亡；工业生产改革也告失败；五年计划三年后中止

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mao resigned as chairman of the People’s Republic of China; remained chairman of the Chinese Communist Party, a more powerful role than chairman of the country
items.zh: 毛泽东辞去中华人民共和国主席职务；仍担任中国共产党主席，这一职务比国家主席权力更大。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mao embarked on the Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution; aimed to defeat enemies and remake Chinese society; schools closed; young people told to speak out against bourgeois values and the people who represented them; youths organized into paramilitary groups called the Red Guards; Red Guards dispersed to rural areas
items.zh: 毛泽东发动“无产阶级文化大革命”；旨在击败敌人并改造中国社会；学校停课；年轻人被鼓动公开反对资产阶级价值观及其代表者；青年被组织成名为红卫兵的准军事团体；红卫兵被派往农村

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Lin Biao named as Mao’s successor; Lin Biao and other military leaders planned coup to unseat Mao; Lin Biao died in 1971; Mao dies in 1976
items.zh: 林彪被指定为毛泽东的接班人；林彪和其他军队领导人策划政变推翻毛泽东；林彪于1971年身亡；毛泽东于1976年去世

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Starting in 1977, Mao’s successor, Deng Xiaoping, favored allowing more free market practices to guide China’s development; he led the country for the next twenty years, opening its market to trade with the United States and other Western countries; allowed more personal liberty; quashed democratic movements
items.zh: 自1977年起，毛泽东的接班人邓小平主张允许更多自由市场做法来引导中国发展；他在接下来的二十年里领导国家，向美国和其他西方国家开放市场进行贸易；允许更多个人自由；镇压民主运动

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1989, students gathered in Beijing’s Tiananmen Square to peacefully demonstrate for greater freedom; Deng sent in military forces to control the crowd; hundreds of peaceful demonstrators killed
items.zh: 1989年，学生聚集在北京天安门广场，和平示威争取更大自由；邓派军队控制人群；数百名和平示威者丧生

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: China became the largest manufacturing country and the second-largest economy in the world.
items.zh: 中国成为世界第一大制造国和第二大经济体。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After its World War II defeat, Japan surrendered Korea, which it had occupied since the early 1900s, to the Soviet Union and the United States; the Soviets occupied the northern half; the United States took control of the southern half
items.zh: 二战后战败，日本将自20世纪初以来占领的朝鲜交给苏联和美国；苏联占领北半部；美国控制南半部

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: By the end of the 1940s, the North was a communist country and the South was an anti communist nation; both led by dictators
items.zh: 到20世纪40年代末，北方成为共产主义国家，南方成为反共国家；两国均由独裁者领导

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1950, North Korean leader Kim Il-sung sent troops to invade South Korea; North Korean troops, with the support of the Soviet Union, quickly conquered almost all the peninsula.
items.zh: 1950年，朝鲜领导人金日成派兵入侵韩国；在苏联支持下，朝鲜军队迅速占领了几乎整个半岛。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The United Nations sent military forces to assist South Korea; mostly American troops led by United States general Douglas MacArthur
items.zh: 联合国派兵援助韩国；主要是美军，由美国将领道格拉斯·麦克阿瑟指挥

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Concerned UN forces might cross the border, Mao Zedong sent Chinese troops to assist the North Koreans; by early 1951, the communists had pushed UN forces back to the thirty-eighth parallel
items.zh: 由于担心联合国军越过边境，毛泽东派中国军队援助朝鲜；到1951年初，共产党军队已将联合国军逼回三八线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1953, two sides agreed to a cease-fire; South Korea, which encompassed all Korean territory south of the thirty-eighth parallel, continued to be a key ally of the United States in East Asia; North Korea, called the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, remained communist; both Koreas were simultaneously admitted to the United Nations in 1991
items.zh: 1953年，双方同意停火；韩国（涵盖三八线以南所有朝鲜领土）继续成为美国在东亚的重要盟友；朝鲜（称朝鲜民主主义人民共和国）保持共产主义；1991年，朝韩两国同时加入联合国

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: First president of South Korea, Syngman Rhee, was anti-communist, but an authoritarian; political and economic instability caused by growing opposition forced Rhee out of power in 1960.
items.zh: 韩国首任总统李承晚反对共产主义，但实行威权统治；日益壮大的反对派引发政治和经济动荡，迫使李承晚于1960年下台。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Land reforms approved during Rhee’s reign opened property ownership to more people and helped create strong economic growth from the 1960s onward; population boomed; more people gained an education; a middle class emerged; growth of urbanization; enormous population growth of South Korea’s capital, Seoul
items.zh: 李承晚执政期间通过的土地改革使更多人获得土地所有权，并助力20世纪60年代以来的强劲经济增长；人口激增；更多人接受教育；中产阶级出现；城市化发展；韩国首都首尔人口急剧增长

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: People of South Korea lived under repressive rule for decades; South Koreans directly elected a president for the first time in 1987.
items.zh: 韩国人民在高压统治下生活了数十年；1987年，韩国人首次直接选举总统。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1988, the Olympic Games were held in Seoul; changed the world view of South Korea
items.zh: 1988年，奥运会在首尔举行；改变了世界对韩国的看法。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Today, South Korea is one of the ten largest economies in the world.
items.zh: 如今，韩国是世界十大经济体之一。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Dictator Kim Il-sung continued to rule North Korea after the Korean War.
items.zh: 独裁者金日成在朝鲜战争后继续统治朝鲜。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Propaganda glorified Kim as the “Great Leader”; he isolated North Korea from the rest of the world.
items.zh: 宣传将金日成美化成“伟大领袖”；他使朝鲜与世界隔绝。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kim Il-sung died in 1994; he was replaced by his son Kim Jong-il; collapse of Soviet Union impacted North Korea’s economy; economic hardship and starvation
items.zh: 金日成于1994年去世；由其子金正日接替；苏联解体影响了朝鲜经济；经济困难和饥荒随之而来

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kim Jong-il died in 2011; replaced by his son Kim Jong-un
items.zh: 金正日于2011年去世；由其子金正恩接替

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Vietnam became a colony of France in the late 1800s; after World War II, communist Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh led an independence movement to end French rule; during the war, Ho led opposition forces in the use of guerilla tactics against occupying Japanese troops
items.zh: 19世纪末越南成为法国殖民地；二战后，越南共产党领袖胡志明领导独立运动以结束法国统治；战争期间，胡志明领导反抗力量使用游击战术对抗占领的日军

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1954, Ho’s forces defeated the French at the Battle of Dien Bien Phu; France withdrew and Vietnam gained independence.
items.zh: 1954年，胡志明的军队在奠边府战役中击败法军；法国撤出，越南获得独立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Vietnam split into two countries; communist government in the North; anti-communist government in the South; leaders from both agreed to hold elections to reunite Vietnam; not supported by United States; in 1959, Ho Chi Minh and North Korea declared war on South Korea
items.zh: 越南分裂为两国；北方为共产主义政府；南方为反共政府；双方领导人同意举行选举以统一越南；但美国不支持；1959年，胡志明和朝鲜对韩国宣战

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: United States viewed Vietnam as part of larger Cold War struggle against communism; U.S. president Dwight Eisenhower believed that the fall of Vietnam to communists would lead to the spread of communism across Southeast Asia
items.zh: 美国将越南视为更大的反共冷战斗争的一部分；美国总统德怀特·艾森豪威尔认为，越南落入共产党之手将导致共产主义在东南亚蔓延

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: U.S. Congress sent hundreds of millions of dollars to help the South Vietnamese government of Ngo Dinh Diem fight communist guerillas (Viet Cong).
items.zh: 美国国会拨款数亿美元，帮助吴廷琰的南越政府对抗共产党游击队（越共）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1964, the United States’ involvement increased in 1964; an American warship in the Gulf of Tonkin reported it had been attacked by the North Vietnamese (Historians now accept that this attack never happened).
items.zh: 1964年，美国的介入加深；一艘美国军舰在北部湾报告称遭到北越攻击（历史学家现在认为这次攻击并未发生）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: U.S. forces began bombing North Vietnam.
items.zh: 美军开始轰炸北越。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In January 1968, the Viet Cong launched the Tet Offensive; series of attacks on South Vietnamese cities conducted during Tet, the Vietnamese new year
items.zh: 1968年1月，越共发动春节攻势；在越南新年（春节）期间对南越城市发动一系列袭击。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: American soldiers brutally killed and tortured more than five hundred people in the My Lai massacre; public opinion in the United States began to turn against the war
items.zh: 美军士兵在美莱村大屠杀中残酷杀害和折磨了五百多人；美国舆论开始转向反对这场战争

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: President Lyndon Johnson succeeded by Richard Nixon in 1968
items.zh: 1968年，理查德·尼克松接替林登·约翰逊总统

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Cease-fire agreement finally reached in1973; the United States began to pull its troops out of Vietnam; two years later, the South Vietnamese capital of Saigon fell to communist forces; North and South Vietnam united under communist rule
items.zh: 1973年终于达成停火协议；美国开始从越南撤军；两年后，南越首都西贡被共产党军队攻占；北越和南越在共产主义统治下统一

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Saigon renamed Ho Chi Minh City
items.zh: 西贡更名为胡志明市

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Many Vietnamese people who opposed communism fled the country.
items.zh: 许多反对共产主义的越南人逃离该国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Vietnam opened its doors to Western countries in 1986. H. Japan
items.zh: 越南于1986年向西方国家开放。H. 日本

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After World War II, the Allies placed Japan under military occupation for seven years; occupation largely directed by the United State under leadership of General Douglas MacArthur
items.zh: 二战后，盟军对日本实行了七年军事占领；占领主要由美国在道格拉斯·麦克阿瑟将军的领导下主导

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: During the occupation, the political system of Japan was transformed; new constitution included a bill of rights that said the country would no longer maintain a military, except for self-defense
items.zh: 占领期间，日本的政治体制被改造；新宪法包含权利法案，规定除自卫外，日本不再维持军队

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Land reforms included the transfer of ownership of farmland from landlords to farmers, ended last remnants of feudal system
items.zh: 土地改革包括将农田所有权从地主转移给农民，终结了封建制度的最后残余

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Workers granted more rights; establishment of unions; women granted right to vote; academic freedom guaranteed
items.zh: 工人获得更多权利；建立工会；妇女获得选举权；保障学术自由

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Population moved from countryside to cities such as Tokyo
items.zh: 人口从农村迁往东京等城市

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Economy of Japan experienced rapid growth as mechanization led to greater efficiencies in industry and agriculture; huge success producing goods for export such as cars, cameras, and televisions
items.zh: 随着机械化提高工业和农业效率，日本经济快速增长；汽车、相机和电视等出口商品的生产取得巨大成功

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Japan experienced recession and recovery; remains one of world’s economic powerhouses
items.zh: 日本经历了经济衰退与复苏；仍是世界经济强国之一

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Europe in the Second Half of the Twentieth Century
items.en: Europe
items.zh: 欧洲

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Europe in the Second Half of the Twentieth Century
items.en: Balkans
items.zh: 巴尔干地区

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Europe in the Second Half of the Twentieth Century
items.en: Russia, Great Britain, Germany, France, Belgium, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Greece, Estonia, Armenia, Belarus, Albania, Bulgaria, Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Slovenia, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Ireland, Northern Ireland

items.subject: History and Geography
items.topic: Europe in the Second Half of the Twentieth Century
items.en: Canada B. Globalization The end of World War II did not mean the end of conflict and competition in Europe. After the war’s end, the clash of ideas between democratic capitalism and authoritarian communism threatened to plunge Europe into another conflict. The next forty-five years were characterized by a long-simmering tension between two armed camps. The Cold War shaped European politics through the early 1990s, and its consequences are still seen to this day.
items.zh: 加拿大 B. 全球化 第二次世界大战的结束并不意味着欧洲冲突与竞争的终结。战后，民主资本主义与极权共产主义之间的思想冲突有可能将欧洲再次拖入冲突。此后的四十五年里，两大武装阵营之间长期酝酿着紧张局势。冷战一直影响到20世纪90年代初的欧洲政治，其后果至今仍可见。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In eastern Europe, after World War II, local communist parties gained support among the citizens.
items.zh: 二战后在东欧，当地共产党在民众中获得了支持。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Western nations feared communist revolutions in Western countries; Western leaders, especially in the United States, viewed rebuilding Europe as way to counter the threat of communism
items.zh: 西方国家担心西方国家发生共产主义革命；西方领导人，尤其是美国领导人，将重建欧洲视为抵御共产主义威胁的一种方式。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Czechoslovak Communist Party won 39 percent of the vote in 1946 elections; seized full control in 1948; arrested their political opponents; Czechoslovakia fully under Soviet control
items.zh: 捷克斯洛伐克共产党在1946年选举中获得39%的选票；1948年夺取全部控制权；逮捕政治对手；捷克斯洛伐克完全处于苏联控制之下。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Several countries, such as Estonia and Belarus, fully absorbed into Soviet Union
items.zh: 爱沙尼亚和白俄罗斯等数个国家被完全并入苏联。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1948, President Truman established the European Recovery Program, (the Marshall Plan), named for Truman’s secretary of state, George C. Marshall (1880–1959). Timeline
items.zh: 1948年，杜鲁门总统设立了欧洲复兴计划（即马歇尔计划），以杜鲁门的国务卿乔治·C·马歇尔（1880–1959）的名字命名。时间线

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: European countries that took aid from the program saw their gross domestic product (GDP) grow during the three and a half years the Marshall Plan was in effect.
items.zh: 接受该计划援助的欧洲国家，在马歇尔计划实施的三年半期间，其国内生产总值（GDP）均有增长。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In the West, in 1946, British leader Winston Churchill said that an “iron curtain” had been lowered across Europe, along the borders of the region under Soviet control; wanted western European and American leaders to strengthen themselves politically and militarily
items.zh: 在西方，1946年英国领导人温斯顿·丘吉尔称，一道“铁幕”已沿着苏联控制区的边界横跨欧洲降落；他希望西欧和美国领导人在政治和军事上加强自身。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Stalin blamed World War II on problems within and between capitalist countries; argued that war was inevitable as long as capitalism existed; believed capitalist competition led to constant struggle for resources and caused “uneven development”
items.zh: 斯大林将第二次世界大战归咎于资本主义国家内部及彼此之间的问题；认为只要资本主义存在，战争就不可避免；相信资本主义竞争导致对资源的持续争夺，并造成“发展不平衡”。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Germany reflected this divide; had been divided in half by the occupying Allies; West Germany, officially known as the Federal Republic of Germany, was democratic, capitalist; East Germany, or the German Democratic Republic, was communist and part of the Soviet alliance
items.zh: 德国体现了这种分裂；它被占领的盟国一分为二；西德，正式名称为德意志联邦共和国，是民主、资本主义的；东德，即德意志民主共和国，是共产主义国家，属于苏联阵营。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1948, the Western alliance of the United States, Great Britain, and France began to plan a new West German state; began issuing deutsche marks in West Berlin; Soviet leaders, were not been consulted; responded by setting up a blockade of West Berlin; Western nations flew large quantities of food and supplies over East German territory to Berlin; blockaded East Germany; blockades lifted in 1949
items.zh: 1948年，由美国、英国和法国组成的西方联盟开始筹划建立一个新的西德国家；开始在西柏林发行德国马克；苏联领导人并未被征询意见；作为回应，他们对西柏林实行封锁；西方国家经由东德领空向柏林空运大量食品和物资；并对东德实行封锁；封锁于1949年解除。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1949, creation of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), a formal military alliance among the Western allied nations
items.zh: 1949年，成立北大西洋公约组织（北约），这是西方盟国之间的正式军事联盟。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Communist countries of eastern Europe entered a similar agreement in 1955; the Warsaw Treaty Organization, or Warsaw Pact, originally consisted of Albania, Bulgaria, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Poland, Romania, and the Soviet Union.
items.zh: 东欧的共产主义国家于1955年签订了类似的协定；华沙条约组织，即华约，最初由阿尔巴尼亚、保加利亚、捷克斯洛伐克、匈牙利、波兰、罗马尼亚和苏联组成。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After the United States bombed Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, the Soviets launched a special project to develop nuclear technology; achieved success in 1949; other world powers joined the atomic race; Great Britain conducted its first nuclear test in 1952; France followed in 1960
items.zh: 1945年8月美国轰炸广岛和长崎后，苏联启动了一项发展核技术的特别工程；1949年取得成功；其他世界大国也加入了核竞赛；英国于1952年进行了首次核试验；法国于1960年紧随其后。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: One rationale behind the development of nuclear weapons was deterrence.
items.zh: 发展核武器的一个基本理由就是威慑。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Tense first phase of the Cold War ended with the death of Joseph Stalin on March 5, 1953; Stalin’s successor, Nikita Khrushchev (1894–1971)
items.zh: 冷战紧张的第一阶段随着约瑟夫·斯大林于1953年3月5日去世而结束；斯大林的继任者是尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫（1894–1971）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1956, Hungarian prime minister Imre Nagy (1896–1958) declared that non-Communists would be allowed to participate in running the government; also declared Hungary’s neutrality in the contest between West and East; the Soviets invaded Hungary
items.zh: 1956年，匈牙利总理纳吉·伊姆雷（1896–1958）宣布允许非共产党人参与政府管理；还宣布匈牙利在东西方对抗中保持中立；苏联出兵入侵匈牙利。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Construction of the Berlin Wall in 1961
items.zh: 1961年修建柏林墙。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Baby boom of the postwar period, especially large number of births from 1945 to 1952, added millions of young people to Europe.
items.zh: 战后时期的婴儿潮，尤其是1945年至1952年间的大量出生，使欧洲增加了数百万年轻人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Advertising, pop culture, and social events targeted young adults, viewed as the leaders of new cultural and social moment
items.zh: 广告、流行文化和社会活动都以年轻人为目标，他们被视为新文化和社会运动的引领者。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Youth culture and youth politics; in May 1968, a French student-led protest became an uprising that included participants from across society; in 1968, citizens of Czechoslovakia rose up during a period called the Prague Spring; Soviet troops and their allies invaded Czechoslovakia on August 20–21, 1968
items.zh: 青年文化与青年政治；1968年5月，法国一场由学生主导的抗议演变成有社会各界人士参与的起义；1968年，捷克斯洛伐克公民在被称为“布拉格之春”的时期奋起反抗；苏联军队及其盟友于1968年8月20日至21日入侵捷克斯洛伐克。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: European economic boom led to the rise of European welfare states, in which governments provided benefits such as free university education, free health care, and generous pensions; Great Britain established the National Health Service to provide health care to all citizens.
items.zh: 欧洲经济繁荣促成了欧洲福利国家的兴起，政府提供免费大学教育、免费医疗和丰厚养老金等福利；英国建立了国民保健署（National Health Service），为全体公民提供医疗服务。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: From 1968 to 1998, a conflict called the Troubles erupted in the six counties of Northern Ireland (part of Great Britain); unionist and republican paramilitaries fought campaigns of terrorism against each other and the British; the two sides agreed to end the conflict in 1998; peace deal, called the Good Friday Agreement F. The Soviet Union Collapses
items.zh: 1968年至1998年间，一场被称为“北爱尔兰问题”（The Troubles）的冲突在北爱尔兰六个郡（英国的一部分）爆发；联合派和共和派的准军事组织相互之间以及与英国人之间展开恐怖活动；双方于1998年同意结束冲突；这项和平协议被称为《耶稣受难日协议》(Good Friday Agreement)。F. 苏联解体

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Between 1989 and 1992, the Soviet Union was abolished, the Soviet bloc broke up, and the Cold War ended; reasons: economic, social, and political
items.zh: 1989年至1992年间，苏联被废除，苏联集团解体，冷战结束；原因包括经济、社会和政治方面。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Soviet economic crisis put pressure on the Soviet government to enact reforms; resistance to change dominated by elderly Soviet men who prioritized building military power above the needs of Russian citizens; years of stagnation began after Leonid Brezhnev (1906–82) became leader of the Soviet Union in 1964
items.zh: 苏联经济危机迫使苏联政府进行改革；抵制变革的主要是年长的苏联男性，他们把建设军事力量置于俄罗斯公民的需求之上；1964年列昂尼德·勃列日涅夫（1906–82）成为苏联领导人后，开始了多年的停滞时期。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1978, Afghanistan’s government was replaced in a coup led by communist army officers; opposition resulted in Russian invasion in 1979; Soviet army failed to control anything beyond the major cities of Afghanistan; thousands of Afghans were killed, and millions more fled to neighboring countries such as Pakistan; Western powers sold weapons to Afghan fighters; Soviet Union withdrew in 1989
items.zh: 1978年，阿富汗政府在一次由共产党军官领导的政变中被推翻；反对派的活动导致1979年俄国入侵；苏联军队未能控制阿富汗主要城市以外的任何地区；成千上万的阿富汗人被杀，另有数百万人逃往巴基斯坦等邻国；西方列强向阿富汗抵抗力量出售武器；苏联于1989年撤军。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mikhail Gorbachev (b. 1931), became the leader of the Soviet Union in 1985; worked to modernize and streamline the Soviet economy and government; proposed a series of cultural reforms called glasnost (openness); eventually, Soviet leadership allowed democratic reforms, including contested elections and secret ballots, for the first time in its history
items.zh: 米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫（生于1931年）于1985年成为苏联领导人；致力于使苏联经济和政府现代化并精简机构；提出了一系列称为“公开性”（glasnost）的文化改革；最终，苏联领导层有史以来第一次允许民主改革，包括竞争性选举和无记名投票。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In the 1980s, independent trade unions in Poland led campaigns for workers’ rights and social change; the largest union, led by Lech Wałęsa (b. 1943), helped force the Polish government to restore a democratic parliament and hold elections in 1989
items.zh: 20世纪80年代，波兰的独立工会发起了争取工人权利和社会变革的运动；最大的工会由莱赫·瓦文萨（生于1943年）领导，迫使波兰政府恢复民主议会并于1989年举行选举。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: November 9, 1989, Berlin Wall collapsed
items.zh: 1989年11月9日，柏林墙倒塌。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Soviet Union reacted to popular movements by removing troops from countries that were becoming democratic, such East Germany, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, and Poland; in 1990, Gorbachev agreed that East and West Germany should be reunited
items.zh: 苏联对民众运动的反应是从正在走向民主的国家撤军，如东德、匈牙利、捷克斯洛伐克和波兰；1990年，戈尔巴乔夫同意东西德应统一。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The former Soviet Union broke up into fifteen independent countries, including Russia, Armenia, and Estonia.
items.zh: 前苏联分裂为十五个独立国家，包括俄罗斯、亚美尼亚和爱沙尼亚。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New Russian president Boris Yeltsin (1931–2007) in charge of ending the Soviet system and beginning a transition to a liberal, democratic, and capitalist country
items.zh: 俄罗斯新总统鲍里斯·叶利钦（1931–2007）负责终结苏联体制，并开始向自由、民主和资本主义国家过渡。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Between June 1991 and May 1992, the five Yugoslavian regions— Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, and Macedonia—declared their independence; population came from many ethnicities
items.zh: 1991年6月至1992年5月间，南斯拉夫的五个地区——斯洛文尼亚、克罗地亚、波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那、塞尔维亚和马其顿——宣布独立；其人口由多个民族构成。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Conflict arose between the majority and minority ethnic and religious populations; Serbs in Croatia wanted to join Serbia; Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina wanted independence from the Muslim majority
items.zh: 多数与少数的民族和宗教群体之间发生冲突；克罗地亚的塞尔维亚人想加入塞尔维亚；波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那的塞尔维亚人希望脱离穆斯林占多数的统治而独立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After two years of fighting, the United Nations sent humanitarian aid to civilians and set up safe zones for refugees; UN forces did not defend safe zones; Serbian forces massacred their opponents; fighting stopped in 1995 after NATO agreed to send troops to stop Serbs from attacking Bosnian forces
items.zh: 经过两年的战斗，联合国向平民提供人道主义援助，并为难民设立安全区；联合国部队没有保卫安全区；塞尔维亚军队屠杀了对手；1995年北约同意派兵阻止塞尔维亚人进攻波斯尼亚军队后，战斗停止。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In Serbia, ethnically Albanian and Muslim citizens formed the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA); rebellion prompted brutal attacks by the Yugoslav army, Serbian police, and Serbian soldiers; thousands of Kosovans driven from their homes; United Nations and NATO forces helped establish a fragile peace; Kosovo declared itself independent in 2008; neither Serbia nor Russia recognized its status as a separate state
items.zh: 在塞尔维亚，阿尔巴尼亚族和穆斯林公民组成了科索沃解放军（KLA）；起义招致南斯拉夫军队、塞尔维亚警察和塞尔维亚士兵的残酷镇压；成千上万的科索沃人被赶出家园；联合国和北约部队帮助建立了脆弱的和平；科索沃于2008年宣布独立；塞尔维亚和俄罗斯均未承认其作为独立国家的地位。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The formation of the European Economic Community (EEC) in 1957 created a common market among the member nations; EEC also began process of creating Europe-wide institutions; the European Parliament has power to consult on European laws and policies; the European Court of Justice hears cases that affect member nations
items.zh: 1957年欧洲经济共同体（EEC）的成立在成员国之间建立了共同市场；欧共体还开始了创建全欧洲范围机构的进程；欧洲议会有权就欧洲法律和政策提供咨询；欧洲法院审理影响成员国的案件。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: European Union (EU), the successor to the EEC, formed in 1993 and today has twenty seven member countries; unit of currency the euro
items.zh: 欧洲联盟（EU），欧共体的继承者，成立于1993年，现有二十七个成员国；统一货币为欧元。

items.zh: 乌干达、肯尼亚、南非、津巴布韦、乍得、加蓬、刚果共和国、中非共和国、阿尔及利亚、加纳、喀麦隆、利比亚、卢旺达共和国、纳米比亚、埃及、突尼斯、摩洛哥、埃及

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Israel, Palestine, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon
items.zh: 沙特阿拉伯、伊朗、伊拉克、阿拉伯联合酋长国、科威特、以色列、巴勒斯坦、约旦、叙利亚、黎巴嫩。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Arabian Peninsula
items.zh: 阿拉伯半岛

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Sinai Peninsula B. Background Before World War I, Africa and the Middle East were divided up among European empires. Following the collapse of these empires after World War II, a wave of independence movements in Africa and the Middle East brought new nations into existence. The colonial era had left some areas richer and more developed than others. Colonial governments had divided people along racial, religious, and ethnic lines. In the postcolonial era, the former empires—and the new superpowers, the United States and the Soviet Union—had business and military interests in Africa and the Middle East that caused them to interfere with the newly free nations.
items.zh: 西奈半岛 B. 背景 第一次世界大战前，非洲和中东被欧洲各帝国瓜分。第二次世界大战后这些帝国崩溃，非洲和中东掀起独立运动浪潮，新的国家纷纷诞生。殖民时代使一些地区比其他地区更富裕、更发达。殖民政府按种族、宗教和民族划分人群。在后殖民时代，昔日的帝国以及新的超级大国——美国和苏联——在非洲和中东拥有商业和军事利益，这导致它们干涉这些新独立的国家。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Colonization of Africa via private companies (British East Africa Company), governed directly by home nation (direct rule), indirect rule; settler colonies (South Africa, Zimbabwe)
items.zh: 通过私营公司（英国东非公司，British East Africa Company）对非洲进行殖民；由宗主国直接统治（直接统治）、间接统治；移民殖民地（南非、津巴布韦）

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Infrastructure developed to transport valuable raw materials from mines and plantations to markets and ports
items.zh: 基础设施建设起来，用于将矿场和种植园的贵重原材料运往市场和港口。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: World War II weakened colonial rule in Africa; many Africans had fought as part of the Allied armies against the Axis Powers.
items.zh: 第二次世界大战削弱了非洲的殖民统治；许多非洲人曾作为盟军的一部分与轴心国作战。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1954, Algerian nationalists launched a war of independence; bloody war against French followed; in 1962, France accepted Algerian independence
items.zh: 1954年，阿尔及利亚民族主义者发动独立战争；随后是对法国人的血腥战争；1962年，法国接受阿尔及利亚独立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kenyans seek independence from the British; Mau Mau independence fighters; fighting ended in 1960; British allowed elections to take place early the next year; elections created a government that wrote a new constitution for an independent Kenya
items.zh: 肯尼亚人寻求脱离英国独立；茅茅党（Mau Mau）独立战士；战斗于1960年结束；英国允许次年早些时候举行选举；选举产生的政府为独立的肯尼亚制定了新宪法。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Jomo Kenyatta (1894–1978), a leader in the movement for independence, became Kenya’s first prime minister.
items.zh: 乔莫·肯雅塔（1894–1978）是独立运动的领袖，成为肯尼亚首任总理。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Kwame Nkrumah (1909–72) formed the Convention People’s Party (CPP), which gained mass support among the people of the Gold Coast.
items.zh: 克瓦米·恩克鲁玛（1909–72）创建了人民大会党（CPP），该党在黄金海岸人民中获得了广泛支持。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nkrumah won election to the Gold Coast’s new parliament and became prime minister in 1952; the CPP’s independence platform gave the party a large majority of seats in the Gold Coast parliament; used this power to formally gain the Gold Coast’s independence
items.zh: 恩克鲁玛在黄金海岸新议会选举中获胜，并于1952年成为总理；人民大会党的独立纲领使该党在黄金海岸议会中占据绝大多数席位；他利用这一权力正式争取黄金海岸的独立。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1957, the Gold Coast was recognized as an independent nation and renamed Ghana.
items.zh: 1957年，黄金海岸被承认为独立国家，并改名为加纳。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Fourteen former French colonies in Africa became independent in 1960, as well as two British colonies and one Belgian colony; the year 1960 came to be known as the “Year of Africa.” Timeline D. Struggles and Civil Wars
items.zh: 1960年，非洲十四个前法国殖民地以及两个英国殖民地和一个比利时殖民地获得独立；1960年因而被称为“非洲年”。时间线D. 斗争与内战

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Newly independent African nations faced challenges; borders had been drawn by European powers; many of the new countries contained conflicting ethnic and religious groups
items.zh: 新独立的非洲国家面临挑战；边界是由欧洲列强划定的；许多新国家内部存在相互冲突的民族和宗教群体。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: New nations aimed to use independence to benefit their own people; continuing trade in African resources helped grow the economy; foreign nations, however, maintained economic and political influence
items.zh: 新国家旨在利用独立为本国人民谋利；非洲资源的持续贸易有助于经济增长；然而，外国仍保持着经济和政治影响力。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Libya gained independence in 1951; in 1959 oil discovered; king of Libya favored western powers; Libya’s military staged a coup in 1969, bringing Muammar al- Qaddafi (1942–2011) to power
items.zh: 利比亚于1951年独立；1959年发现石油；利比亚国王亲西方；1969年利比亚军方发动政变，使穆阿迈尔·卡扎菲（1942–2011）上台。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Rwanda gained independence in 1961; two main groups in Rwanda—the Tutsi and the Hutu; traditionally, the Tutsi are smaller, wealthier group; the Hutu majority poor farmers
items.zh: 卢旺达于1961年独立；卢旺达有两大群体——图西族和胡图族；传统上，图西族是人数较少、较富裕的群体；占多数的胡图族是贫穷的农民。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1994, Hutu extremists launched campaign of mass murder directed at Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
items.zh: 1994年，胡图族极端分子发动了针对图西族和温和派胡图族的大屠杀运动。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mobutu Sese Seko (1930–97) ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as a dictator from 1965 to 1997; Idi Amin (1924–2003) in Uganda
items.zh: 蒙博托·塞塞·塞科（1930–97）从1965年到1997年以独裁者身份统治刚果民主共和国（DRC）；伊迪·阿明（1924–2003）统治乌干达。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In Ghana, Jerry Rawlings took power in a coup in 1981; was democratically elected in 1992; Rawlings brought political stability to the country and implemented economic reforms
items.zh: 在加纳，杰里·罗林斯于1981年通过政变上台；1992年通过民主选举当选；罗林斯为国家带来政治稳定并实施了经济改革。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Namibia gained independence from South Africa in 1990; established politically stable democracy; has one of the strongest economies in Africa
items.zh: 纳米比亚于1990年脱离南非获得独立；建立了政治稳定的民主制度；拥有非洲最强经济体之一。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: South Africa won its independence from Great Britain in 1910, but most of its people were not free; Black population did not have the same rights and power as the white minority that controlled the government and the economy
items.zh: 南非于1910年脱离英国获得独立，但大多数人民并不自由；黑人人口没有享有与控制政府和经济白人少数群体相同的权利和权力。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1913, South Africa’s government passed the Land Act; led to the forced removal of Black South Africans from their land; their property sold by the government to white farmers at a reduced cost; Black South Africans were relocated to other areas, where they lived in poverty
items.zh: 1913年，南非政府通过《土地法》；导致南非黑人被强制迁离其土地；他们的财产被政府以低价出售给白人农民；南非黑人被迁往其他地区，在那里过着贫困生活。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The white minority officially imposed a system called apartheid in 1948; under this system, white and non-white people were required to live in separate areas and could not use the same public facilities.
items.zh: 白人少数群体于1948年正式推行名为种族隔离（apartheid）的制度；在这一制度下，白人和非白人被要求居住在分开的地区，且不能使用相同的公共设施。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Organization of Black South Africans, the African National Congress (ANC), fought apartheid policies
items.zh: 南非黑人的组织——非洲人国民大会（非国大，ANC）——反对种族隔离政策。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: South African government tried to silence the ANC; in 1960, police forces killed sixty nine unarmed demonstrators (Sharpeville massacre); government outlawed the ANC
items.zh: 南非政府试图压制非国大；1960年，警察杀害了六十九名手无寸铁的示威者（沙佩维尔惨案）；政府取缔了非国大。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nelson Mandela, who had first led peaceful protests against apartheid, became the leader of an armed wing of the ANC, called Umkhonto we Sizwe (Spear of the Nation).
items.zh: 纳尔逊·曼德拉最初领导反对种族隔离的和平抗议，后来成为非国大武装组织“民族之矛”（Umkhonto we Sizwe，Spear of the Nation）的领导人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1964, Mandela and other ANC leaders sentenced to life in prison
items.zh: 1964年，曼德拉和其他非国大领导人被判无期徒刑。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: South African police killed about six hundred Black South Africans during protests in the township of Soweto in 1976.
items.zh: 1976年，南非警察在索韦托镇的抗议活动中杀害了约六百名南非黑人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: International community outraged; began to pressure South African government to end apartheid and release Mandela from prison; introduction of sanctions
items.zh: 国际社会感到愤怒；开始向南非政府施压，要求结束种族隔离并释放曼德拉；实施制裁。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: President F. W. de Klerk, in 1990, legalized the ANC and freed Nelson Mandela and other ANC leaders.
items.zh: 1990年，总统弗雷德里克·威廉·德克勒克使非国大合法化，并释放了纳尔逊·曼德拉和其他非国大领导人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: South African government began to end apartheid; in 1994 allowed South Africans of every race to vote; Nelson Mandela elected president
items.zh: 南非政府开始结束种族隔离；1994年允许各种族的南非人投票；纳尔逊·曼德拉当选总统。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Apartheid had done lasting damage to Black South Africans; by the early twenty-first century, white South Africans still controlled almost three-quarters of the country’s farmland.
items.zh: 种族隔离给南非黑人造成了持久的伤害；到21世纪初，南非白人仍控制着该国近四分之三的农田。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: African cities and nations have emerged as global leaders in science and technology in the new millennium; the cities of Algiers in Algeria, Lagos in Nigeria, Nairobi in Kenya, and Johannesburg in South Africa are all considered major international centers for business and culture.
items.zh: 在新千年里，非洲的城市和国家已成为科技领域的全球领导者；阿尔及利亚的阿尔及尔、尼日利亚的拉各斯、肯尼亚的内罗毕和南非的约翰内斯堡都被视为重要的国际商业和文化中心。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Innovators across the continent have come up with new solutions to age-old problems: how to transport water and bring medical care to rural areas; addressed new challenges; expanding mobile and Internet access; many inventions rooted in computer and mobile technology, an area in which African nations are leading the rest of the world
items.zh: 整个非洲大陆的创新者提出了解决古老问题的新方案：如何向农村地区输送水并提供医疗；应对新的挑战；扩大移动和互联网接入；许多发明植根于计算机和移动技术，在这一领域非洲国家正领先于世界其他地区。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The Middle East is not a distinctive geographic zone or a continent; it is a region defined primarily by European and American observers in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.zh: 中东并非一个独特的地理区域或大洲；它主要是十九、二十世纪由欧美观察者定义的一个地区。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Large proportion of the world’s proven oil reserves are in the Middle East—principally in Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, the United Arab Emirates, and Kuwait.
items.zh: 世界已探明石油储量的很大一部分位于中东——主要在沙特阿拉伯、伊朗、伊拉克、阿拉伯联合酋长国和科威特。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Prior to World War I, the Ottoman Empire controlled the land of Palestine; Palestine had a large Arab population.
items.zh: 第一次世界大战前，奥斯曼帝国控制着巴勒斯坦地区；巴勒斯坦有大量阿拉伯人口。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: European anti-Semitism and a desire for self-determination led some Jews to seek a national homeland.
items.zh: 欧洲的反犹太主义和对民族自决的渴望使一些犹太人寻求建立民族家园。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Great Britain received a mandate to rule Palestine; in 1917, during the First World War, the British issued the Balfour Declaration, which officially supported the creation of a Jewish homeland in Palestine.
items.zh: 英国获得了统治巴勒斯坦的委任统治权；1917年第一次世界大战期间，英国发表《贝尔福宣言》，正式支持在巴勒斯坦建立犹太人家园。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Many Jewish people fled to Palestine to escape persecution by the Nazis and their allies before and during World War II; Jewish population in Palestine grew to about six hundred thousand by 1945; Arabs numbered around a million; violence broke out between the two groups—and both sides attacked the British
items.zh: 二战前和二战期间，许多犹太人逃往巴勒斯坦以躲避纳粹及其盟友的迫害；到1945年巴勒斯坦的犹太人口增长到约六十万；阿拉伯人约有一百万；两个群体之间爆发暴力冲突——双方都袭击了英国人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After World War II, British give up mandate in Palestine
items.zh: 二战后，英国放弃对巴勒斯坦的委任统治。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The UN created two states, one Jewish and one Arab, in 1947; the Jewish state declared its independence as Israel in 1948.
items.zh: 联合国于1947年建立了两个国家，一个犹太国家，一个阿拉伯国家；1948年犹太国家宣布独立，成为以色列。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After the signing of the Israeli Declaration of Independence in 1948, armies from neighboring Arab countries of Egypt, Jordan, Iraq, Syria, and Lebanon launched a war against Israel; Israelis also seized land from Palestinians; fighting lasted for ten months; when conflict ended, Israel had expanded its territory beyond the land that had been designated for the Jewish state; many people had been displaced
items.zh: 1948年《以色列独立宣言》签署后，来自埃及、约旦、伊拉克、叙利亚和黎巴嫩等邻国的阿拉伯军队向以色列发动战争；以色列人也夺取了巴勒斯坦人的土地；战斗持续了十个月；冲突结束时，以色列的领土已扩展到指定给犹太国家的土地之外；许多人流离失所。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The division of Palestine set up a long-running conflict between the Jewish state and the Arab population that is still ongoing, both within Israel and in surrounding countries.
items.zh: 巴勒斯坦的分割造成了犹太国家与阿拉伯人口之间长期的冲突，这场冲突在以色列境内和周边国家至今仍在持续。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: One trigger for violence is the status of Jerusalem; as part of the division, the holy city of Jerusalem was divided in half; Jews and Muslims both consider Jerusalem to be among the holiest cities in the world
items.zh: 引发暴力的一个导火索是耶路撒冷的地位问题；作为分割的一部分，圣城耶路撒冷被一分为二；犹太人和穆斯林都认为耶路撒冷是世界上最神圣的城市之一。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: After the establishment of Israel in 1948 and the war that immediately followed, approximately 750,000 Palestinians fled the land they considered their home; Palestinians spread across different neighboring countries; were not organized politically; in 1964, Palestinian leaders formed the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO);Yasser Arafat became the leader of the PLO in 1969
items.zh: 1948年以色列建国及随即爆发的战争之后，约75万巴勒斯坦人逃离了他们视为家园的土地；巴勒斯坦人散居在不同的邻国；在政治上没有组织；1964年，巴勒斯坦领导人成立了巴勒斯坦解放组织（巴解组织，PLO）；1969年亚西尔·阿拉法特成为巴解组织领导人。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1967, Israel fought the Six-Day War against Syria and Egypt.
items.zh: 1967年，以色列与叙利亚和埃及打了六日战争（第三次中东战争）。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1973, Egypt launched a surprise attack on Israel during Yom Kippur.
items.zh: 1973年，埃及在赎罪日（Yom Kippur）之际对以色列发动突然袭击。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1979, Egypt and Israel signed a peace treaty to end the off-and-on war that had been fought for thirty years; Israel returned the Sinai Peninsula to Egypt; Egypt agreed that Israel had the right to exist
items.zh: 1979年，埃及和以色列签署和平条约，结束了持续三十年、断断续续的战争；以色列将西奈半岛归还埃及；埃及承认以色列有生存权。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: From 1987 to 1991, Palestinians participated in a series of protests and riots called the first intifada to protest the occupation of Gaza and the West Bank; led to a peace agreement called the Oslo Accords, which established the Palestinian National Authority as the governing body of parts of Gaza and the West Bank
items.zh: 1987年至1991年，巴勒斯坦人参加了一系列被称为第一次起义（intifada）的抗议和暴动，抗议对加沙和约旦河西岸的占领；由此达成了名为《奥斯陆协议》(Oslo Accords) 的和平协议，该协议设立了巴勒斯坦民族权力机构，作为加沙和约旦河西岸部分地区的管理机构。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Peace process halted during the second intifada—2000 to 2005; Israel withdrew from Gaza toward the end of 2005
items.zh: 第二次起义（2000年至2005年）期间和平进程中断；2005年底以色列从加沙撤军。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Egyptian revolution, started in 1919, led to the end of British rule in Egypt in 1922.
items.zh: 1919年开始的埃及革命导致1922年英国在埃及的统治结束。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: British and the French refused to give up control of the Suez Canal; caused tension over thirty year period; led to second revolution in 1952
items.zh: 英国和法国拒绝放弃对苏伊士运河的控制；在三十年间造成紧张局势；导致1952年第二次革命。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Gamal Abdel Nasser (1918–70) orchestrated the overthrow of King Farouk.
items.zh: 贾迈勒·阿卜杜勒·纳赛尔（1918–70）策划推翻了法鲁克国王。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1956, Nasser’s government took control of the Suez Canal.
items.zh: 1956年，纳赛尔政府控制了苏伊士运河。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Britain, France, and Israel invade Egypt to seize back control of the canal in October, 1956; eventual withdrawal of forces due to threat of sanctions
items.zh: 1956年10月，英国、法国和以色列入侵埃及，企图夺回运河控制权；由于面临制裁威胁，最终撤军。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Nasser died in 1970 and was succeeded by Anwar al-Sadat; he signed Camp David Accords with Israel in 1979; assassinated in 1981
items.zh: 纳赛尔于1970年去世，由安瓦尔·萨达特继任；他于1979年与以色列签署《戴维营协议》；1981年遇刺身亡。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hosni Mubarak ruled Egypt from 1981 until 2021; removed from office during Arab Spring
items.zh: 胡斯尼·穆巴拉克从1981年到2021年统治埃及；在阿拉伯之春期间被免职。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1941, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi became the shah, or king, of Iran; favored having strong ties with Great Britain and the United States
items.zh: 1941年，穆罕默德·礼萨·巴列维成为伊朗的沙阿（国王）；倾向于与英国和美国保持紧密关系。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Mohammad Mosaddegh disagreed with shah; wanted Iran’s oil wealth to be used to fund development programs to benefit ordinary Iranians; Mosaddegh built political support for a program to nationalize Iran’s oil company
items.zh: 穆罕默德·摩萨台与沙阿意见相左；希望将伊朗的石油财富用于资助惠及普通伊朗人的发展项目；摩萨台为将伊朗石油公司国有化的计划争取了政治支持。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1951, Mosaddegh’s oil nationalization law passed; the shah made him the country’s premier.
items.zh: 1951年，摩萨台的石油国有化法案通过；沙阿任命他为总理。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1953, the United States and Great Britain orchestrated a coup, overthrew Mosaddegh and returned the shah to total control of Iran; Iranian oil profits renegotiated; shah brutal ruler; secret police
items.zh: 1953年，美国和英国策划政变，推翻摩萨台，使沙阿重新完全控制伊朗；伊朗石油利润被重新谈判；沙阿是残暴的统治者；设有秘密警察。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, a fundamentalist, advocated the overthrow of the shah; wanted to transform Iran into an Islamic state; shah removed Ayatollah from the country
items.zh: 原教旨主义者阿亚图拉·鲁霍拉·霍梅尼主张推翻沙阿；希望将伊朗变成伊斯兰国家；沙阿将霍梅尼驱逐出境。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In mid-1970s, Islamic leaders grew angrier with the rule of the shah; more members of the public support Ayatollah Khomeini
items.zh: 20世纪70年代中期，伊斯兰领袖对沙阿的统治愈发愤怒；更多民众支持阿亚图拉·霍梅尼。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In September, 1978, shah ordered security forces to fire into a crowd of demonstrators; hundreds killed, thousands wounded; riots broke out two months later; Khomeini called for the overthrow of the shah
items.zh: 1978年9月，沙阿命令安全部队向示威人群开火；数百人死亡，数千人受伤；两个月后爆发骚乱；霍梅尼号召推翻沙阿。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In December, 1978, the governing regime fell; the shah fled the country.
items.zh: 1978年12月，执政政权倒台；沙阿逃离该国。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Khomeini became the leader of the new Islamic Republic of Iran in 1979; new government set up a theocracy based on religious beliefs and implemented Islamic laws
items.zh: 1979年，霍梅尼成为新成立的伊朗伊斯兰共和国的领导人；新政府建立了以宗教信仰为基础的神权政体，并实施伊斯兰法律。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In late 1979, student revolutionaries stormed the United States embassy in Tehran; took more than fifty American hostages; were held for 444 days before their release
items.zh: 1979年末，学生革命者冲入美国驻德黑兰大使馆；扣押了五十多名美国人质；他们被关押444天后才获释。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Iraq ruled from 1979 to 2003 by Saddam Hussein (1937–2006); Iraq’s ruling party was secular
items.zh: 伊拉克从1979年到2003年由萨达姆·侯赛因（1937–2006）统治；伊拉克的执政党是世俗的。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Iraq and Iran hostile to each other throughout the 1970s
items.zh: 整个20世纪70年代，伊拉克和伊朗相互敌对。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1980, Saddam Hussein ordered an invasion of Iran; war lasted until 1988
items.zh: 1980年，萨达姆·侯赛因下令入侵伊朗；战争持续到1988年。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 1990, Iraq invaded and annexed the neighboring country of Kuwait to claim its oil fields; United States–led coalition of international forces repelled Hussein’s forces from Kuwait in the 1991 Persian Gulf War.
items.zh: 1990年，伊拉克入侵并吞并邻国科威特，以攫取其油田；在1991年波斯湾战争中，美国领导的国际联军将侯赛因的军队赶出科威特。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: On September 11, 2001, terrorists belonging to the Islamic fundamentalist group al-Qaeda launched attack on the United States; hijacked and flew planes into the twin towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, the Pentagon, and a field in Pennsylvania
items.zh: 2001年9月11日，伊斯兰原教旨主义组织基地组织（al-Qaeda）的恐怖分子对美国发动袭击；他们劫持飞机并撞向纽约世界贸易中心双子塔、五角大楼以及宾夕法尼亚州的一处田野。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: United States responded by launching a war against the Taliban, the de facto government of Afghanistan, which had allowed al-Qaeda to use the country as its headquarters.
items.zh: 美国以发动对塔利班的战争作为回应，塔利班是阿富汗事实上的政府，曾允许基地组织将该国作为其总部。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The United States removed the Taliban from power; set up new government friendly to its interests
items.zh: 美国推翻了塔利班政权；建立了符合其利益的新政府。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Concurrently, the United States invaded Iraq in 2003 based on claims that Iraq had weapons of mass destruction.
items.zh: 与此同时，美国以伊拉克拥有大规模杀伤性武器为由，于2003年入侵伊拉克。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: Hussein forced from power, tried for war crimes, and eventually executed; Hussein’s removal left Iraq without a strong leader; different factions of Shiites and Sunnis violently vied for power
items.zh: 侯赛因被迫下台，因战争罪受审，最终被处决；侯赛因的下台使伊拉克失去了强有力的领导人；什叶派和逊尼派的不同派系激烈争夺权力。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: U.S. troops left Iraq in 2011; weapons of mass destruction never found
items.zh: 美军于2011年撤离伊拉克；大规模杀伤性武器从未被发现。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: In 2011, U.S. soldiers in Pakistan found Osama bin Laden, the al-Qaeda leader responsible for the September 11 attacks, and killed him.
items.zh: 2011年，美军在巴基斯坦找到了应对9·11袭击负责的基地组织领导人奥萨马·本·拉登，并将其击毙。

items.subject: History and Geography
items.en: The war in Afghanistan continued until 2021, when the United States and Great Britain withdrew troops; the Taliban quickly returned to power.
items.zh: 阿富汗战争持续到2021年，美国和英国撤军；塔利班迅速重新掌权。
